Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 11:

(Verse) ﴿11﴾

There is difference of opinion regarding the meaning of this verse, but the preferred view is that it refers to the incident that occurred on the day of Hudaybiyyah, when a group plotted treachery against the Muslims and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), intending to attack them unawares, but Allah made them captives in the hands of the Muslims. (For details, see Surah al-Fath.)

In short, whatever the circumstances of the incident, the point of importance and significance here is what is before us in the educational system of Islam, namely that anger and enmity should be suppressed, and that the enmity harboured in the hearts of the Muslims against their enemies should be removed, so that the hearts of the Muslims may be at peace, and they may think with a cool mind and believe that Allah is their Guardian and their Protector. Through this gentleness, seriousness and tranquillity, the Muslims acquire self-restraint, tolerance develops in their hearts, and they establish justice with ease. The Muslims will feel remorse if, despite all this, they still fail to fulfil the covenant made with Allah, although He is at all times their Guardian and Protector, and is holding back the hand that reaches out towards them. Another verse says:

﴿When a people intended to stretch out their hands against you, but He restrained their hands from you.﴾ (5:11)

The advancing of hands, their seizing, and then their being held back: this mode of expression is a vivid and graphic one, and it is more effective than abstract expression. Within this expression, image and movement come before the eyes as though on a screen. This mode of expression makes the statement forceful and weighty. It appears as though this is an entirely new style, used for the first time, and in it a tangible situation also comes before the eyes, running across the screen of the imagination in a moving form. This is the distinctive style of expression of the Holy Qur'an, and it is for this reason that the Qur'an is inimitable.

Lesson No. 47 at a Glance:

At the end of the previous lesson, mention was made of the covenant that was concluded between Allah and the Muslims, and the great favour Allah had bestowed upon them by making that covenant was reminded to them. This was so that they might discharge well the duties imposed upon them under that covenant, and fear that they might break it and violate it.

Throughout this whole lesson, the details are given of how the People of the Book violated the covenants they had made with Allah. It is also told how severe were the punishments they received in this world as a result of those violations. This is so that, on the one hand, this clarification may serve the community of Muslims as a historical admonition and lesson, and the details of the true situation of the People of the Book may come before their eyes; and on the other hand, they may be told that the Sunnah of Allah is immutable, and that He makes no concession to anyone in His decisions. Thirdly, it may become known what the true reality of the People of the Book is, and what their stance has always been in history, so that the conspiracies they have hatched against the Muslims may be properly countered and their intrigues and machinations may be defeated. They carry out these conspiracies and intrigues under the guise of religious firmness, although they have always been breaking those covenants.

In this lesson, the covenant that Allah made with the people of Moses is also examined, at the time when they were delivered from the humiliating and subjugated life of Egypt. The Children of Israel also broke that covenant. It is also described what befell them as a result of this breach of faith: they were expelled with the curse of God, and, deprived of guidance and favour, they were declared outcasts from His presence. Then the covenant made with those who said that they were Christians is also examined. They broke that covenant, and as a result Allah created enmity and hostility among them, and it was announced that this enmity would remain until the Day of Resurrection. Then the stance of the Children of Israel is also X-rayed with reference to the Holy Land, where they had pledged that they would attack it. They broke that pledge and turned back on their heels, purely out of cowardice; they dealt treacherously with Allah and did not fulfil the responsibilities of the covenant. They plainly told Moses (peace be upon him): "You go, you and your Lord, and fight; we shall sit here."

In the midst of this examination of the covenants and stances of the People of the Book, it is also shown how much intellectual deviation arose among them as a result of these breaches of faith. In those covenants it was agreed that they would acknowledge only one God and submit before Him. In return, Allah was to bless them with favours and honours, and He promised them: "You shall be given sovereignty over this land." But they disobeyed God and deprived themselves of all these things. Consequently, cursed by Allah and sunk in sectarianism, they spent their lives in exile.

After these observations, they are invited anew to accept guidance. This guidance, which is of the utmost importance, has been presented by this final messenger, presented by the Last of the Prophets, the Seal of the Prophets, and because of which the proof has been established against mankind, so that they cannot say that a long time has passed and no prophet has come, and that a long period has elapsed since the last prophet, so they forgot the guidance, and now what will be the reckoning against them? Behold, Muhammad (ﷺ) has come as a bearer of good news and a warner; now what excuse do you have? Tell us!

From this whole discussion, the following conclusion also naturally emerges: the religion of Islam is one in its foundation. The covenant of Allah with His servants is also one: that they believe, regard Allah as One without partner, pay zakat, and spend from the sustenance He has given them for the sake of Allah. This is a covenant which fixes correct beliefs, fixes correct worship, and points out the foundations of the collective system of Islam. After this brief survey, let us now turn to a detailed discussion of the verses.

(Verse 12 to 14)

Allah made a covenant with the Children of Israel, and it was an agreement between two parties. The wording of this covenant was in the form of a condition and its consequence. The Qur'an has quoted the condition and its consequences exactly as they were. This original wording is given after a description of the circumstances of the covenant and the occasion on which it was concluded. This covenant was made between Allah and twelve representatives of the Children of Israel. These representatives were the representatives of the twelve tribes of the Children of Israel. These twelve tribes were the grandsons and descendants of Prophet Ya'qub (peace be upon him), who was named Israel. The number of these representatives was twelve, and the wording of this covenant was as follows:

﴿And Allah said, "Indeed, I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the sound way."﴾ (5:12)

"Indeed, I am with you" — what a great covenant! Who can be against one who has Allah on his side? Whatever stands against him will have no reality and no effect. And whoever has Allah with him will never lose his way, because one whose companion is Allah is certainly upon guidance. Then Allah will also be sufficient for him.

Whoever has Allah with him will neither be distressed nor be disappointed, because his nearness and closeness to Allah gives him contentment and makes him successful. In short, whoever is a companion of Allah, and whose companion is Allah, has Allah as his guarantor. He attains his aim. At this lofty station, he has no further need or desire for anything.

However, Allah did not declare this companionship as mere jest or humour, nor because of some special friendship with them, nor is it a right arising from some personal nobility for which there are no causes and no conditions. Rather, this companionship has been settled under a formal covenant. It is based on condition and consequence.

The condition is that they will establish prayer. Merely performing prayer is not sufficient; its establishment must be such that all its principles are realised within it, and it becomes a complete link between the servant and Allah. Prayer should be for them a cultural and educational element, in accordance with Allah's upright system of education and system of life, in such a way that this prayer restrains from all immorality, forbids all evils, and that prayer feels shame at standing before Allah's court carrying a store of immorality and disapproved deeds.

Giving the wealth and provision that Allah has bestowed upon them, fulfilling the right of this blessing, they should pay zakah regularly, and consider that the true owner is Allah and that they are following Allah in disposing of this wealth. This is because Allah is the true owner, and people dispose of wealth as trustees and agents of Allah. Furthermore, the payment of zakah is necessary also so that the collective needs of the Islamic society may be met through it. Moreover, so that the golden principle of the Islamic economic system may be put into practice: that wealth should not circulate only among the wealthy, but that economic life should be established on the principle of a collective system of support. Also, wealth should not be concentrated in a few hands, which causes recession in the general society and destroys people's purchasing power. Its final result is that in society productive activity becomes paralysed, or at least becomes very sluggish. Its clear outcome is that a small number indulges in luxury while the large mass of the common people remains impoverished and lives a life of poverty, as a result of which social corruption and mischief arise, and this corruption appears in various forms. All this mischief is checked by the payment of zakah, and in removing this mischief the Islamic system of distribution of wealth does a great work, and Islam plays its economic role.

Belief in the messengers of Allah, belief in all messengers without any distinction or separation, because they all came from Allah and all brought the religion of Allah, and denial of any one of them entails disbelief, because it is a denial of the One who sent them all.

This covenant should not be mere faith and bare belief, but a positive affirmation, and with it practical support for the messengers. Among these duties should be help and cooperation with them in the obligations that Allah has imposed upon them, and for the sake of which these messengers devoted their lives. Belief in the religion of Allah necessarily requires that whoever wishes to establish the religion should be supported by every believer, who should rise and give them full assistance, so that this religion is established on some land of this earth and rises as a reality in people's lives. This is because the religion of Allah is not merely the name of doctrinal conceptions, nor is this religion merely the name of ritual worship; rather, it is a real and practical system of life, a definite system that exercises authority and acts in all affairs of life. Every system and every methodology needs support, help and cooperation; it requires the provision of strength. Struggle must be undertaken for it, so that it may be established, be defended, and be protected. If such a situation does not exist, then it will be considered that the believer has not fulfilled the covenant he made.

After zakah, the mention now comes of general spending in the way of Allah. Allah says that He has made this general spending obligatory, but it is a loan. Although Allah is the owner of all wealth and is the Giver, yet it is His grace and generosity that He asks for what He gave as a loan for Himself. These were all the conditions. Now, what is the consequence of this condition?

The first consequence is that Allah will forgive your sins. Human beings inevitably commit errors and are inclined to evil, even if one is very righteous. Forgiving his mistakes is also a very great blessing for him, and through Allah's vast mercy, his weakness, frailty, incapacity and shortcoming are remedied.

Then, in its consequence, there come gardens beneath which rivers flow, and this is Allah's pure grace and generosity. No human being can reach this degree of Allah's grace and generosity merely by his own deeds. It is purely Allah's grace that can bring a person to this station, and this station is attained when a person strives for it, to the extent of his capacity and within the scope of his ability.

And one partial condition in the covenant and pact was also this: ﴿But whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the sound way.﴾ (5:12)

Therefore, for such a person there will be no guidance, nor will he return from misguidance. When guidance has become clear, a covenant has been made with him, the path has become evident, and the reward for walking upon it has also been determined, then his violation of it is inevitably misguidance.

This was the covenant of Allah with the representatives of the Children of Israel, and these representatives were representatives of the whole Children of Israel nation. They all agreed to their representation. Thus this covenant became, as it were, binding upon every individual of the Children of Israel, and upon the community and nation composed of the Children of Israel. But observe what the Children of Israel did with this covenant.

They openly broke this covenant made with their Allah. They unlawfully killed their prophets. They plotted to have Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) killed and put to death, although Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) was the last of their prophets. They distorted their Torah. They forgot their laws and did not implement any law. They adopted a deceitful, hostile and ignoble stance regarding the final prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ). They betrayed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and broke the agreements they had made with the Messenger (ﷺ). Therefore they went out of the guidance of Allah, their hearts became hard, and they became unfit to accept guidance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 13:

﴿So because of their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of.﴾

This is the Urdu translation: "Then, because of their breaking their covenant, We cast them away from Our mercy and hardened their hearts. Now their condition is that they twist words and take the matter from one place to another. They have forgotten a large part of the teaching that was given to them."

How true is the word of Allah! Even today these are the characteristics of the Jews. This is the curse that is constantly visible on their foreheads. Through it their true nature and disposition become manifest. The one upon whom the curse of God rests is cast away from the court of guidance. Misfortune shines in their features. The sign of Allah's mercy is not found on their faces. Their dealings are empty of human feeling, even though they may, through cunning or out of fear, forcibly bring smiles onto their faces, soften their speech, and show the utmost gentleness in their meetings. The one upon whom the curse of God rests is cast away from the court of guidance. Misfortune shines in their features. The sign of Allah's mercy is not found on their faces. Their dealings are empty of human feeling, even though they may, through cunning or out of fear, forcibly bring smiles onto their faces, soften their speech, and show the utmost courtesy in their meetings. This is because hardness of countenance and dryness of features show that the person's heart is dry and his temperament harsh. Moreover, their essential characteristic is that they shift matters from their place. First they distorted their book, the Torah, and corrupted the form in which Allah revealed it to Prophet Musa (peace be upon him). This distortion was carried out either by adding to the book things of their own liking and claiming that all of this was revealed by Allah, or the distortion occurred in such a way that the verses remained original but they changed their meaning according to their own wishes and, to achieve their base aims, introduced enormous alterations into the meaning of those verses, and thus fabricated lies against Allah. Or the distortion was such that they forgot the commands of Allah, abolished the Islamic system of life and Shari'ah, stopped practising the Shari'ah in their lives, and let their society go free, because after the enforcement of the Islamic system they would have had to adopt the straightforward conduct of this pure and upright religion of Allah, to which they were not accustomed.

﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them.﴾ (5:13)

This is an address to the Messenger ﷺ. He is being told what the condition of the Jews is in the Islamic society of Madinah. They will always be treacherous and will never cease from betrayal toward the Prophet ﷺ. They repeatedly committed treachery in practice. As long as they remained in Madinah, they kept doing something or other every day. After that, as long as they remained in the Arabian Peninsula, their conspiracies continued. And after that, throughout history, the Jews persisted in the same treachery against Islamic society, although the Islamic society was the only society that gave them refuge, delivered them from the oppression of others, treated them well, and in the Islamic society they always lived a life of prosperity. But they always dealt with the Islamic society in exactly the same manner in which they dealt with Muhammad ﷺ. Like scorpions, snakes, wolves and jackals, they kept conspiring against the Muslims and betraying them, and even today they remain engaged in the same deceit and trickery. Whenever they gained power, they took harsh revenge on the Muslims; they laid snares for them and plotted against them, and they became friends of every enemy of the Muslims. Wherever they found an opportunity and a chance, they attacked the Muslims. They are extremely hard-hearted and utterly merciless where Muslims are concerned. They never showed mercy to the Muslims, and regarding the Muslims they always forgot their covenant and responsibility. Most of them are exactly as Allah described them in His Book. And just as their nature shows, they have always been covenant-breakers, and this has been their practice since ancient times.

The manner of expression is such that, addressing the Messenger, it is said that you will find them like this, with reference to Madinah: ﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them.﴾ (5:13) "You will always keep discovering treacherous people among them, except for a few."

Their acts will be treacherous, there will be corruption in their intentions, their speech will be deceitful, and in their view they will be treacherous. Here, the subject has been omitted from the verse and an attribute has been placed in its position, namely "khā'inah" (treacherous), and this has created generality in its meaning: mere treachery, an atmosphere full of treachery, and a shadow of treachery hanging over them at all times. The essence of their nature is that they are treacherous. This is the essence of their stance, and this has been their conduct toward the Messenger of Allah and the community of Muslims. Treacherous... treacherous... treacherous.

This Qur'an is the teacher, guide and leader of this ummah, and its singer of guidance through the ups and downs of the paths of life. It informs the ummah of the conditions of its enemies, and places before the ummah the temperament and history of its enemies, and along with this it also gives Islamic guidance. If this ummah keeps consulting its Qur'an, gives ear to the guidance of the Qur'an, and practically enforces the principles and laws of the Qur'an in its life, then its enemies will never be able to harm it at all.

But when the Muslim ummah itself broke the covenant it had made with its Lord, and when it cast the Qur'an behind its back, it fell into the condition in which it actually is, although this ummah recites the Qur'an with extraordinary melody and ecstatic fervour, makes amulets and charms from it, and uses it for blowing and exorcism.

Allah related to the ummah the full account of what befell the Children of Israel: how they became accursed, were cast away from the court, became hard-hearted, and what distortions they made in the Book of Allah, and how they broke their pacts and promises with Allah. This whole account has been narrated so that this ummah does not break the covenants and promises it has made with Allah, lest its end become the same as the end of every breaker of a covenant made with Allah, of everyone who turns back on his word. But when the Muslim ummah neglected these Qur'anic warnings, left the right path and fell onto a wrong path, Allah took from the Muslim ummah the station of leadership of humanity, and in the caravan of humanity this ummah went into the row of those who follow behind.

As long as this ummah does not turn back to its Lord, as long as it does not stand firmly by its covenants and promises, and as long as it does not fulfil the conditions of the agreement, Allah's promise regarding it will remain suspended. If it fulfils the conditions, Allah will again grant this ummah established power on earth; it will become the leader of all humanity, and then it will be a witness of truth over people. If it does not fulfil these conditions, it will remain among those who follow behind in the caravan of humanity. This is Allah's promise, and Allah never goes against His promise.

At the time these verses were revealed, the instructions from Allah to His Prophet were as follows:

﴿So pardon them and overlook, indeed Allah loves the doers of good.﴾ (5:13) (So when they have reached this state, whatever mischief they commit is exactly what is to be expected from them.) Therefore, forgive them and overlook their conduct. Allah loves those who practise goodness; that is, you should pardon all their evil deeds. This is the way of goodness. Overlook their treacheries too, and this is also goodness.

That was the situation at the time this Surah was being revealed. In later periods the circumstances became such that they left no room for pardon and forbearance, and the Prophet ﷺ expelled them from Madinah, and afterward, in the period of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, they were expelled from the whole Arabian Peninsula.

After this, Allah informs the Muslim community that He had also taken a covenant from the Christians. They too broke that covenant, and as a result they too suffered the punishment for breaking it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 5, verse 14:

﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. So We caused among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will soon inform them of what they used to do.﴾ (5:14)

Here there is a particular manner of expression, and within it a particular indication. ﴿And from those who say, "We are Christians"﴾ (5:14): "And We took a covenant from those who said, 'We are Christians.'"

The indication in this manner of expression is that they did claim to be Christians, but in practice they did not fulfill that covenant. The foundation of this covenant was that they would regard Allah as One, without partner. But they began their deviation precisely from their fundamental belief in Tawhid (the Oneness of God). Having set out on that path, they went further, and this was the lesson (hazz) which they forgot, although this lesson had been well impressed upon them. As a consequence of forgetting this lesson, they went far along the wrong path, and sectarian and factional divisions arose among them, and then many religions and schools of thought came into being among them.

These schools of thought grew to such an extent that today their number cannot be counted. In ancient times too they had countless sects, and in the modern age too they have countless sects. (A summary discussion will come shortly.) Such enmity and hatred arose among these sects as has no parallel in the history of religions, and just as Allah says, these differences will remain until the Day of Resurrection, and they will remain because they paid no regard to the covenant they had made with Allah. They forgot precisely that lesson and outlook on life which had been well impressed upon them. When Allah informs them in the Hereafter of the details of what they used to do in this world, then their recompense will be decided there. At that time Allah will place all their works before them, greatly humiliating them, and then will punish them.

Among those who claimed to be Nasara (helpers), such differences, factionalism, and enmity arose that an example is hard to find. This is recounted by Allah in His Noble Book, both in their ancient history and in their modern history. In these sectarian wars so much blood was shed that no such bloodshed occurred in all the historic wars they fought throughout their entire history, whether the bloodshed resulted from differences arising from religious beliefs, or was for the acquisition of religious leadership, or resulted from political, economic and social differences. This bloody conflict was so long and so deep that its traces remained for centuries, and those wounds did not heal even after centuries; and just as Allah said, He who is the most truthful of speakers, these differences will remain until the Day of Resurrection, and their real cause is only that they cast behind them the covenant they made with Allah, and they utterly forgot that doctrinal lesson which had been well impressed upon them. The first clause of this covenant was that they would remain steadfast upon the belief in Tawhid, from which they deviated very shortly after the raising of Hazrat Masih (peace be upon him); and the details of the causes and events of this are difficult to present here. (For details, see Muhadarat fi al-Nasraniyyah by Abu Zahra, and Fi Zilal al-Quran, Part Three.)

With the discussion of the Jews' and Christians' violation of the covenant they made with Allah, and the comments made upon it, having reached this point, the address now turns to both the Jews and the Christians. Before both of them the announcement of the Prophethood of Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) is now made: that this Prophethood has been sent for you, just as this Prophethood is for the unlettered Arab nations and for the whole world; all people are addressed by this message and call. To all, a command has been given by Allah to believe in this final Messenger. This matter is one clause of the covenant Allah made with both the Jews and the Christians, as we have already explained its details. This Prophet of the final age has also made disclosures of some matters which they used to conceal, although those disclosed matters were present in the books they possessed. They kept these matters hidden with great care, which was a breach of their promise. There were also many other matters which the Messenger of God (ﷺ), in his forgiveness and forbearance, did not disclose, because in the new legal system of Islam there was no need to disclose them. After this, Allah mentions some of their misguidance and deviations which they introduced into their correct Islamic beliefs, such as the saying of the Christians that Hazrat Isa, son of Maryam, is God, and the saying of the Jews that Musa is the beloved of Allah. And at the end it is told that after these disclosures, proclamations, and the spreading of clear light by this final Messenger, there will be no argument left for you before Allah and before people, and it will no longer be possible for them to say that since a long period had passed after Isa (peace be upon him) upon us, therefore we forgot the teachings of God and the matter became confused for us.

(Verse 15 to 19)

The People of the Book disliked the idea that the call to Islam should come to them through a prophet who was not from among them. Moreover, they could not bear that a prophet should come to them from a nation of unlettered people (ummi ummah), in the face of whom they considered themselves superior and regarded themselves as more learned. This was because they were People of the Book, while these were unlettered Arabs. When Allah wished to exalt these unlettered people, He raised among them a Prophet, declared him the Seal of the Prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin) and the final Messenger, and made his message the Seal of Messages (khatam al-risalat). His message was made a general message for all of humanity. Allah taught these unlettered people, and in a short span of time they attained, compared with all of humanity, the highest station of knowledge: in their conceptions and beliefs they were the most advanced, in their methods and their system of life the most correct, in their order, administration and law the most excellent, and in their morals and social life the most righteous. All these matters are included in the fact that this was the grace and bounty of Allah upon them. This religion was given to them as a favour, and Allah chose it as religion for them. Had the Arabs, these unlettered people, not received this blessing, they could never have become guardians of all humanity. If this religion is set aside, what other gift do the Arabs have to offer to humanity?

In these circumstances, Allah addresses the People of the Book. It is recorded that they are being specifically invited to accept Islam, and they are being invited to believe in this Messenger and to help him, in exact accordance with the covenant that was taken from them, that they would support and aid the final Prophet. Allah also records that this Messenger has been sent to them by Allah, the Unlettered One. He is the Messenger of the Arabs, the Messenger of the People of the Book, and then the Messenger of the whole of humanity. Therefore you cannot deny his message, nor can you say that his prophethood is only for the Arabs, or that no invitation has been specifically addressed to the People of the Book in this message.

﴿O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you much of what you used to hide of the Book, and overlooking much﴾ (5:15)

That is, Muhammad ﷺ is a Messenger to you, and among his duties concerning you is to clearly expose the truths that you concealed for centuries, which were in your books, to explain them openly, to reveal secrets and to clarify ambiguous matters. In this respect, the Jews and the Christians are equal. The Christians concealed the very first foundation of the religion, namely the doctrine of the Oneness of God (tawhid). Likewise, the Jews concealed several legal rulings, such as the punishment of stoning for an adulterer and the prohibition of usury for all people. They also concealed the good tidings concerning the final Prophet, Muhammad ﷺ, of which the Qur'an says: ﴿Whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not touch upon many of the matters they had hidden, because they did not form part of the Islamic Shariah, that is, Allah abrogated them along with the other elements of previous laws which had fallen into disuse in human societies. Though they were once prescribed, they were prescribed for the small societies of the earlier prophets, for a limited period. Until this final and universal Messenger came, meant for all of humanity. This final message became firmly established in the world, Allah completed it, and as a grace chose it as the complete religion for people. Now its abrogation, any alteration in it, or any amendment to it is forbidden.

Here it is also stated what the aims of the final message are, what its nature is, and what changes this message will bring into people's lives:

﴿...There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book. By it Allah guides those who seek His pleasure to the ways of peace, and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission, and guides them to a straight path﴾ (5:15–16)

No other word fits this Book more truly, applies to it more completely, or expresses its reality more fully than that this Book, the Qur'an, is a light and a new illumination. This is a reality which a Muslim feels well in his heart, his being, his whole life, his outlook, his values, his events and the individuals of his society. As soon as the lamp of faith is lit in a Muslim's heart, he feels a light and illumination within himself. His personality is illuminated by this light, he becomes content. Whatever comes into his environment is illuminated, becomes clear, plainly visible and set right.

The distinctive features of a human being, the darkness of his clay, the coarseness of his flesh and bone, the surge of his desire and pleasure, all are illuminated. All of them shine, are lit up and become clear and refined. The burden of materialism becomes light. Coarseness and turbulence acquire gentleness and coolness. Dust and ambiguity are removed from a person's thought and vision. Hesitation and uncertainty disappear from his actions. Bewilderment and confusion are dispelled from the direction of his gaze. He does not walk the path of cattle, which has a destination neither known nor marked. His path becomes clear, straight and bright. His aim becomes evident, the purposes of his life are determined, and the human soul finds rest on this path.

"This is a light and a clear Book." These two attributes, light and clear, are the attributes of one and the same thing, and this is the Book which the Prophet ﷺ brought.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 16:

(Verse) "Yahdi bihi Allahu man ittaba'a ridwanahu subula as-salami wa yukhrijuhum mina adh-dhulumati ilan-nuri bi-idhnihi wa yahdihim ila siratin mustaqim" (5:16)

(Through it Allah guides those who seek His pleasure to the paths of peace, and by His leave brings them out of darkness into light, and guides them to the straight path.)

Allah has chosen Islam as the religion. Those who submit to this pleasure and choice of Allah, and who choose it for themselves, Allah places on the paths of peace.

This manner of expression applies one hundred percent to the Qur'an, and the Qur'an is the most accurate example of being a means of peace. The path that Islam prescribes for an individual is the path of peace. It is peace of conscience, peace of intellect, peace of the limbs. It is peace of the home and the family. It is peace of society, it is peace of humanity. It is peace with this life, peace with this universe, peace with Allah, the Lord of the universe. It is all-encompassing and comprehensive peace, which this humanity has never found and never will find, except in the Islamic system of life, in the Islamic method, under the law of the Islamic Shari'ah, and only in a society that is founded upon the Islamic Shari'ah and the Islamic ideology of life.

This is the great truth: Allah guides to this religion the person with whom Allah is pleased. And that person is one who also considers the will of Allah alone, and in the will of Allah are the paths of peace, namely Islam. All paths of peace lie in Islam. Only one who has seen all the paths of jahiliyyah, both ancient jahiliyyah and modern jahiliyyah, which are the paths of war and conflict, can grasp the depth and profundity of this truth. Only the person who has personally seen the restlessness arising in the depths of conscience due to jahiliyyah, and has tasted it, can grasp the depth of this reality. Likewise, one who has seen the unrest arising from jahili customs, jahili systems of life and ways of living, and has seen the chaos that this system creates in the affairs of human life.

Those to whom these verses were first addressed knew well what subul as-salam meant, because having lived in jahiliyyah they had firsthand experience of what peace is. Therefore they knew personally the meaning of subul as-salam. They were personally enjoying it, because they had emerged from that unfamiliar life of jahiliyyah.

At this time we are in dire need of understanding this peaceful aspect of Islam, because in the jahiliyyah spread around us humanity is suffering oppression and cruelty; for centuries every kind of war has been waged, on the battlefield, within the human conscience, and within societies.

We, who once lived in a period of Islamic history under the shelter of Islam's peace, have now abandoned that peace and entered this unending conflict and war, which has shattered our hearts and souls, which has brought our morals and conduct to breakdown and disintegration, and which has utterly ruined our societies and our nations. Yet we could very easily re-enter that peace, because the message of that peace is preserved with us. It can display its miracle when we become pleased with the will of Allah and choose it for ourselves, since Allah has chosen it for us.

We are now suffering the calamities of jahiliyyah, although Islam is near us and with us. We are afflicted with the continuous war and insecurity of jahiliyyah, although the peace of Islam is within our reach. What a bad bargain we are making: we are taking an inferior thing in exchange for a superior one. We are leaving guidance and taking error, and while we could show the path of peace and security, we ourselves are suffering severe disorder. We will be able to bring humanity out of the disorder of jahiliyyah only when we first bring our own selves out of jahiliyyah. First we ourselves must take refuge in the shade of Islamic peace. When we enter the shade of Allah's pleasure and submit to the religion that Allah has chosen for us, then we will be among those of whom Allah says that they have proceeded straight on the paths of peace (subul as-salam), and Allah has placed them upon those paths. (For details see: Al-Islam wal-Salam al-Alami; Al-Islam wa Mushkilat al-Hadarah; and Fi Zilal al-Quran, Part Two, commentary on the verse "udkhulu fi as-silm.")

(Verse) "wa yukhrijuhum mina adh-dhulumati ilan-nur bi-idhnihi" (5:16): "and by His leave brings them out of darkness into light."

All jahiliyyahs are darkness. In them there are the darknesses of doubts and suspicions, the darknesses of superstitions, myths and imaginings, and the darknesses and deserts of lust, inclinations and tendencies. There are the darknesses of bewilderment, restlessness, wildness and wandering. People in it go very far from the abode of peace and security. Then instability arises in values, instability in the standards of good and evil, and instability in the guidance of government. The light of the Islamic system stands in contrast to these darknesses, and light is light, which can be seen from afar in darkness. In it the intellect is illuminated, the conscience is illuminated, the personality is illuminated, and life and all its affairs are illuminated.

(Verse) "wa yahdihim ila siratin mustaqim" (5:16): "and guides them to the straight path." This path runs straight alongside human nature and alongside the laws by which that nature is governed. It also runs straight alongside the nature of this universe and the laws (nawamis) according to which this universe operates. This path leads straight to Allah; it has no labyrinths and no bends, no multiple byways and no varying inclinations.

It is Allah who created this human being and his nature. He created this universe and its laws, and it is He who then prescribed the Islamic system of life for mankind. It is He who chose this religion for the believers. Therefore it is natural and evident that this system should guide people to the correct and straight path, whereas all other systems and methods made by weak, ignorant and mortal humans are utterly incapable of this.

Allah is great and true, and free from need of both worlds. Their guidance brings Him no benefit, nor does their misguidance cause Him any loss; but out of His mercy alone He desires to bring them onto this path.

This is the straight path. As for the belief that Allah is the Messiah son of Mary, that is a path of disbelief. The belief that the Jews and Christians are the sons of Allah and His beloved is a fabrication, and they have no proof for it. Both these beliefs existed among the People of the Book, and both beliefs introduced adulteration into the sincerity of Tawhid. The Last Prophet came precisely in order to correct the mistaken beliefs of people, and to bring back to the right path those who had deviated from the true reality and gone astray.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 17:

(Verse) "Certainly they have disbelieved who say, 'Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary.' Say, 'Who could prevent Allah at all if He intended to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth entirely? And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.'" (5:17)

"Certainly they have disbelieved, those who said that the Messiah, son of Mary, is God. O Prophet! Tell them: if God wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and all the people of the earth, who has the power to restrain Him from that intention? God alone is the owner of the heavens and the earth and of all that is between them. He creates whatever He wills, and His power extends over everything."

The belief that Jesus (peace be upon him) brought from Allah was the same belief in Tawhid that every Messenger brought. To worship Allah alone is the affirmation that every Messenger made. However, distortions crept into this clear and distinct belief. These distortions occurred when idolatry entered Christianity, and the Christians introduced the corrupt matter of idol-worship and made it a part of the belief in Tawhid, mixing it into it so thoroughly that it became impossible to extract the true essence of the Christian belief in Tawhid.

These deviations within Christianity did not come all at once. These polytheistic beliefs entered Christianity gradually. One by one, the religious assemblies of the Christians introduced them into the religion, which were convened one after another. The beliefs of the Christians took on a strange and wondrous form, in which mythological stories entered, which, upon hearing, leave a person astonished. To the extent that even for the believers among the Christians themselves, explaining this belief became difficult.

For some time after Jesus (peace be upon him) was raised up, belief in Tawhid remained among his disciples and followers. Among the Gospels written about the circumstances of Jesus (peace be upon him), one important Gospel is the Gospel of Barnabas. This Gospel says about Jesus (peace be upon him) that he was a Messenger from Allah. After this, differences arose among them. Some said that Jesus (peace be upon him) was one Messenger like all the other Messengers; others said that, true, he is a Messenger, but he has a special relationship with Allah the Exalted. Some people said that he is the son of God because he was born without a father. But according to this statement, he is a creation of Allah. Some held the view that he was the son of Allah but not created, rather he was eternal like the Father.

To end these differences, a conference was held in the year 325 CE at Nicaea, in which 48,000 religious leaders and scholars took part. Regarding them, a religious leader who is a renowned expert in the history of Christianity says:

"These people differed in opinions and doctrines. Some said that Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother were two gods apart from Allah. They were called Berbers and were generally known as Remonians. Some said that the Messiah was born from the Father in the way that one flame is born from another flame. No one can say that the original flame has diminished because of the second flame that separated from it. This statement was adopted by Sabellius and his followers. Some say that Mary did not conceive, that is, for ten months. Jesus came out of her womb in the way that water comes out of a gutter, because the Word entered her ear and came out from there, from where a child is born, and this process took place immediately. This statement is that of Elian and his companions. Among them, some believed that Jesus was a human being and that he was born from the human essence. The mercy of Allah joined with him and, by its own will, descended into him, and for this reason he gained the title of Son of Allah. These people say that Allah is an eternal essence and is one. He is one hypostasis with three names. These people do not believe in the Word and the Holy Spirit. This is the statement of Paul of Samosata. This was Peter of Antioch. These people are called Paulicians. Among them, some said that they were three gods and still are: one good, one evil, and one just. This statement is that of the accursed Marcion and his companions. Their belief is that Marcion was the head of the disciples. These people do not accept Peter. Among them there were also people who considered the Messiah to be God, and this was the belief of Peter, which is called the messenger. This same belief was adopted by 318 bishops." (Muhadarat fi al-Nasraniyyah, Shaykh Abu Zahra)

Emperor Constantine adopted this final belief, though he had only recently become a Christian and did not have much knowledge of Christianity. He unleashed his armies against the opponents; these people were exiled, and especially terrible persecutions were inflicted upon those who did not believe in the divinity of Jesus (peace be upon him). They considered only the Father to be God and regarded Jesus (peace be upon him) as a creature and human.

The author of the History of the Coptic Peoples writes about the text of this decision:

"This holy assembly and the church of the Apostle declare forbidden every belief which affirms that there was a time when the Son of God did not exist, and that before birth he did not exist, that he came into being from non-existence, or that this son was created from a matter and essence separate from the Father; and also the belief that he was created, or that he is subject to change and that shadow overtakes him."

However, this assembly could not eliminate the monotheists among the Christians, and among them the branch of Arius remained. This branch came to dominate Constantinople, Antioch, Babylon, Alexandria and all of Egypt.

After this, differences began regarding the Holy Spirit. Some said that it too is a god; others said that it is not a god. On this, the First Council of Constantinople was convened in 381 to end these differences.

At this council, the bishop of Alexandria read a paper, and according to it, Dioscorus, Patriarch of Alexandria, says: "For us, the Holy Spirit is nothing other than the Spirit of God, and the Spirit of God is nothing other than His life. If we were to say that the Holy Spirit is created, our statement would be that the Spirit of God is created; and when we accept that the Spirit of God is created, we would accept that the life of God is created; and when we said that the life of God is created, the whole belief would become that God is not living. When we adopted the belief that God is not living, we adopted disbelief. And whoever becomes a disbeliever, upon him is the curse."

Thus, at this council, a definitive decision was made regarding the divinity of Christ, just as had been decided at the council of Nicaea. In this way the Trinity of Father, Son and Holy Spirit was established. After this, another dispute began: how did the divine nature and the human nature come to be combined, or how did the divine and the human (Lahut and Nasut) come to be united? Nestorius, the priest of Constantinople, was of the opinion that there is one hypostasis and one nature. The divinity of the hypostasis is from the Father and it is attributed to the Father; and the human nature was transferred through birth from Mary, and Mary was not God, since she was the mother of a human being; she was not the mother of God...... The sons [of the Church] write that the Messiah who came among the people and conversed with the people:

"This man who claims to be the Messiah and is united with the Son in love, and is said to be God and Son of God, this is not in reality, but is by grant."

Then it says:

"The belief of Nestorius was that our Lord Jesus Christ was not God, that is, in terms of his essence; rather, he was a man full of blessing and grace, or he was a gift from God. If so, he made no mistake and did not say anything blasphemous."

The Bishop of Rome opposed his opinion, and likewise the patriarch of Alexandria and the bishops of Antioch also opposed it. Therefore they agreed upon a fourth council. This council was convened at Ephesus in 413 CE, and this council decided, as Ibn Batriq says:

"Mary is the Mother of God, and Christ is the true God and man, and he is known with two natures, and these two have become united in one hypostasis." This council cursed Nestorius.

After this, the Church of Alexandria adopted a new opinion. For this, another council was again convened at Ephesus, and it decided:

"The Messiah is one nature in which Lahut and Nasut have been combined." But this opinion was not accepted, and severe disputes on this matter continued. Thereupon, the council of Chalcedon was convened in 451 CE, and it decided that the Messiah has two natures, not one. The divine nature is one separate nature, and the human nature is another separate nature, and the union of both has taken place in the person of Christ. These people condemned and reviled the second council of Ephesus.

However, the Egyptians did not accept the decisions of this council. As a result, between the Monophysite (Mutawafiyya) doctrine of Egypt and the Melkite (Sahi) doctrine, which was the protégé of the Roman Emperor's government, bloody disputes arose; about which we have already cited the article of Arnold earlier. See his book "The Preaching of Islam" at the beginning of Surah Al 'Imran.

Our view is that the references to these many false ideas about the divinity of the Messiah are sufficient to show how many bloody riots occurred because of this false belief, how many lengthy enmities arose, and how many sects came into existence which exist to this day.

After this, the final Message comes, so that it may decide this matter with truth and speak with an undeniable word with decisiveness. Thus the final Messenger comes and instructs the People of the Book in the correct belief in this manner: "Those also are disbelievers who say that Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary." And: "Those also are disbelievers who say that Allah is one of three." (Details are coming ahead.)

Allah the Exalted directs their attention: just use your intellect, and also consider the real state of affairs. (Say: if Allah wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and all the people of the earth, who has the power to restrain Him from that intention?)

Thus, the essence of Allah, His nature, His will, His power, and the essence of Jesus (peace be upon him) are completely separated. Likewise, the essence of his mother and all other beings are separated from Allah, with the utmost certainty and the utmost clarity: that the essence of Allah is unique and without partner; His will is unrestricted; His dominion is His alone. No one can reject His will or repudiate His commands. He can destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, his mother, and all the inhabitants of the earth. He is the Owner of everything. He is the Creator of everything, and the Creator is necessarily distinct from the creation, and everything is His creation.

(Verse) "And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent."

Thus the Islamic belief becomes clear and pure: very evident, very simple, and entirely lucid in contrast to the deviation, scattered thoughts, baseless tales and idol-worship that were mixed with the beliefs of a group of the People of the Book, in contrast to their layered heaps. The first characteristic of the Islamic belief and ideology, namely that divinity and sovereignty belong to Allah alone and worship is for Allah alone, without any doubt, without any complication, and without any dust, makes a decisive and clear distinction between the two realities.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 18:

The Jews and Christians used to say that they are the sons of Allah and His beloved. (Verse) "وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصَارَىٰ نَحْنُ أَبْنَاءُ اللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ" (5:18) (The Jews and the Christians say: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved.") They adopted the belief in fatherhood (being a father) for Allah, although they may hold various conceptions of this fatherhood. Its effect falls upon the belief in Tawhid in any case: the decisive distinction between the divinity of Allah and the servanthood of Jesus becomes weak, and until there is a clear distinction between Allah and His servants, neither beliefs can be correct nor can life be set upon the right path. It is necessary that the direction toward which all servants turn be determined, that they worship this one direction alone, and that the qibla and the source from which human beings derive their law and the principles of civilisation also be determined. And from it they should derive the values of life and the standards of good and evil, without there being any confusion or mutual intermingling in these dimensions, or the attributes of the servant and of God being mixed together, or any notion of a blending between the servant and God arising. Therefore, shirk is not merely a theoretical matter; rather, as a result of shirkī beliefs, a crookedness arises in the whole of life.

When the Jews and Christians made the claims that they are the sons of Allah and His beloved, then, as the necessary consequence of these conceptions, they also held the belief that Allah, the Exalted, would not punish them for their sins, even if they committed them. They would not enter the Fire, and if they did enter it, they would remain in it only for a few days. This would mean that the justice of Allah would not function properly, and that Allah has a special, friendly relationship with some of His servants, so He leaves them free to spread whatever corruption they wish upon this earth, and they will not be punished like other wrongdoers. Every person can think about what kinds of corruption would arise in a society because of anyone who holds this belief, and what kinds of unrest this false outlook on life would create in a society.

Here Islam delivers a decisive blow against this false conception, cutting out its root and closing the door to all those corruptions through which they could enter a society, and it decides that there is no favouritism in the justice of Allah, and that this belief itself is false.

(Verse) "قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُم بِذُنُوبِكُم ۖ بَلْ أَنتُم بَشَرٌ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ۚ يَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَاءُ" (5:18) (Say: "Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings from among those whom He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.")

Through this, a decisive truth comes to light from the standpoint of belief and faith. It is decided that the claim of being sons is utterly false; rather, the prophets are created servants just like other people. And it is decided that with Allah, justice, fairness, reward and punishment, and forgiveness follow a single principle. In this sphere Allah has not kept double standards. This is a matter of the will of Allah, in which punishment also follows certain causes and principles, and corruption likewise has its causes and principles.

This recompense and punishment will be neither according to the principle of personal relationships, nor is there any reality to being sons. After this, the point is repeated that Allah alone is the owner of everything, and that all things will return to Him.

(Verse) "وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ" (5:18) (To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the final return.)

Surely the owner is distinct from his slave. There is a difference in essence; His will is separate; and all people return to the Owner.

Now this discourse comes to its conclusion, and the People of the Book are invited once again so that the proof is established against them and they have no room for excuse. The People of the Book are brought face to face with their end, without any haze and without any complication. Their end comes into full view, clearly illuminated.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 19:

(Verse) "O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you [the religion] after a lull in messengers, lest you say, 'There came to us no bringer of good tidings and no warner.' But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent." (19)

O People of the Scripture, this Messenger has come to you at a time when he is giving clear instruction in the religion, while the sending of messengers had ceased for a long period, so that you could not say, "No bringer of good tidings and no warner came to us." Behold, now the bringer of good tidings and the warner has come... and Allah is over all things competent.

Because of this decisive confrontation, the People of the Scripture no longer have any argument that this Messenger, who is unlettered (ummi), was not sent to them. Allah the Exalted says:

(Verse) "O People of the Scripture, indeed Our Messenger has come to you" (5:19). O People of the Scripture, Our Messenger has already come to you.

Their argument also falls away, namely that a long time passed in which they were given no reminder, no good tidings and no warning reached them, so they forgot and adopted waywardness. Now the bringer of good tidings and the warner has come to them.

Here they are reminded that nothing can defeat Allah. It is no difficulty for Him to send a Messenger from among the unlettered, and it cannot prevent Him from holding the People of the Scripture accountable for the sins they commit.

(Verse) "And Allah is over all things competent" (5:19). (Indeed, Allah is competent over all things.) With this, the discourse concerning the People of the Scripture comes to an end, in which all their deviations and waywardness are laid bare, by which they abandoned their true religion that their own prophets had brought to them. The doctrinal conceptions that Allah has chosen for faith are also decided, the position they have taken regarding the Prophet ﷺ is shown to be false, and the excuse they could have offered on the Day of Resurrection is cut off in this world itself.

In this way, Allah calls them on one side to the path of guidance, and on the other side the avenue of their intrigues within the Muslim ranks is closed. The path of the Muslim community becomes illuminated, and the straight way becomes clearly visible to all seekers of guidance.

At the end of this lesson, the discourse turns to how the Children of Israel behaved toward their prophet and deliverer, Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him), and how they adopted this attitude at the very moment they stood at the threshold of the land that Allah Himself had promised them. And how did they treat the covenant they had made with their Lord? How did they break it, and what punishment did Allah then inflict upon them for this breach of covenant?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 20–21:

(Verses) 20 to 26.

This is a part of the history of the Children of Israel, and it has been related here in detail. The details are given for several aspects of wisdom.

One of these is that the Children of Israel were among those who first opposed the Islamic call in Madinah, plotted against it, remained at war with it in Madinah, and continued to fight against it throughout the Arabian Peninsula. From the very first day they were at war with the Muslim community. They created hypocrisy in Madinah and continued to nurture the hypocrites. They kept supporting these hypocrites, and this support was against the Islamic way of life and also against the Muslims. They incited the polytheists to war against the Muslims, made grand promises to them, and plotted together with them against the Muslims. It was these very people who spread rumours against the Muslims, carried out secret intrigues, kept resorting to cunning, and kept creating unrest in the ranks of Islam. They also tried to spread doubts, both regarding Islamic beliefs and against Islamic leadership. And after some time these people came out fully in the open against the Muslims. Therefore there was a need to lay bare before the Muslim community their complete reality, so that it would know what kind of people its enemies are, what their temperament is, what their history is, what their means of hostility are, and what the nature of the struggle is that they have launched against the Muslims.

Allah knew that these people would remain enemies of the Islamic nation throughout the whole future history of Islam, exactly as they had always been enemies of truth in their own history. Therefore Allah placed their history before the Islamic nation, clearly and thoroughly, and He also laid before it the means that these people used against the Islamic nation.

Another aspect of this wisdom is that the Children of Israel were the bearers of the religion which, before the final religion of Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ), was the true religion, and before Islam the Children of Israel were a nation with a long history. Deviation had occurred in their beliefs, and they repeatedly broke the covenant that they had made with Allah, which they had made with Allah. Because of this ideological deviation and violation of the covenant, their lives were adversely affected. All these matters required that the Muslim nation be made aware of their entire history, because it is the trustee and heir of all the earlier messages and the guardian of the divine way of life and correct beliefs. For these reasons Allah wished that the Muslim nation should know of all these historical upheavals, and that it should know where these people stumbled and what consequences followed. What effect their history and conduct had on the life and morals of the Children of Israel, so that through this experience the Islamic movement would proceed cautiously at those points where people stumble, where Satan attacks, and where deviation begins, so that by means of these historical experiences it would remain on the right path.

And another aspect of this wisdom was that the experiences of the Children of Israel had many dimensions. These were very long experiences, and Allah knew well that when a long period passes over nations and communities, they become hard-hearted, their later generations深 drift away from the true path, and that the history of the Muslim nation will remain long until the Day of Resurrection, and that periods will come upon it in which it will be afflicted with circumstances exactly like those of the Children of Israel. Therefore there was a need that, before the leaders and the renewers and revivers of religion (mujaddids) who arise in Islamic history, there should also be examples of such experiences, showing how deviation and misguidance seep into nations and communities. These renewers should know that once the disease has been diagnosed, how its cure will be effected. For those who deliberately turn far from guidance and the straight path are very hard-hearted. Heedless, unrefined and less-informed people accept guidance very quickly, because a new call comes before them which pleases them, and they accept it. They shake off the dust from themselves, because it is a new thing for them. Since this new call is something new for their nature, life blossoms in them. But for those people before whom a call has already come, that call is no longer attractive to them. It neither stirs movement in them, nor does it create in them the sense that this is a great call which should be taken seriously. For this reason, to influence such people much more effort, and a long and patience-testing struggle, is required.

These were among the very important aspects of the wisdom in the details of the story of the Children of Israel. Therefore Allah has always given these narratives with details, because the Muslim nation was the heir of beliefs, and it now had to discharge the duties of leading humanity. There may be several other aspects, but it is not possible to give more than these indications here. So in this lesson we return to that assembly.

(Verses) "And [recall] when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the blessing of Allah upon you when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings and gave you what He had not given anyone else among the worlds. O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you, and do not turn back [in retreat] on your heels, for you will turn back as losers.'"

Here, in the words of Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him), there is an indication that he had perceived that his people were hesitant regarding this struggle, and he feared that they would turn back on their heels. He had thoroughly tested them during the long journey of the Children of Israel's return from Egypt, and had found that these people repeatedly disobeyed. Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) had brought them out of Egypt and freed them from that life of humiliation and misfortune in which they had been afflicted during their long period of slavery in Egypt. This freedom was granted to them in the name of Allah, and by the overwhelming power of Allah the sea was split for them, and in it Pharaoh and his army were drowned. Then, when they passed by a people who worshipped idols, they immediately demanded, "O Musa, make for us also a god just as they have gods." (Verse: "Yā Mūsā ijʿal lanā ilāhan kamā lahum ālihah.") And when Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) went to Mount Sinai at the appointed time for conversation with Allah, Samiri, from the ornaments which their women had taken from the women of the Egyptians when they came out, made a calf for them. This calf would make a sound just as a calf makes a sound. These people fell upon this calf and said that this is indeed the god whom Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) went to Mount Sinai to meet. Again, a clear miracle of Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) was that he brought forth for them twelve springs from a rock within the scorching desert. Manna and quail, very delicious foods, were sent down upon them, but they rejected these delicious and nourishing foods and demanded the foods they used to eat in Egypt, though there they had lived a life of great humiliation. There they demanded greens, vegetables, wheat, garlic and onions, and they did not show patience with the food that was being sent down upon them, although they were working for honour, sincerity and lofty aims. Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) was drawing them toward those lofty aims, while they were running backwards. Then Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) also tested them in the matter of the cow, when Allah commanded them to slaughter a cow, and they hesitated, made excuses, and for a long time groped in darkness. Finally, compelled, they acted upon the command, but they were hardly willing to do it. (Verse: "Fa-dhabahūhā wa-mā kādū yafʿalūn.")

Then they were also tested when they returned from Mount Sinai, and they had the tablets containing the covenant which Allah had taken from them. They rejected this covenant and remained steadfast in breaking it. Despite these blessings, and their disobedience in return, and after that Allah's forgiveness of them, they still did not accept that covenant, and Allah had to hold the mountain over their heads as though it were a piece of cloud, and they came to such a state that they were certain it was about to fall upon them. (Verse: "Wa-ẓannū annahu wāqiʿum bihim.") Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) had thoroughly tested them during that long journey to freedom. He brought them up to the threshold of the Holy Land, the promise of which Allah Himself had made to them, and it was for that land that they had left Egypt. It was the land concerning which Allah had covenanted that these people would establish a kingdom in it, and that Allah would again send prophets among them, so that they might spend the best days of life under Allah's supervision and guidance.

Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) had tested them well, so it was his right to fear once more their breach of faith. That is why, in this final call, Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) placed before them all the matters worth mentioning from their past history, and placed before them all the good tidings that were to be attained by them in the future. He set before them all the matters by which their courage could be increased, and he also set before them the sternest warning:

(Verses) "And [recall] when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the blessing of Allah upon you when He appointed prophets among you and made you kings and gave you what He had not given anyone else among the worlds. O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned to you, and do not turn back [in retreat] on your heels, for you will turn back as losers.'"

The blessing of Allah and those promises were fulfilled. Allah sent prophets among them and raised up kings. In this regard Allah gave them what He had not given any other nation of the world up to that point in history, and the Holy Land which they were about to conquer, which had been written for them. And this writing was Allah's, so its fulfilment was certain as the truth of certainty. Every promise that Allah had made to them before had been fulfilled one by one, and this was a promise towards which they were moving. To turn back from it would be for them a loss in this world and the Hereafter... But the Children of Israel were, after all, the Children of Israel: cowardly, lazy, those who turn back on their heels, and who break their word again and again.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 20–21:

(Verses) 20 to 26.
