Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 5, verse 41:

These verses show that they too were revealed in the early years after the Hijrah, at a time when the Jews were still present in Madinah: at least in the period before the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwa Ahzab), and before the punishment of Banu Qurayzah, or even earlier, that is, at a time when Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa were around Madinah. Of these, the former were expelled after Uhud and the latter were expelled before Uhud. In that period the Jews were busy with their conspiracies against the Muslims, and in that period the hypocrites would slip into their homes to seek refuge, just as a snake slips into its hole, and these two groups were far ahead in disbelief. Although the hypocrites said with their mouths that "we have believed," their conduct was deeply distressing to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and caused him great pain.

Allah consoles and comforts the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and makes these people's deeds bearable for him. At the same time, He exposes the reality of these people before the community of believers: that they are very forward in disbelief, and that both these groups are included in it. He gives the Prophet (ﷺ) guidance on the conduct that must be adopted towards them, when they come to him to have judgments made, and this comes after their plots, which they had arranged among themselves before coming to the Prophet (ﷺ), have also been brought out into the open.

(Verse) "41."

"O Messenger, let not those grieve you who race to disbelief, whether from among those who say with their mouths, 'We believe,' while their hearts have not believed, or from among the Jews, who listen eagerly to lies and listen on behalf of other people who never came to you; they distort the words of the Book of Allah after they have been properly placed, and they say to the people, 'If this is what you are commanded, accept it, and if not, beware.'"

Narrations state that these verses were revealed concerning those Jews who had committed certain crimes. There is difference among the narrations as to the specific crime: some say it was theft, and some say it was adultery. Both of these crimes were hadd offences according to the Torah, but the Jews had established other laws of their own. The first reason for this was that they did not enforce the hudud of the Torah upon their nobles. Then, out of leniency toward everyone, they had suspended these punishments. In place of these hudud they had themselves fixed some discretionary punishments, just as the so-called Muslims of today have done the same in their own lands. When offences were committed among them in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ), they decided that they would ask the Messenger (ﷺ) about them. If the Messenger (ﷺ) too ordered these same light discretionary punishments, they would enforce them, and before Allah they would have an excuse, that a messenger had given their ruling; but if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the same ruling as the Torah, they would reject it. They sent some of their people to the Messenger (ﷺ) for a ruling, and concerning them it is related:

(Verse) "If you are given this, then accept it, and if you are not given it, then beware" (5:41)

(Verse) "from among those who say with their mouths, 'We believe,' while their hearts have not believed" (5:41). Do these people not seek rulings against the religion, not in order to enforce it, but to turn it aside? Do these people not lay their hands on the religion merely so that it may fulfil their desires and sign off on what suits them? If the religion tells them the true thing and pronounces its judgment in accordance with truth, these people then have no need of the religion. Then they say:

(Verse) "They say, 'If this is what you are given, accept it, and if you are not given it, then beware'" (5:41). This is their condition. Allah has related the story of the Children of Israel with all its details solely so that coming generations may take a lesson from it, and that wise people may be forewarned in advance about the places where one slips on this path.

Allah, concerning those who race ahead in disbelief, and concerning those who consult by night against Islam and play secret games, pronounces the judgment that these people have set out on the path of trial, and into the pit of that trial they are bound to fall of their own accord. In this you have no authority. You cannot avert this trial from these people, because they have gone far ahead on that path.

(Verse) "And whomever Allah desires to put into trial, you can do nothing for him against Allah" (41)

The hearts of these people have become impure, and Allah does not wish to purify their thoughts, so these people will remain in filth in this way.

(Verse) "Those are the ones whose hearts Allah did not want to purify" (41)

Soon Allah will disgrace them in this world, and in the Hereafter a great punishment is prepared for them.

(Verse) "41."

(For them there is disgrace in this world, and a severe punishment in the Hereafter.) Therefore, the Messenger (ﷺ) bears no responsibility for these people, and you should not be distressed by their disbelieving conduct. Do not speak on their matter, for the decision concerning their affair has already been made.

After this, the further conditions of these people are described, and it is explained that although these people have gone far away in their conduct and moral corruption, yet if they come to you with a dispute, you should judge between them with complete justice.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 42:

"Verse 42.

"They are listeners to falsehood and consumers of what is forbidden (al-suht). So if they come to you (with their cases), you may either judge between them or turn away from them. If you turn away from them, they cannot harm you in any way. And if you judge, judge between them with justice, for Allah loves those who act justly."

Here it is stated again that they are habitual listeners to falsehood, which shows that they have become accustomed to it. Their ears prick up with eagerness at falsehood, lies and what is unjust, and they are deeply averse to truth and right when they hear it. In such deviant and misguided societies, falsehood is always listened to with rapt attention, and when a person's heart and mind become corrupted, this is their condition. When the soul grows dim, it keeps searching for falsehood and finds truth extremely distasteful. In such eras, falsehood enjoys wide currency and is much talked about, while truth falls into disrepair in those accursed times.

These people lend their ears to falsehood with great keenness because their conduct is the consumption of what is forbidden. Al-suht means everything that is unlawful, such as usury, bribery, payment for delivering speeches, and payment for issuing legal opinions (fatwa). These are the foremost of their unlawful gains. In every age, when a society departs from Islamic values, these vices become extremely prevalent. The unlawful is termed al-suht because forbidden wealth destroys blessing in property, and every kind of blessing is removed from all deviant and misguided societies. As we ourselves see with our own eyes today, in all those societies that have turned away from Allah's system of life, no blessing remains. Everywhere there is nothing but deficiency.

Regarding these people, Allah grants the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) the choice that if they come to him with their disputes, he may either turn away and not judge between them, in which case they cannot harm him at all, or, if he wishes, he may judge between them with the utmost equity. He should not be swayed by their desires in any way, nor be influenced by the fact that they are very swift in the path of disbelief, that they plot and devise schemes against the Muslims at every turn. This is because "Indeed Allah loves those who act justly" (5:42).

A Muslim ruler and a Muslim judge who deals with justice deals with it in relation to Allah. He does so out of fear of Allah and for Allah's pleasure, because Allah loves those who act justly. Even if people commit injustice, betray trust and deviate from the path of truth, justice remains above consideration of how they conduct themselves, because justice is not for the sake of people but for the sake of Allah. Islamic Shari'ah has given a full guarantee of this, and Islamic judiciary has acted upon it in every time and place.

That the Jews were given the authority to decide their own cases indicates that these verses were revealed at a very early stage. In later periods, judging according to Islamic Shari'ah became obligatory, since in the Dar al-Islam (abode of Islam) judgments may be made only according to Islamic Shari'ah, and it is obligatory for the residents of the Dar al-Islam to decide their matters according to the sharia law. Keeping this in view, the special principle was laid down in Islamic society concerning the People of the Book, that their cases will be decided according to their own sharia. For example, transactions that are lawful in their sharia will be lawful for them, such as ownership of swine, eating its flesh, ownership of wine and drinking it (though they are not permitted to sell it to Muslims). Moreover, usurious dealings are prohibited for them, because usury is forbidden in the Books of the People of the Book as well. Likewise, the prescribed punishments for adultery (hadd al-zina) and theft (hadd al-sariqa) will be enforced upon them, because these prescribed punishments are in force in their own books as well. Rebellion, corruption on earth (fasad fi al-ard) and other general discretionary punishments (ta'zir) will be enforced upon them in the same way as they are enforced upon ordinary Muslims, because these matters are essential for the peace and security of the Dar al-Islam, whether one is Muslim or non-Muslim, and no leniency may be shown to anyone in this matter.

In that period of choice, in which they had the latitude that if they wished they could decide their cases according to their own laws, these people would sometimes bring certain disputes to the Prophet (ﷺ). For example, Imam Malik (rahimahullah), through the chain of Nafi', related from Abdullah ibn Umar (radiyallahu anhu): "Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ). They mentioned to him that a man and a woman from among them had committed adultery. The Prophet (ﷺ) asked them, 'What do you find concerning stoning in the Torah?' They said, 'We shall disgrace them and flog them.' Abdullah ibn Salam said, 'You are lying. The Torah contains the punishment of stoning.' They brought the Torah and opened it. One of them placed his hand over the verse of stoning and read what came before and after it. Abdullah ibn Salam said, 'Lift your hand.' He lifted it, and beneath it was the verse of stoning written. They said, 'Yes, this is the verse of stoning.' Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that they be stoned. I saw the man bending over the woman, shielding her from the stones." (Bukhari and Muslim; the wording is that of Bukhari.)

Similarly, Imam Muslim, with his chain, related from Ibn Abbas (radiyallahu anhu)... These verses were revealed concerning two groups of Jews. One group, in the days of jahiliyyah, had compelled the other to accept this ruling: that if the slain person was from a lowly class and had been killed by a man of honour, the blood-money would be fifty wasq; and if a lowly man killed a man of honour, the blood-money would be one hundred wasq. In Medina these people continued to judge in this manner, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Medina. Then a man from the lowly class killed a man of honour. The honourable tribe demanded that one hundred wasq be paid as blood-money. The people of the lowly tribe said, "Is this distinction lawful between two tribes that share one religion, one lineage and one city, and where the blood-money of one is half that of the other? The blood-money we have been paying was paid because of the injustices you committed, and you imposed this distinction by force. Now that Muhammad (ﷺ) has come, we are not prepared to pay double." War was about to break out between the two tribes, but as a result of discussion between them it was agreed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) should be their arbiter. The men of the honourable tribe then said, "By Allah, Muhammad will not give us more than what we used to pay." Their words were true: the lowly tribe used to pay double to us under compulsion, and they were under our power. Therefore, it was appropriate to send a secret mission to the Prophet to find out whether, if they decided in your favour, you should accept him as arbiter, and if there was a fear that he would not decide in your favour, you should not make him an arbiter. Accordingly they sent a secret mission composed of hypocrites to the Messenger (ﷺ). When these people came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah informed him of what they intended, and these verses were revealed:

"O Messenger, let not those grieve you who race to disbelief" (5:41), up to "the defiantly disobedient" (al-fasiqun). In short, these verses were revealed solely concerning these people, and they are the intended subject (Abu Dawud, through Abu al-Zinad, from his father). Ibn Jarir, in one narration, also named the honourable tribe as Banu al-Nadir and the lowly tribe as Banu Qurayza. This indicates, as has been said above, that these verses had already been revealed before the expulsion and chastisement of those tribes.

After this, in a harsh manner of speech, by way of a rhetorical question of denial, it is said concerning the Jews' position that it is their general attitude to evade implementing the law of the Torah:

"And how would they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is Allah's command, and then after that they turn away?"

It is a grave sin that they possess the law of God and yet turn away from it, and come to the Messenger (ﷺ) hoping that he will not judge according to the Shari'ah and will judge according to what they have written in their Torah. Yet the injunctions of the Qur'an are themselves the original injunctions of the Torah. Just as these people evade the commands of the Torah, so too they turn away from the commands of the Messenger (ﷺ), either by not obeying his commands or by no longer being content with his rulings. But here the context does not end merely with a rhetorical question of denial; rather, from the Islamic standpoint, a judgment is pronounced upon this position."

(Verse 43) "But how do they make you their judge when they have the Torah, in which is the judgement of Allah?" — this is the sense of the verse; the Arabic and the Urdu rendering of the verse itself appear in the commentary as "ومن يکم..." — however, the passage as given begins mid-commentary, so I translate only the text provided.

Translation:

"Rather, these people do not have faith at all."

It is simply impossible that someone who does not judge according to Allah's law should still be a believer, or that someone who is not pleased with Allah's law should still claim, while holding that claim, to be a believer. This is absolutely impossible. If a person accepts faith, he must implement the Shari'ah throughout his entire life. If he does not do so, then his claim to faith is false, and his position is the exact opposite of this definitive text: ﴿And those are not believers﴾ (5:43). This matter is not limited merely to the rulers failing to implement Islamic Shari'ah. Rather, even if the subject people, upon whom the Shari'ah is implemented, are not pleased with the implementation of the Shari'ah, they will be outside the fold of Islam, even though they verbally claim to have faith.

This verse exactly corresponds to the verse of Surah an-Nisa in which it is said:

﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in full acceptance﴾ (4:65)

"By your Lord, they will not become believers until they make you their judge in their disputes. Then they will find within themselves no discomfort at your decision, and will submit completely." These two verses concern the common people who are ruled, not the rulers, yet both place them outside faith. Those who are not pleased with the decisions of Allah and His Messenger are told by these verses that they do not remain believers, or that if the Messenger judges and these people turn away and do not accept it.

The summary of the matter is, as we said at the beginning of this lesson, that this issue is the issue of acknowledging Allah's sovereignty. It is the issue of acknowledging or denying Allah's sovereignty, His sustaining authority, and His watchfulness and guardianship over man. Accepting Allah's Shari'ah and having disputes decided by it is a manifestation and proof of acknowledging Allah's sovereignty and His guardianship, while not having decisions made by the Shari'ah is a manifestation and proof of denying it.

The above was the ruling about those who do not accept Allah's decisions. Now Allah says: what is the ruling about the rulers who do not judge according to Allah's Shari'ah, and this ruling is that of all the religions revealed by Allah, beginning with the ruling of the Torah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 5, verse 44–45 (part 1 of 2):

(Verse) "Numbers 44 to 45."
Whatever religion has come from Allah has come so that it becomes a system of life, a practical system for the people's lives. Every religion has come so that it may lead humanity, organize people, show them the right path, and protect them from errors and wickedness. Religion does not come merely so that it remains a belief and an ideology in human consciousness, nor does it come merely so that a few acts of worship continue in churches and mosques. Although these two matters are necessary for the belief and practice of a human being, the organization of human life, its reform, and protection from wickedness are not possible through belief and acts of worship alone, unless the whole system of life, the system of law, and the system of society based on religion are enforced; unless these things are practically implemented; unless people who rule according to that sovereignty and law occupy positions of authority; and unless there is a government that holds accountable those who violate Islamic laws and guidance and that enforces Islamic punishments. Until then, the implementation of the law of Islam is not possible.

Human life cannot be established until the ideology of life, the acts of worship, and the law are derived from one single source. The rule of that source must prevail over hearts, over what is hidden in the breasts, and over the practical movements and stillnesses of human beings. It must reward people in this world and also in the Hereafter, and it must take account and reckoning.

When the governance over human life becomes divided, and the sources of guidance become different, for example, if governance over conscience and faith belongs to one god, while governance over outward order and law belongs to another ruler, and the master of the reward of the Hereafter is someone else, and the power that punishes in this world is yet another, then in such circumstances the human self is torn into pieces between two different rulers. Within his personality there are two different tendencies, and his life is divided into two kinds of contradictory modes of conduct. In such circumstances, that corruption arises in life to which the Holy Qur'an has pointed in various ways.

(Verse) "Had there been in them (the heavens and the earth) gods other than Allah, they would both have been corrupted." (If there were many gods in the heavens and the earth, corruption would prevail in them.)

(Verse) "Had the truth followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them would have been corrupted." (If the truth were to follow their desires, the earth, the heavens, and whatever is within them would fall into corruption.)

(Verse) "Then We placed you on a clear way of the affair, so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know." (Then We have placed you upon a Shariah, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.)

This is why whatever religion has come from Allah has come so that it becomes a system of life. Whether this religion is for a village, for a nation, or for the whole of humanity, it is on condition that it is the true religion and that it is accompanied by a Shariah. In every religion there is, on one hand, an ideology of life, and on the other hand, within it, a Shariah for detailed guidance of life. In it there are certain acts of worship for the worship of Allah. These three aspects are the essential constituent elements of every religion; wherever any religion has come from Allah, these three aspects must be present in it. Human life can be established and set right only when religion is made the system of life. (For details, see my books al-Islam wa Mushkilat al-Hadarah and al-Mustaqbal li Hadha al-Din, and Khasais al-Tasawwur al-Islami wa Muqawwimatuhu.)

There is evidence in the Holy Qur'an that some of the earlier religions were for a limited region, for example for one village, one city, or one tribe, but these religions too comprised a complete system of life, and for the circumstances of that village or town of that time they were a complete system of life. Here the Holy Qur'an speaks about the great religions: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

(Verse) "Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which there was guidance and light." (We revealed the Torah, in which there was guidance and light.) (5:44)

The Torah, in the form in which Allah the Exalted revealed it, was a book sent for the guidance of the Children of Israel. It was a lighthouse of light for them on the path of truth, and a model for living their lives. It contained three branches: the ideology of life, the acts of worship, and the civil law for the state.

(Verse) "By it the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah and to which they were witnesses." (The prophets who were Muslims judged the affairs of those Jews by it, and likewise the rabbis and the scholars also based their judgments on it, because they had been made responsible for the protection of the Book of Allah and they were witnesses to it.)

Allah the Exalted did not reveal the Torah merely so that it would contain guidance only about the ideology of life and beliefs. Within it were the details of belief and acts of worship, but it was also guidance and light in the sense that it contained the details of a legal system and was a complete system, because the whole of human life had to be kept within the limits of this system. According to the Torah, all those prophets who considered themselves Muslims and had submitted judged accordingly. They did not reserve any part of their lives for themselves, but surrendered their whole lives to Allah. They did not act according to their own will in any matter, nor did they rule by their own authority; they associated themselves with Allah's right of sovereignty. This is Islam in its true meaning. These prophets governed the Jews through this Torah, and the Torah was their constitution and law of Shariah in this regard. Apart from the prophets, the rabbis and the scholars also continued to judge in accordance with it. These were their scholars and judges, and their duty was to keep in place the rule of the Torah. They were to bear witness that they had discharged this right. This testimony they gave by ensuring that their own lives passed in accordance with the system of the Torah, and that they also bore witness that their people had established the Torah and judged accordingly.

Before the discussion about the Torah concludes, the address turns towards the Muslim community, so that they may be drawn to the question of whether they too judge according to their own Book or not. Perhaps there are times when the personal desires of people, their enmity, and their struggles become obstacles in this path. In such difficult circumstances, what then are the duties of the guardians of the Book of Allah, and what is the punishment for opposition from people and turning away from the Book of Allah?

(Verse) "So do not fear the people, but fear Me, and do not sell My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers." (So, O People of Judaism, do not fear people but fear Me, and do not sell My signs for a paltry price. Those who do not judge by the law that Allah has revealed are the disbelievers.) (44)

Allah the Exalted certainly knew that obstacles would arise in every age in the path of judging according to the commands of Allah, and that some people would oppose it. Some people will not accept it with joy and contentment; moreover, some influential and powerful people, and some rebellious people who have hereditarily seized control of governments, will oppose it. They will oppose it because they have wrapped the mantle of Allah's right of sovereignty around themselves. Now, in the Islamic system, they see this mantle being stripped away, and the right of sovereignty becomes exclusively for Allah. They can no longer make laws for people for which Allah has not given permission. Likewise, the interests of self-seeking and materialistic elements also become obstacles in its path, those who exploit people and inflict oppression on the masses. Such people know well that the just system of Islam will never permit such oppression to continue. Likewise, those who are luxurious, self-indulgent, and addicted to the pleasures of food and pleasure stand in the way of implementing the Islamic system; those who take pride in worldly possessions and are slaves to personal interests. They fear that the Islamic Shariah will compel them to lead a pure life, and that if they do not lead a pure life, they will have to face punishment. Apart from these directions and considerations, many other kinds of barriers and obstacles also appear, especially from those people who, by nature, do not wish for goodness and cannot bear to see the reign of righteousness and justice.

Allah knew that in the path of implementing the Islamic Shariah these obstacles would appear from various directions. Allah also knew that the guardians of Islam, its strivers and martyrs, would have to face these obstacles, and that they would have to stand firmly against them, and that they would have to bear losses of life and property. Therefore Allah the Exalted addresses them.

(Verse) "So do not fear the people, but fear Me." (5:44) (Do not fear people, but fear Me.) In this way, when they fear no one but Allah, they will not be slack in implementing the Shariah out of fear of anyone. This fear may come from several directions: first, from those people who do not bow at all before the Islamic system of law and do not recognize the Islamic Shariah, who do not even accept Allah as the lawgiver; or those who do not want the Shariah implemented because it would strike at their exploitative system, with which their interests are bound up and to which they have become accustomed. Or these people belong to general misguided and deviant classes, for whom the commands of the Shariah are very heavy, and they are distressed by it. The meaning is that, without fearing all these classes, or while fearing other people, they should not hold back from implementing Allah's commands, because only Allah is worthy of being feared by us, and fear should be directed to Him alone.

Allah also knew that those who guard the Book and bear witness in the cause of Islam might be seduced by the desires of this brief worldly life. These guardians of Islam see that the ruling authorities, the wealthy classes, and the lustful and self-indulgent people stand as obstacles in the way of implementing Islam. There was a possibility that the people of religion, while dealing hypocritically with these classes, might become their agents for worldly gains, as the scholars of misguidance in every religion in every age have always done, and especially the scholars of the Children of Israel have always committed this evil act. Therefore Allah called upon such people.

(Verse) "And do not sell My signs for a small price." (5:44) (And do not sell My verses for a paltry price.)

This takes many forms, such as remaining silent at a point where truth must be spoken, or distorting the commands, or issuing rulings in which truth and falsehood are mixed together.

As for what is meant by a small price: every price is a small price, even if, by distorting the religion, the whole world comes into someone's possession. But the price obtained by these scholars of misguidance is only certain interests, certain stipends, certain titles, and other small worldly benefits, and in exchange for these they sell their religion. But for this act they will surely be cast into Hell.

If the hedge begins to eat the crop, and if the watchman himself becomes a robber, and if witnesses begin to lie, what could be worse than this? Those for whom the words "people of religion" are used, those who are called scholars, if they begin to commit treachery, if they begin to commit injustice, hide the commands of religion, keep silent about the implementation of the Shariah of Allah, change the meaning of the verses, and alter the commands of the Shariah for influential people, then for such people there is a most fitting judgment from Allah.

(Verse) "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers." (5:44) (And those who do not judge by the law that Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers.) The statement is categorical. By using the word "man" (whoever), generality is created in its meaning. "Man" is both a relative and a conditional particle, and afterward, after "fa," the clause is the answer of the condition. Thus this ruling is freed from the restriction of particular circumstances and of time and place, and becomes a general ruling: whoever does not judge according to Allah's command, whatever lineage or tribe he may be from, will be considered a disbeliever.

The cause of this ruling is what we have already explained: whoever does not judge according to the law that Allah has revealed denies Allah's right of sovereignty. Sovereignty is one of the most important attributes of Allah, and the direct requirement of sovereignty is that Allah's Shariah be the source of law. Whoever does not judge in accordance with it, and denies Allah's right of sovereignty, and claims for himself this attribute of Allah, will become a disbeliever. If someone does this, what meaning remain of Islam and faith? If there is a claim of faith and Islam with the tongue, but action, which is the best means of expressing what is in the heart, shows a person expressing disbelief, then the verbal profession of Islam becomes certainly meaningless.

To resort to evasion regarding this categorical, explicit, and general ruling is merely fleeing from facing reality. Making interpretations regarding such a definitive and explicit ruling would have no purpose other than to change the meaning of Allah's clear commands. Therefore, any person to whom this definitive ruling applies cannot escape in any way from the consequences of this explicit and emphatic ruling.

After setting out this fundamental and foundational principle of the religion of Islam, the discourse now turns back to the Torah. In the Torah too, Allah had enjoined the rulings of the Sharia, and the prophets, the people of religion and the scholars were commanded to judge according to the law of the Torah, because they had been made its guardians and were also witnesses to it.

﴿And We prescribed for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds, equal retaliation.﴾ (5:45)

"In the Torah We had written down for the Jews this command: life for life, eye for eye, nose for nose, ear for ear, tooth for tooth, and for all wounds equal retribution."

These rulings which were revealed in the Torah were retained in the Islamic Sharia and became a part of it. Thus they stand as Sharia rulings until the Day of Resurrection, because the Sharia of the Muslims is for all time. Although the implementation of these rulings can take place only in Dar al-Islam (the abode of Islam), because that is the only practical possibility, and the government which implements these rulings has its authority within the bounds of Dar al-Islam. Yet whenever it comes within the capacity of the Muslims, it is obligatory upon them to implement the Islamic Sharia outside Dar al-Islam as well, because the Islamic Sharia is for all of mankind and is not bound by limits and restrictions, since this is Allah's intention.

When these rulings of the Torah were made part of the Islamic Sharia, a legal provision was added alongside them: ﴿Whoever forgoes it as charity, it is an expiation for him.﴾ (5:45) (Then whoever gives it up as charity, it is an expiation for him.)

There was no such provision in the Torah. According to the rulings of the Torah, these crimes were not capable of being settled by compromise (compounding); in them the complainant could neither grant a pardon nor was reconciliation possible. For this reason there was no expiation for them.

It is appropriate here, in connection with the theme of Fi Zilal al-Quran, to say a brief word about the crimes of retaliation (qisas).

Islamic Sharia establishes, regarding qisas, the first principle of equality. Blood is equal for all and the punishment is also equal for all. In no other Sharia apart from Islam is there equality of a life for a life. Accordingly, in Islam there is a life for a life and an organ for the same organ. In this matter there is no distinction or consideration of region, class, lineage, blood or nation.

A life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and full equal retaliation for wounds. In this matter there is no distinction, no racial, class or national difference. Between ruler and ruled there is no difference. All are equal in the eyes of Islamic Sharia, and this is because all were created from one pair, Adam and Hawwa (Eve). (Abu Kum Adam wa Umm Hawwa.)

The golden principle which Islamic Sharia introduced to this world is the principle of equality, and by giving equality Islam, as it were, gave man a new birth. Before this, man had not attained true equality. The first principle of this equality was that all people would be equal before the law. They would obtain justice from one and the same platform.

Second, that qisas would be taken by one and the same measure from everyone, and everyone's would be the same.

Human-made systems and laws took centuries of travel to reach this degree of equality, and under the influence of Islamic Sharia the legal systems of the world attained Islamic equality only in certain respects, though in practice they could not establish the kind of equality that Islam established.

The Jews, to whom the Torah containing the golden principles of human equality had been revealed, turned away from those laws. And this turning away they did not confine to themselves and others, as the Qur'an quotes their saying: ﴿There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered (gentiles).﴾ (Aal-Imran 3:75). Rather, they could not establish equality even among themselves. In particular, they did not act upon legal equality; as they regarded the tribe of Banu Nadir as superior and the tribe of Banu Qurayzah as lowly, and the punishments for the two were separate. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, he established legal equality between them. He declared the life of the lowly among them equal to the life of the honourable.

The result of enforcing the law of qisas on this great principle is that it is a severe, lesson-giving punishment, and with its existence every person thinks again and again before taking any step regarding homicide, the infliction of grave harm, or breaking of limbs, whether he should take that step or not. Because he knows that if he kills, he will have to mount the gallows, and his lineage, his social standing and his colour or race will be of no benefit to him. He will receive exactly the punishment that his crime deserves. If he destroys someone's hand, foot or other limbs, the same limbs of his will be destroyed. If he destroys an eye, an ear or a nose, these same organs of his will be destroyed. And if anyone thinks that he will merely be imprisoned, he will never desist from such crimes, however long the prison term may be. This is because bodily punishment, bodily defect and the disfigurement of appearance are, compared with the hardships of imprisonment, more painful, as we have set out in detail in the discussion of the hadd of theft in connection with the amputation of the hand.

Furthermore, let it also be kept in view that the punishment of qisas is a punishment which, once carried out, satisfies human nature, and hatred and rancour are removed from the human soul. The wounds of the heart heal and the fire of vengeance is extinguished, a fire which tribal and pre-Islamic vengeance keeps kindling over long periods. For although some people accept blood-money for homicide and compensation for wounds, there are others who insist upon the carrying out of the punishment of qisas.

In enacting legislation, Islam has kept in view the feelings of human nature, just as the Sharia of the Torah strictly observed it, and by the full enforcement of qisas it satisfied human nature. But in the Islamic Sharia it also established for the one who takes qisas the principle that he may forgive, provided that he has the option of taking qisas. ﴿Whoever forgoes it as charity, it is an expiation for him.﴾ (5:45)

That is, whoever forgives qisas with a willing heart, Allah will, in return, forgive the sins of the one who forgives. Sometimes people may incline towards pardon and forgiveness, and there may be hope of pardon and forgiveness from them. Especially from those people who do not need financial compensation, and for whom the enforcement of qisas also does not bring satisfaction, because the relative who has been separated from them, or the loss which they have suffered personally and which is irreparable... for what will the heir of the victim gain if the killer is also killed? Or if his brother or someone else has been taken from him, what benefit will he derive from financial gains? From such things one can only obtain justice and peace and security in this world, but the feeling remains alive for ever in the hearts of the heirs or the criminal. If people have hope of forgiveness from Allah, their hearts can become pure, and the rancour of hatred can be removed from their hearts.

Imam Ahmad narrated through Waki', Yunus, Abu al-Safar: Abu al-Safar says that a man from Quraysh broke the tooth of an Ansari... He sought help from Hadrat Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him). Mu'awiyah said, "We will make him content." But the Ansari insisted that the law of qisas be enforced. Thereupon Amir Mu'awiyah said, "You know, and this Ansari knows." Abu al-Darda' was sitting in that gathering. He said, "I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: whenever a Muslim receives a wound at the hand of another Muslim and then forgives it, Allah will raise his rank or will forgive some of his shortcomings." Upon this the Ansari said, "I forgive."

Thus that man's heart was content and satisfied, although he had not agreed to any financial compensation which Hadrat Mu'awiyah had hinted at.

This is the Sharia of the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, which He has ordained for His creation, in which the inclinations and feelings of people are taken into account, in which the willing consent of hearts plays a very great part, and because of which peace, security and willing contentment arise among people.

Having explained that this was the Sharia of the Torah and that it is now part of the Islamic Sharia, a general ruling is then given:

﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the wrongdoers.﴾ (5:45) This is a general expression. There is no indication here by which we could call it restricted, yet a new attribute, "the wrongdoers" (al-zalimun), has been brought for such people.

One should not understand from describing them as "the wrongdoers" that there is some difference between this description and the earlier description "the disbelievers" (al-kafirun). Rather, those who do not judge according to the law revealed by Allah are, in addition to being disbelievers, also wrongdoers. They are disbelievers because they deny the sovereignty of Allah, since sovereignty is the exclusive right of God and only Allah can legislate; and if someone makes his own law, he claims sovereignty for himself and takes for himself the right of legislation. And he is a wrongdoer because he makes people follow his own sharia instead of the Sharia of Allah, although the Sharia of Allah is suitable for them and through it the conditions of their lives can be reformed. He also commits injustice because he casts himself into destruction, makes himself deserving of the punishment of disbelief, and plunges his own self and the lives of all people into corruption.

This meaning is demanded by the rules of Arabic grammar, because by the rules of Arabic the subject of the conditional and the verb of the condition are one: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed﴾ (45). Now this condition has a first response and a second response. Here the second response will be added to the first response of the condition, and the subject in the condition for both will be "man" (whoever), which is unrestricted and general.

Now it is shown that after the Torah this ruling also continued to apply.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 5, verse 44–45 (part 1 of 2):

(Verse) "Numbers 44 to 45."
Whatever religion has come from Allah has come so that it becomes a system of life, a practical system for the people's lives. Every religion has come so that it may lead humanity, organize people, show them the right path, and protect them from errors and wickedness. Religion does not come merely so that it remains a belief and an ideology in human consciousness, nor does it come merely so that a few acts of worship continue in churches and mosques. Although these two matters are necessary for the belief and practice of a human being, the organization of human life, its reform, and protection from wickedness are not possible through belief and acts of worship alone, unless the whole system of life, the system of law, and the system of society based on religion are enforced; unless these things are practically implemented; unless people who rule according to that sovereignty and law occupy positions of authority; and unless there is a government that holds accountable those who violate Islamic laws and guidance and that enforces Islamic punishments. Until then, the implementation of the law of Islam is not possible.

Human life cannot be established until the ideology of life, the acts of worship, and the law are derived from one single source. The rule of that source must prevail over hearts, over what is hidden in the breasts, and over the practical movements and stillnesses of human beings. It must reward people in this world and also in the Hereafter, and it must take account and reckoning.

When the governance over human life becomes divided, and the sources of guidance become different, for example, if governance over conscience and faith belongs to one god, while governance over outward order and law belongs to another ruler, and the master of the reward of the Hereafter is someone else, and the power that punishes in this world is yet another, then in such circumstances the human self is torn into pieces between two different rulers. Within his personality there are two different tendencies, and his life is divided into two kinds of contradictory modes of conduct. In such circumstances, that corruption arises in life to which the Holy Qur'an has pointed in various ways.

(Verse) "Had there been in them (the heavens and the earth) gods other than Allah, they would both have been corrupted." (If there were many gods in the heavens and the earth, corruption would prevail in them.)

(Verse) "Had the truth followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them would have been corrupted." (If the truth were to follow their desires, the earth, the heavens, and whatever is within them would fall into corruption.)

(Verse) "Then We placed you on a clear way of the affair, so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know." (Then We have placed you upon a Shariah, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.)

This is why whatever religion has come from Allah has come so that it becomes a system of life. Whether this religion is for a village, for a nation, or for the whole of humanity, it is on condition that it is the true religion and that it is accompanied by a Shariah. In every religion there is, on one hand, an ideology of life, and on the other hand, within it, a Shariah for detailed guidance of life. In it there are certain acts of worship for the worship of Allah. These three aspects are the essential constituent elements of every religion; wherever any religion has come from Allah, these three aspects must be present in it. Human life can be established and set right only when religion is made the system of life. (For details, see my books al-Islam wa Mushkilat al-Hadarah and al-Mustaqbal li Hadha al-Din, and Khasais al-Tasawwur al-Islami wa Muqawwimatuhu.)

There is evidence in the Holy Qur'an that some of the earlier religions were for a limited region, for example for one village, one city, or one tribe, but these religions too comprised a complete system of life, and for the circumstances of that village or town of that time they were a complete system of life. Here the Holy Qur'an speaks about the great religions: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

(Verse) "Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which there was guidance and light." (We revealed the Torah, in which there was guidance and light.) (5:44)

The Torah, in the form in which Allah the Exalted revealed it, was a book sent for the guidance of the Children of Israel. It was a lighthouse of light for them on the path of truth, and a model for living their lives. It contained three branches: the ideology of life, the acts of worship, and the civil law for the state.

(Verse) "By it the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah and to which they were witnesses." (The prophets who were Muslims judged the affairs of those Jews by it, and likewise the rabbis and the scholars also based their judgments on it, because they had been made responsible for the protection of the Book of Allah and they were witnesses to it.)

Allah the Exalted did not reveal the Torah merely so that it would contain guidance only about the ideology of life and beliefs. Within it were the details of belief and acts of worship, but it was also guidance and light in the sense that it contained the details of a legal system and was a complete system, because the whole of human life had to be kept within the limits of this system. According to the Torah, all those prophets who considered themselves Muslims and had submitted judged accordingly. They did not reserve any part of their lives for themselves, but surrendered their whole lives to Allah. They did not act according to their own will in any matter, nor did they rule by their own authority; they associated themselves with Allah's right of sovereignty. This is Islam in its true meaning. These prophets governed the Jews through this Torah, and the Torah was their constitution and law of Shariah in this regard. Apart from the prophets, the rabbis and the scholars also continued to judge in accordance with it. These were their scholars and judges, and their duty was to keep in place the rule of the Torah. They were to bear witness that they had discharged this right. This testimony they gave by ensuring that their own lives passed in accordance with the system of the Torah, and that they also bore witness that their people had established the Torah and judged accordingly.

Before the discussion about the Torah concludes, the address turns towards the Muslim community, so that they may be drawn to the question of whether they too judge according to their own Book or not. Perhaps there are times when the personal desires of people, their enmity, and their struggles become obstacles in this path. In such difficult circumstances, what then are the duties of the guardians of the Book of Allah, and what is the punishment for opposition from people and turning away from the Book of Allah?

(Verse) "So do not fear the people, but fear Me, and do not sell My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers." (So, O People of Judaism, do not fear people but fear Me, and do not sell My signs for a paltry price. Those who do not judge by the law that Allah has revealed are the disbelievers.) (44)

Allah the Exalted certainly knew that obstacles would arise in every age in the path of judging according to the commands of Allah, and that some people would oppose it. Some people will not accept it with joy and contentment; moreover, some influential and powerful people, and some rebellious people who have hereditarily seized control of governments, will oppose it. They will oppose it because they have wrapped the mantle of Allah's right of sovereignty around themselves. Now, in the Islamic system, they see this mantle being stripped away, and the right of sovereignty becomes exclusively for Allah. They can no longer make laws for people for which Allah has not given permission. Likewise, the interests of self-seeking and materialistic elements also become obstacles in its path, those who exploit people and inflict oppression on the masses. Such people know well that the just system of Islam will never permit such oppression to continue. Likewise, those who are luxurious, self-indulgent, and addicted to the pleasures of food and pleasure stand in the way of implementing the Islamic system; those who take pride in worldly possessions and are slaves to personal interests. They fear that the Islamic Shariah will compel them to lead a pure life, and that if they do not lead a pure life, they will have to face punishment. Apart from these directions and considerations, many other kinds of barriers and obstacles also appear, especially from those people who, by nature, do not wish for goodness and cannot bear to see the reign of righteousness and justice.

Allah knew that in the path of implementing the Islamic Shariah these obstacles would appear from various directions. Allah also knew that the guardians of Islam, its strivers and martyrs, would have to face these obstacles, and that they would have to stand firmly against them, and that they would have to bear losses of life and property. Therefore Allah the Exalted addresses them.

(Verse) "So do not fear the people, but fear Me." (5:44) (Do not fear people, but fear Me.) In this way, when they fear no one but Allah, they will not be slack in implementing the Shariah out of fear of anyone. This fear may come from several directions: first, from those people who do not bow at all before the Islamic system of law and do not recognize the Islamic Shariah, who do not even accept Allah as the lawgiver; or those who do not want the Shariah implemented because it would strike at their exploitative system, with which their interests are bound up and to which they have become accustomed. Or these people belong to general misguided and deviant classes, for whom the commands of the Shariah are very heavy, and they are distressed by it. The meaning is that, without fearing all these classes, or while fearing other people, they should not hold back from implementing Allah's commands, because only Allah is worthy of being feared by us, and fear should be directed to Him alone.

Allah also knew that those who guard the Book and bear witness in the cause of Islam might be seduced by the desires of this brief worldly life. These guardians of Islam see that the ruling authorities, the wealthy classes, and the lustful and self-indulgent people stand as obstacles in the way of implementing Islam. There was a possibility that the people of religion, while dealing hypocritically with these classes, might become their agents for worldly gains, as the scholars of misguidance in every religion in every age have always done, and especially the scholars of the Children of Israel have always committed this evil act. Therefore Allah called upon such people.

(Verse) "And do not sell My signs for a small price." (5:44) (And do not sell My verses for a paltry price.)

This takes many forms, such as remaining silent at a point where truth must be spoken, or distorting the commands, or issuing rulings in which truth and falsehood are mixed together.

As for what is meant by a small price: every price is a small price, even if, by distorting the religion, the whole world comes into someone's possession. But the price obtained by these scholars of misguidance is only certain interests, certain stipends, certain titles, and other small worldly benefits, and in exchange for these they sell their religion. But for this act they will surely be cast into Hell.

If the hedge begins to eat the crop, and if the watchman himself becomes a robber, and if witnesses begin to lie, what could be worse than this? Those for whom the words "people of religion" are used, those who are called scholars, if they begin to commit treachery, if they begin to commit injustice, hide the commands of religion, keep silent about the implementation of the Shariah of Allah, change the meaning of the verses, and alter the commands of the Shariah for influential people, then for such people there is a most fitting judgment from Allah.

(Verse) "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers." (5:44) (And those who do not judge by the law that Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers.) The statement is categorical. By using the word "man" (whoever), generality is created in its meaning. "Man" is both a relative and a conditional particle, and afterward, after "fa," the clause is the answer of the condition. Thus this ruling is freed from the restriction of particular circumstances and of time and place, and becomes a general ruling: whoever does not judge according to Allah's command, whatever lineage or tribe he may be from, will be considered a disbeliever.

The cause of this ruling is what we have already explained: whoever does not judge according to the law that Allah has revealed denies Allah's right of sovereignty. Sovereignty is one of the most important attributes of Allah, and the direct requirement of sovereignty is that Allah's Shariah be the source of law. Whoever does not judge in accordance with it, and denies Allah's right of sovereignty, and claims for himself this attribute of Allah, will become a disbeliever. If someone does this, what meaning remain of Islam and faith? If there is a claim of faith and Islam with the tongue, but action, which is the best means of expressing what is in the heart, shows a person expressing disbelief, then the verbal profession of Islam becomes certainly meaningless.

To resort to evasion regarding this categorical, explicit, and general ruling is merely fleeing from facing reality. Making interpretations regarding such a definitive and explicit ruling would have no purpose other than to change the meaning of Allah's clear commands. Therefore, any person to whom this definitive ruling applies cannot escape in any way from the consequences of this explicit and emphatic ruling.

After setting out this fundamental and foundational principle of the religion of Islam, the discourse now turns back to the Torah. In the Torah too, Allah had enjoined the rulings of the Sharia, and the prophets, the people of religion and the scholars were commanded to judge according to the law of the Torah, because they had been made its guardians and were also witnesses to it.

﴿And We prescribed for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds, equal retaliation.﴾ (5:45)

"In the Torah We had written down for the Jews this command: life for life, eye for eye, nose for nose, ear for ear, tooth for tooth, and for all wounds equal retribution."

These rulings which were revealed in the Torah were retained in the Islamic Sharia and became a part of it. Thus they stand as Sharia rulings until the Day of Resurrection, because the Sharia of the Muslims is for all time. Although the implementation of these rulings can take place only in Dar al-Islam (the abode of Islam), because that is the only practical possibility, and the government which implements these rulings has its authority within the bounds of Dar al-Islam. Yet whenever it comes within the capacity of the Muslims, it is obligatory upon them to implement the Islamic Sharia outside Dar al-Islam as well, because the Islamic Sharia is for all of mankind and is not bound by limits and restrictions, since this is Allah's intention.

When these rulings of the Torah were made part of the Islamic Sharia, a legal provision was added alongside them: ﴿Whoever forgoes it as charity, it is an expiation for him.﴾ (5:45) (Then whoever gives it up as charity, it is an expiation for him.)

There was no such provision in the Torah. According to the rulings of the Torah, these crimes were not capable of being settled by compromise (compounding); in them the complainant could neither grant a pardon nor was reconciliation possible. For this reason there was no expiation for them.

It is appropriate here, in connection with the theme of Fi Zilal al-Quran, to say a brief word about the crimes of retaliation (qisas).

Islamic Sharia establishes, regarding qisas, the first principle of equality. Blood is equal for all and the punishment is also equal for all. In no other Sharia apart from Islam is there equality of a life for a life. Accordingly, in Islam there is a life for a life and an organ for the same organ. In this matter there is no distinction or consideration of region, class, lineage, blood or nation.

A life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and full equal retaliation for wounds. In this matter there is no distinction, no racial, class or national difference. Between ruler and ruled there is no difference. All are equal in the eyes of Islamic Sharia, and this is because all were created from one pair, Adam and Hawwa (Eve). (Abu Kum Adam wa Umm Hawwa.)

The golden principle which Islamic Sharia introduced to this world is the principle of equality, and by giving equality Islam, as it were, gave man a new birth. Before this, man had not attained true equality. The first principle of this equality was that all people would be equal before the law. They would obtain justice from one and the same platform.

Second, that qisas would be taken by one and the same measure from everyone, and everyone's would be the same.

Human-made systems and laws took centuries of travel to reach this degree of equality, and under the influence of Islamic Sharia the legal systems of the world attained Islamic equality only in certain respects, though in practice they could not establish the kind of equality that Islam established.

The Jews, to whom the Torah containing the golden principles of human equality had been revealed, turned away from those laws. And this turning away they did not confine to themselves and others, as the Qur'an quotes their saying: ﴿There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered (gentiles).﴾ (Aal-Imran 3:75). Rather, they could not establish equality even among themselves. In particular, they did not act upon legal equality; as they regarded the tribe of Banu Nadir as superior and the tribe of Banu Qurayzah as lowly, and the punishments for the two were separate. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, he established legal equality between them. He declared the life of the lowly among them equal to the life of the honourable.

The result of enforcing the law of qisas on this great principle is that it is a severe, lesson-giving punishment, and with its existence every person thinks again and again before taking any step regarding homicide, the infliction of grave harm, or breaking of limbs, whether he should take that step or not. Because he knows that if he kills, he will have to mount the gallows, and his lineage, his social standing and his colour or race will be of no benefit to him. He will receive exactly the punishment that his crime deserves. If he destroys someone's hand, foot or other limbs, the same limbs of his will be destroyed. If he destroys an eye, an ear or a nose, these same organs of his will be destroyed. And if anyone thinks that he will merely be imprisoned, he will never desist from such crimes, however long the prison term may be. This is because bodily punishment, bodily defect and the disfigurement of appearance are, compared with the hardships of imprisonment, more painful, as we have set out in detail in the discussion of the hadd of theft in connection with the amputation of the hand.

Furthermore, let it also be kept in view that the punishment of qisas is a punishment which, once carried out, satisfies human nature, and hatred and rancour are removed from the human soul. The wounds of the heart heal and the fire of vengeance is extinguished, a fire which tribal and pre-Islamic vengeance keeps kindling over long periods. For although some people accept blood-money for homicide and compensation for wounds, there are others who insist upon the carrying out of the punishment of qisas.

In enacting legislation, Islam has kept in view the feelings of human nature, just as the Sharia of the Torah strictly observed it, and by the full enforcement of qisas it satisfied human nature. But in the Islamic Sharia it also established for the one who takes qisas the principle that he may forgive, provided that he has the option of taking qisas. ﴿Whoever forgoes it as charity, it is an expiation for him.﴾ (5:45)

That is, whoever forgives qisas with a willing heart, Allah will, in return, forgive the sins of the one who forgives. Sometimes people may incline towards pardon and forgiveness, and there may be hope of pardon and forgiveness from them. Especially from those people who do not need financial compensation, and for whom the enforcement of qisas also does not bring satisfaction, because the relative who has been separated from them, or the loss which they have suffered personally and which is irreparable... for what will the heir of the victim gain if the killer is also killed? Or if his brother or someone else has been taken from him, what benefit will he derive from financial gains? From such things one can only obtain justice and peace and security in this world, but the feeling remains alive for ever in the hearts of the heirs or the criminal. If people have hope of forgiveness from Allah, their hearts can become pure, and the rancour of hatred can be removed from their hearts.

Imam Ahmad narrated through Waki', Yunus, Abu al-Safar: Abu al-Safar says that a man from Quraysh broke the tooth of an Ansari... He sought help from Hadrat Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him). Mu'awiyah said, "We will make him content." But the Ansari insisted that the law of qisas be enforced. Thereupon Amir Mu'awiyah said, "You know, and this Ansari knows." Abu al-Darda' was sitting in that gathering. He said, "I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: whenever a Muslim receives a wound at the hand of another Muslim and then forgives it, Allah will raise his rank or will forgive some of his shortcomings." Upon this the Ansari said, "I forgive."

Thus that man's heart was content and satisfied, although he had not agreed to any financial compensation which Hadrat Mu'awiyah had hinted at.

This is the Sharia of the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, which He has ordained for His creation, in which the inclinations and feelings of people are taken into account, in which the willing consent of hearts plays a very great part, and because of which peace, security and willing contentment arise among people.

Having explained that this was the Sharia of the Torah and that it is now part of the Islamic Sharia, a general ruling is then given:

﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the wrongdoers.﴾ (5:45) This is a general expression. There is no indication here by which we could call it restricted, yet a new attribute, "the wrongdoers" (al-zalimun), has been brought for such people.

One should not understand from describing them as "the wrongdoers" that there is some difference between this description and the earlier description "the disbelievers" (al-kafirun). Rather, those who do not judge according to the law revealed by Allah are, in addition to being disbelievers, also wrongdoers. They are disbelievers because they deny the sovereignty of Allah, since sovereignty is the exclusive right of God and only Allah can legislate; and if someone makes his own law, he claims sovereignty for himself and takes for himself the right of legislation. And he is a wrongdoer because he makes people follow his own sharia instead of the Sharia of Allah, although the Sharia of Allah is suitable for them and through it the conditions of their lives can be reformed. He also commits injustice because he casts himself into destruction, makes himself deserving of the punishment of disbelief, and plunges his own self and the lives of all people into corruption.

This meaning is demanded by the rules of Arabic grammar, because by the rules of Arabic the subject of the conditional and the verb of the condition are one: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed﴾ (45). Now this condition has a first response and a second response. Here the second response will be added to the first response of the condition, and the subject in the condition for both will be "man" (whoever), which is unrestricted and general.

Now it is shown that after the Torah this ruling also continued to apply.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 46–47:

The Injeel (Gospel) was given by Allah to Hazrat Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) so that it would serve as a system of life for the people. The Injeel itself contained no new legal system; rather, it introduced only very slight changes into the legal system of the Torah. The Injeel affirmed the legal system and the principles of the Torah, and only a few changes were introduced. Allah sent down in the Injeel guidance, new light and admonition for the Ummah of Muslims. For whom? For those who were God-fearing. Therefore, the muttaqun (the God-conscious) are those who derive guidance, light and admonition from the books of Allah, and it is such people whom these books guide. As for those hearts that are dry, lifeless and hard like stone, no admonition reaches them. Such hearts find no meaning in the Word; they find no spirit in the guidance; they find no taste in faith. They do not find a path through this guidance and these lights, nor do they answer the call and the summons. The light and radiance are present, but it brings no benefit to their sight and insight. Guidance is present, but only exalted souls perceive this guidance. Admonition is present, but only hearts that understand take admonition.

Allah placed in the Injeel too guidance, light and admonition for the God-fearing, and made it a system of life for the People of the Injeel, and a source of laws for them. That is, the Injeel was a system of life only for the People of the Injeel. It was not for all people, because the call of the Injeel was not universal; yet its implementation was necessary, as was that of the Torah, as with every prophethood and as with the call of every messenger who came before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whose call was in accordance with the call and Shariah of the Prophet ﷺ. Therefore, that part of the previous shara'i'

which agrees with Islam carries the status of the Shariah of Islam and the Shariah of the Qur'an, as we have said under the ruling of qisas.

That is, the People of the Injeel too were required to judge according to the Shariah of the Injeel:

"And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein" (5:47). That is, the fundamental principle was that judgments be made according to the commands of Allah. Neither the People of the Injeel nor the Jews had any standing so long as they implemented the Torah before Islam. After the coming of Islam, it is now the duty of all the people of the world to implement the Shariah of Islam. This Shariah is now the Shariah of all, and it is now the final messengership and the final Shariah.

"...by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are indeed the defiantly disobedient (fasiqun)" (5:47).

Here too the verse is extremely general and absolute. The attribute of kufr and zulm applied earlier to such an act is in addition to these two; the attribute of fisq is added. The fasiqun here are not any other people, but are the very kafirun and zalimun, whom the attribute of fisq also characterizes. Whoever does not judge according to the law revealed by Allah will be characterized by this attribute.

It is kufr because rejecting the Shariah of Allah amounts to rejecting the sovereignty of Allah. It is zulm because imposing on people a law other than that of Allah is zulm, and through that law corruption is brought into their lives. And it is fisq because whoever leaves the system of life of Allah becomes a fasiq automatically. In short, all these attributes are bound up with the act of not judging according to the law of Allah, and the doer of it commits all these attributes, and there is no distinction among them.

Now the discussion reaches the final messengership of the Messenger ﷺ, and the discussion concerns the final Shariah, the Islamic Shariah. In it, Islam has been presented in its final form so that it becomes the religion of all humanity, and the Shariah of Islam becomes the Shariah of all people. Moreover, all the guidance that was given to any messenger before it has been gathered and preserved within it, and this Shariah will remain in force until Allah rolls up this entire universe. It is a system of life upon which Islamic life is established in every respect. Life is confined within its circle and revolves around its axis. Man derives his beliefs and conceptions from it; he structures his collective system in accordance with it, and he shapes his individual and social relations accordingly. This Shariah has been revealed so that it prevails in the courts, that a system is established according to it, that its dominance is seen in books and offices, and that its following and implementation be carried out with utmost care. No part of it should be abandoned, and no part of it should be altered, whether it concerns minor or major matters, because the choice is either the Islamic Shariah or it is jahiliyyah. In implementing this Shariah, no laxity or compromise can be permitted with the intention that many people be gathered under the name of Islam on that pretext, because if Allah had willed, He would have made all people one ummah. Allah desires that the rule of His Shariah be established; then whatever happens, happens.

That is, the People of the Injeel too were required to judge according to the Shariah of the Injeel:

"And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein" (5:47). That is, the fundamental principle was that judgments be made according to the commands of Allah. Neither the People of the Injeel nor the Jews had any standing so long as they implemented the Torah before Islam. After the coming of Islam, it is now the duty of all the people of the world to implement the Shariah of Islam. This Shariah is now the Shariah of all, and it is now the final messengership and the final Shariah.

"...by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are indeed the defiantly disobedient (fasiqun)" (5:47).

Here too the verse is extremely general and absolute. The attribute of kufr and zulm applied earlier to such an act is in addition to these two; the attribute of fisq is added. The fasiqun here are not any other people, but are the very kafirun and zalimun, whom the attribute of fisq also characterizes. Whoever does not judge according to the law revealed by Allah will be characterized by this attribute.

It is kufr because rejecting the Shariah of Allah amounts to rejecting the sovereignty of Allah. It is zulm because imposing on people a law other than that of Allah is zulm, and through that law corruption is brought into their lives. And it is fisq because whoever leaves the system of life of Allah becomes a fasiq automatically. In short, all these attributes are bound up with the act of not judging according to the law of Allah, and the doer of it commits all these attributes, and there is no distinction among them.

Now the discussion reaches the final messengership of the Messenger ﷺ, and the discussion concerns the final Shariah, the Islamic Shariah. In it, Islam has been presented in its final form so that it becomes the religion of all humanity, and the Shariah of Islam becomes the Shariah of all people. Moreover, all the guidance that was given to any messenger before it has been gathered and preserved within it, and this Shariah will remain in force until Allah rolls up this entire universe. It is a system of life upon which Islamic life is established in every respect. Life is confined within its circle and revolves around its axis. Man derives his beliefs and conceptions from it; he structures his collective system in accordance with it, and he shapes his individual and social relations accordingly. This Shariah has been revealed so that it prevails in the courts, that a system is established according to it, that its dominance is seen in books and offices, and that its following and implementation be carried out with utmost care. No part of it should be abandoned, and no part of it should be altered, whether it concerns minor or major matters, because the choice is either the Islamic Shariah or it is jahiliyyah. In implementing this Shariah, no laxity or compromise can be permitted with the intention that many people be gathered under the name of Islam on that pretext, because if Allah had willed, He would have made all people one ummah. Allah desires that the rule of His Shariah be established; then whatever happens, happens.

(Verse 48 to 50.)

When a person reflects on the clarity of this expression, on this decisive ruling, and on this complete authority, he finds that every matter that could arise in a person's heart concerning the abandonment of the Shariah has been forestalled. On reflection, one is astonished that any Muslim could, despite these directives, abandon the Shariah in any way. Such a person abandons it under the pretext of circumstances and necessities, and yet still claims to be a Muslim. Even more astonishing is that a person should completely abandon the Islamic Shariah and still say that he is a Muslim. The audacity of these people is such that they have thrown off the yoke of Islam from their necks, yet still call themselves Muslims as before. They have entirely excluded the whole Shariah from their lives. They do not acknowledge the sovereignty of Allah, and this is so because they do not confine lawmaking to Allah, and they do not accept that the Islamic Shariah is practicable in every kind of circumstance and at every time, and that it is obligatory upon us to implement the Shariah in all circumstances.

﴿And We have sent down to you the Book with the truth﴾ (5:48). (O Prophet, We sent down this Book to you, bringing the truth.)

This truth is such that it comes from Allah, and Allah has the right to reveal the Shariah and to impose laws and obligations upon people. Furthermore, the contents of this Book are all truth: its doctrines are true, its laws are true, the stories and reports recorded in it are true, and the guidance given in it is rightly given.

﴿Confirming what is before it of the Book and as a guardian over it﴾ (5:48). (It confirms what remains of the Book before it, and it is a protector and guardian over it.)

Thus, it is the final complete form of the religion of Allah, and the final source and point of reference. It is the final system of life and the final law, and after it there will be no change in law, Shariah, system or constitution, and no amendment or abrogation.

The natural requirement of this principle is that we refer all our differences to this Book, so that it may decide concerning them, whether the differences relate to beliefs and concepts, as has generally occurred among the adherents of heavenly religions and their scholars, or whether the differences exist among the Muslims themselves. The reference and source to which they will turn in all the affairs of their whole life is this very Book. And in these matters, the personal opinion of even the greatest of human beings has no value, if that opinion lacks a proof from the Qur'an and Sunnah behind it.

Accordingly, the direct requirement of this principle and reality appears as follows:

﴿So judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, diverting from what has come to you of the truth﴾ (5:48). (Therefore, judge among the people by the law that Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires by turning away from the truth that has come to you.) Initially, this command was addressed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, concerning those People of the Book who used to bring their disputes to him. But this command is not restricted to that occasion of revelation; rather, it is a general command, applicable to every time and place, because after you there is no new Messenger to come, nor will any new prophethood be sent after you, such that this command could be changed, on the ground that the Qur'an is no longer the point of reference.

Allah has perfected this religion and thereby completed His favour upon the Muslims, and has chosen this Islamic system of life for all the believers. Now there is no path to amendment or change in it, nor can they, on any principle, replace a command of Allah by changing it and enforcing another command in its place.
