When Allah chose this religion for people, He knew that this religion contains within itself room for all people, and when this religion was made the point of reference for guidance, Allah knew that in it there is welfare and good for everyone. It can resolve all the problems of the lives of all people until the Day of Resurrection, and that any change in it (let alone turning away from it) is a cause of disbelief. A person who does such an act has left the religion, even if he calls himself a Muslim a hundred thousand times with his tongue. This is the necessary consequence of the nature of this religion.

Allah knew that on this path people would present lengthy excuses, and these excuses would be presented so that, turning away from the law revealed by Allah, they would follow the laws made by those who have falsely become rulers, or who are themselves subjugated. In some circumstances, fears will arise in some people's hearts about the full implementation of the Islamic system, but in these verses Allah twice admonished the Noble Prophet ﷺ about this: that he should not follow the desires and apprehensions of such people, and should guard against the trial posed by such people.

The first of these apprehensions is that a person has a natural urge that everyone should be pleased with him, and that the concerns of all classes and all inclinations should be taken into account. In those inclinations that conflict with the Islamic Shariah, their concerns should be considered, leniency should be shown in minor matters, or negligence should be exercised in matters that apparently do not fall within the sphere of the Shariah.

The reports state that the Jews made an offer to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they would believe if he would compromise with them on certain rulings, one of which was the command of stoning (rajm). This warning was revealed especially on such an occasion, as is evident from it. However, the command given in these verses is not restricted to any particular cause; it is general. This command may apply to various circumstances, and those who bear the Shariah may face such situations in every age. But it was Allah's will that He should speak most decisively in this matter and close every hidden path of human desire, by which a person, in accordance with circumstances and events, compromises on the implementation of the whole Shariah, or compromises to placate certain people, while the desires and inclinations of people differ. Accordingly, Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ that if Allah had willed, He would have made people one community, but Allah has ordained for every nation a system and a way, and has tested them with the Shariah He bestowed upon them, and they will be tested concerning what has been given to them for this worldly life. Each one devises for himself a method. After this, all people will be returned, and Allah will inform them of the reality and will call them to account for the ways they adopted. Therefore, it is not permissible for them to be lax or negligent in the Shariah, nor to strive to gather people of different schools and paths, because such a gathering is not even possible.

﴿For each of you We have made a law and a clear way. Had Allah willed, He would have made you one nation, but [He did this] to test you in what He has given you. So compete in good deeds. To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of that about which you used to differ﴾ (5:48).

Thus Allah has closed all the avenues of Satan: all those paths which apparently appear good and through which the hearts could be won over, especially in a situation where some matters of the Shariah's implementation are bargained away, and through this negligence all people are kept satisfied, or where slogans such as "attaining national unity" are raised through laxity in the Shariah.

The Islamic Shariah is a most precious treasure. It is too precious for an attempt to be made, at the cost of some of its parts, to achieve some goal that the decree of Allah has not willed. It is Allah who created people, and gave each individual a distinct capacity, and the paths and inclinations of people are entirely different and varied. Each has his own method and his own way. And it was the requirement of Allah's wisdom that people be created with such diverse natures. Allah presented guidance to them, and they were left in such a way that they strive to outdo one another. This competition is a kind of trial among them, and because of this trial, when all people go to Allah, they will be rewarded or punished.

For this would be obstinate argument and a failed endeavour: that someone should try to unite people by sacrificing some part of the Islamic Shariah, or that under the pretext of reforming people and correcting their economic conditions, some unusual interpretation of the Shariah should be devised. Change in the Islamic Shariah, or turning away from it, can only produce corruption in the world, not reform. Such an approach can yield only this result: that people turn away from the straight and correct way of Allah, that justice and fairness disappear from people's lives, and that some people become slaves of others, and then some of them attain the station of lord and deity over others. This would be a great mischief and corruption, and such a great evil cannot be permitted to occur for the sake of a merely imaginary goal, especially when that goal is unattainable, for Allah has not established the principle that all people should come onto one single path. This goal also contradicts the wisdom and plan under which Allah created different paths, different methods, and different tastes. It is He who is also the Creator of truth, and all matters, first and last, are in His hand, and all people will return to Him.

An attempt to remove some part of the Shariah for such goals is, according to this verse, a failed endeavour, and the practical life of humanity bears witness to this. For it there is no practical justification needed, and there is no evidence for it from the will of Allah, nor is there anything of the kind in Islamic consciousness. Islamic consciousness and feeling demand that the will of Allah be put into effect. Some people who call themselves Muslims even go so far as to say: "We do not implement the Islamic system of Shariah because it would reduce the number of tourists coming to our country." Indeed, they say exactly this.

Thus the Qur'an clarifies this reality again; the first verse is also this one:

﴿So judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, diverting from what has come to you of the truth﴾ (5:48). (So judge between them according to the truth that Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires in preference to the truth that has come to you.) This could mean that the whole Shariah should not be abandoned merely because of people's desires. But if a part of the Shariah has to be left, then here it is commanded concerning this that even some of what Allah has revealed is forbidden to be left.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 49:

(Verse) "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they divert you from some of what Allah has revealed to you." (5:49) (So, O Prophet (ﷺ), judge between these people according to the law that Allah has revealed. Be wary, lest these people, by putting you into temptation, divert you even slightly from the guidance that God has sent down to you.)

This admonition is extremely severe and very detailed. It is a true depiction of the situation, because this is a great temptation. We must be wary of it and make all our judgments according to the Shari'ah of Allah. If there is not a complete Shari'ah, then there will be complete pursuit of desires, which Allah warns against.

In the next verse, certain doubts and anxieties are removed, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is consoled: that if these people do not like to implement the lesser rulings of the Shari'ah before its major rulings, and if these people do not adopt Islam as a complete religion, or do not make their decisions according to Islamic Shari'ah, (this refers to the period when judgment according to Shari'ah was optional, and the system of Shari'ah had not yet been definitively enforced; when the Dar al-Islam (abode of Islam) was fully established, then judgment according to Shari'ah was made obligatory) then these people should prepare themselves for the punishment of Allah.

(Verse) "So if they turn away, know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins. And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient." (5:49)

"So if they turn away, know that Allah intends to bring them affliction for some of their sins, and it is a fact that most of these people are transgressors."

If these people turn away, what responsibility rests upon you? You should hold firmly to the Shari'ah with full strength in your own place and implement the commands of Allah. Their aversion and turning away should not loosen your grip and should not remove you from your position. These people are turning away only because Allah is going to put them into severe affliction for some of their sins. This is Allah's plan: that these people suffer evil consequences, not you. Neither you, nor the Shari'ah of Allah, nor the religion of Allah will be affected, nor will the Islamic front that has fully grasped the Shari'ah be affected. Yes, it is part of human nature that the majority of people remain engaged in depravity and sin, and therefore they go out of Islam and deviate. (Verse) "And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient." (5:49) Surely the majority of people remain engaged in depravity and immorality. These people will continue in this way, and you cannot change this situation. The Shari'ah is not at fault in this, and it is not possible to set the majority upon the straight path.

In this way, all the avenues of Satan's whisperings within the soul of a believer are closed, and a believer walks his path with proof. The question of abandoning any ruling from the Islamic Shari'ah and Islamic commands does not arise. This cannot be done for any worldly purpose, nor can it be done in any circumstance.

Here the Holy Qur'an brings humanity to a crossroads and stands them there. Either they must adopt the path of judgment and law, or they will adopt the path of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). There is neither a third path nor any alternative path between these two crossroads. In the world the commands of Allah will be enforced, and the Islamic Shari'ah will be enforced in people's lives; that is, either the Islamic system will lead humanity, or the rules of jahiliyyah will be enforced, lawlessness will be enforced, and the system of slavery will continue. Now at this crossroads, people must decide what they want.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 50 (part 1 of 2):

(Verse) "Afa hukmal-jahiliyyati yabghoon? Wa man ahsanu minallahi hukman liqawmin yuqinoon." (5:50)

(Do they then seek the judgement of the Age of Ignorance? And who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who have certainty?)

Here this verse defines the meaning and implications of jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance, a state of disbelief and rebellion against God). It is the Qur'an of Allah that defines the meaning of jahiliyyah, and according to it, jahiliyyah is that human rule be imposed over human beings in the state. This is in essence the slavery of humans by humans, a denial of the sovereignty of Allah, and an abandonment of the doctrine of the sovereignty of Allah. This denial and abandonment is, in fact, an affirmation of the sovereignty of humans, and the worship and servitude of humans.

In the light of this verse, jahiliyyah is not related to time and place; rather, jahiliyyah is the name of a condition which existed yesterday, exists today, and will exist tomorrow. Therefore, what is prohibited is that a jahili condition, which contradicts Islam, should be adopted in opposition to the Islamic system.

People may have different circumstances, and in every age, either they will act in accordance with the Shariah of Allah, except that they abandon some of its parts, or they will accept the system of the Shariah completely with submission and contentment. In such a case, people will be counted within the religion of Allah. Or they are deciding their affairs according to a law made by humans, whatever its form may be, and they accept it; therefore these people will be counted within the religion of those whose law they accept. In such circumstances these people will certainly not enter the religion of Islam. Whoever does not get judgement made according to the command of Allah, in fact gets judgement made according to jahiliyyah, and whoever denies the Shariah of Allah, in fact desires the Shariah of jahiliyyah and dwells in jahiliyyah.

This is a crossroads on which Allah the Exalted places people, and after that people are given the choice to adopt whichever path they wish to go upon.

After this, people who want judgement according to jahiliyyah are questioned with stern gaze. This interrogation is in the negative form, yet in an interrogative manner the supremacy of the commands of God is decided.

(Verse) "Wa man ahsanu minallahi hukman liqawmin yuqinoon." (5:50) (And who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who have certainty?) ... Yes, it is entirely correct that there is no law and command other than the law and commands of Allah. Who is there who can claim that he is the legislator of people, or that he can make a better law for them than Allah the Exalted? What evidence does he hold for this great claim?

Can anyone claim that he knows people better than the Creator of people? Can anyone say that he is more sympathetic to people than the Lord of people? And is there anyone who can say that he is more aware of the interests of people than Allah, the God of the worlds? Can anyone dare to say that Allah, who was establishing the final Shariah for people, who was making His Messenger ﷺ the Seal of the Prophets, who was making their message the Seal of Messages and their Shariah an everlasting Shariah, was unaware of any circumstance of the times that would come until the Day of Resurrection? Was He unaware that new needs of people would arise, new circumstances would emerge, and that in this legislation He would have taken no account of them? The implication then would be that Allah did not know of these circumstances, and that this knowledge was revealed to people only in the final age.

The one who answers this question is someone who wishes to remove the Islamic Shariah from the stream of life, who wishes to implement the Shariah of jahiliyyah in its place. He wishes to change his desires into law, or regards the desires of a people as law, or regards the desires of a generation as higher than the command of Allah and the law of Allah. I ask: what answer does such a person give to the above questions, especially if this person also holds the conceit that he is a Muslim?

Circumstances, environment, people's lack of interest, fear of enemies, and so forth: were all these matters not within the knowledge of Allah? Especially at a time when Allah was commanding Muslims to implement the Shariah in their society, to live their lives according to the Islamic system, and not to leave out any one of the commands that Allah has revealed.

Was this matter not within the knowledge of Allah? New circumstances will arise and in them there will be no Shariah ruling. New customs will emerge and circumstances will compel people. All these matters were within the knowledge of Allah when He was commanding with great severity that the Shariah be implemented, and if they did not implement it, He was warning them of such severe consequences.

A non-Muslim may say whatever he wishes, but what will Muslims, who are the callers to Islam, answer to these questions? Can they remain upon Islam, or can anything of Islam remain with them if they think and say these things?

Undoubtedly this is a decisive and clear-cut matter: a person stands at a crossroads. There is no other path, and no debate or wrangling is possible in it, nor can any sophistry be effective. It is either one path or the other: either Islam or jahiliyyah, either faith or disbelief, either the command of Allah or the rule of jahiliyyah. Those who do not judge according to the commands of Allah are disbelievers, wrongdoers and transgressors. And among the governed, those who do not accept the commands of Allah do not remain believers.

For a believer, this issue must be most clear and decisive in his heart and mind. He should not accept the influence of any time or place upon the implementation of the Shariah, nor should he waver, and in this matter he should show no regard for friend or enemy. As long as Muslims do not reach a firm decision in their consciences on this issue, their circumstances cannot be set right, nor will they have a single standard and measure, nor will their system be clear, nor will there be any distinction between truth and falsehood within their consciences, and they will not be able to advance a single step upon the highway of Islam. If it is permitted that this issue remain unclear in the minds of the masses, ambiguous, and that it be left loose among people and the common folk as it is, then... but those who wish to become Muslims properly must have clear minds. They should cultivate this quality within themselves.

Lesson No. 50 at a glance:

Regarding the time of revelation of this Surah, what we said in the introduction is confirmed by the verses of this lesson, namely that this Surah was not entirely revealed after the conquest (Fath), which was after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah in the sixth year of Hijrah. Several parts of this Surah had been revealed earlier, at least before the expulsion of the Banu Qurayzah, which took place in the fourth year of Hijrah, that is, in the time of the Battle of the Confederates (Ahzab), although we cannot call it earlier than the period of the expulsion of the Banu Nadir (after the Battle of Uhud) and the Banu Qaynuqa (after the Battle of Badr).

In any case, these verses point to certain events, and they allude to some events that occurred within the Muslim community. They take up the circumstances that existed in Medina regarding the hypocrites and the Jews, and these circumstances could certainly not have remained when the strength and power of the Jews had been broken, and their final blow, in the form of the event of the Banu Qurayzah, had taken place in the fourth year of Hijrah.

The prohibition that you should not take the Jews and Christians as friends, and the warning, indeed the threat, that whoever takes them as friends will be one of them, and the indication that those in whose hearts is a disease hasten to them, saying that they fear misfortune, and the instilling of aversion in Muslims, that they should not befriend these people because they treat your religion as a jest and sport, and the indication that they mock the establishment of prayer: all these events could only be possible if the Jews in Medina possessed full strength and power. Had this strength not existed, such circumstances could not have arisen in Medina, and such events could not have occurred, nor would such a severe threat and warning have been necessary, nor would such repeated opposition have been needed. Nor would the nature of the Jews have been described, nor would they have been so publicized and so criticized, nor would there have been a need to unveil their deceit and trickery, nor would their circumstances have been so repeated or so illuminated.

Some traditions also exist, in which certain circumstances and events are linked to the event of the Banu Qaynuqa, although that event took place after the Battle of Badr. Concerning them, there is the position of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and his saying that the Jews are his friends and that he maintains ties with the Jews, such as his statement: "I am a man who fears bad circumstances, so I cannot abandon the support of my allies."

Even if these traditions did not exist, it would still be known from the theme and subject matter of the Surah that its topics, the events described within it, the events of the Seerah of the Prophet ﷺ, and its stages and periods in Medina all give preference to what we have mentioned above, and likewise in the introduction of the Surah we adopted this same position.

From all the verses of this lesson, the method is apparent by which the Qur'anic method of training prepared the Muslim community to perform the role which it was to perform in this world by the will of Allah. Also, from these verses, the fundamental elements that were necessary to be present in the mind and thought of a Muslim soul and a Muslim community are apparent. These fundamental elements are the same for every age. They are permanent elements and permanent principles, and they are not specific to any one age or any one generation. These are the principles upon which an individual is built, and the organization of a community is likewise built upon these very principles.

The Qur'an builds every Muslim individual on the foundation that all his sympathies, with complete sincerity, should be with Allah, His Messenger, the ideology, and the community established upon it. There must be complete boycott between a Muslim individual and community and that individual and community which stands opposed to the Islamic ranks, and which has raised the banners hostile to Islam, that is, the community which does not acknowledge the leadership of the Holy Prophet ﷺ and does not merge into the community which stands at the position of the Party of Allah (Hizbullah). The Qur'an gives a person the awareness that he is fortunate that Allah has chosen him for His work, and that he is the veil of the divine decree, and through him the decrees of Allah become manifest from behind the veil, in the form of historical events that occur, and that this is the great bounty of Allah, which whoever has received, has received. Except that to form friendships with any communities other than the Islamic community is tantamount to apostasy from the religion of Islam, and is abandoning the station which Allah has granted them, and casting off the robe of honour which Allah had clothed them in.

These guidances are given very clearly in the verses of this lesson, for example: "O you who believe! Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then he is indeed one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."

"O people who have believed, whoever of you reverts from his religion (let him go), Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah, and not fearing the blame of any blamer. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing."

"Your allies are none but Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah, and they bow [in worship]. And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies - then indeed, the party of Allah - they will be the predominant."

Then the Qur'an also instils in a Muslim's awareness the reality of his enemies, and makes them aware of the reality of the struggle which is raging between them and the Muslims. This struggle is an ideological struggle. Creed and ideology are a matter which is constantly in progress between a Muslim and his enemies. The enmity of Muslims is, before all other things, for their creed and religion. The disbelievers hold this enmity toward Muslims because they have determined to disobey this religion. This is why whoever follows this religion upon the straight path, they utterly dislike him.

"Say: O People of the Scripture, do you resent us for no reason except that we have believed in Allah and in what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient?" This is the ideology, and this is ideological difference, and these are the motives of difference.

The importance of this system of training and the guidance given within it is very great. This is because love for Allah, passionate attachment to the Messenger and his religion, attachment and love for the community founded upon it, and understanding the true nature of the struggle that arises between this religion and its enemies, and knowing its enemies well, are in fact the essence of the religion. These are matters whose importance cannot be denied. Their importance also lies in this: without them the essential conditions of faith are not fulfilled, an individual Muslim's personal training is not completed, and it is not possible to form a community that can act as a driving force for this religion. Those who are carrying the banner of this religion cannot become firm Muslims until then; until then they cannot possess a solid personality; and until then they cannot bring about any change on this earth, unless distance arises in their hearts from all those who are raising banners against this Islamic front. Until the love and friendship of the believers is reserved exclusively for Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and until they grasp the true reality of this struggle, the requirements of the religion cannot be fulfilled. And until they are certain that they have gathered solely for this purpose, and that our enemies are all united and in agreement against the Islamic community and Islamic beliefs.

These verses do not stop merely at informing the Muslims of the reasons for which the enemies of the religion of Islam have launched war against them; rather, the verses also identify the enemies, clarify the extent of their depravity and sinfulness, and make known how far they have deviated from the religion, so that the Muslims may know what kind of enemies they are facing, and that their conscience may be satisfied that they are in the right in this confrontation. This battle is in dire need and there is no escape from it. "O you who believe! Do not take the Jews and the Christians as friends; they are allies of one another." 

"O you who believe! Among those who were given the Scripture before you, and the disbelievers, do not take as friends those who have made your religion a mockery and a diversion. Fear Allah, if you are believers. When you call to prayer, they take it as a mockery and a sport. That is because they are a people who do not understand." 

"When they come to you, they say, 'We believe,' while they came in disbelief and left in disbelief. And Allah knows best what they conceal. You see many of them racing to sin, transgression and consuming unlawful gain. Evil indeed is what they have been doing." 

"The Jews say, 'The hand of Allah is chained.' Their own hands are chained, and they are cursed for what they have said. Rather, His hands are both outstretched; He spends as He wills." 

Because of these qualities of theirs, and because of their attitude toward the Muslim community, and because they have all united against the Muslim community, and because they ridicule the religion of the Muslims and especially the prayer, a true Muslim has no other recourse but to defend himself against these people with complete seriousness and full composure.

These texts also mention the outcome of this confrontation and give its complete result here. It is also made clear what Islam produces in this world itself, even before the Hereafter: "And whoever takes Allah, His Messenger and the believers as allies, then indeed the party of Allah are the ones who will be victorious." ... "If the People of the Scripture had believed and been god-fearing, We would have removed their misdeeds from them and admitted them to Gardens of Bliss. If only they had established the Torah, the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have been provided with sustenance from above them and from beneath their feet."

Moreover, these verses also mention the qualities of those Muslims whom Allah chooses for the service of His religion, and grants them the great favour of having been chosen for this noble role: "O you who believe! Whoever of you turns back from his religion, [then let him go]—Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah and not fearing the blame of any blamer. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing."

All these decisions and resolutions are measures for the establishment of the Islamic system, and their purpose is that an individual Muslim and the Muslim community be trained upon firm foundations.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 51–52 (part 1 of 3):

Verses 51 to 53.

It seems appropriate here to define the concept of walayah (alliance and close friendship) and rafaqah (companionship), from which Allah strictly forbids the believers, saying that there should be no companionship with the Jews and Christians.

The meaning of this companionship is that there should be no treaty of alliance, mutual cooperation and mutual support with the Jews and Christians. It does not mean that you follow their religion. This is because it is not even possible to imagine that there could be a Muslim who follows the religion of the Jews and Christians. In reality, this was a friendship of mutual alliance and cooperation, concerning which the minds of Muslims at that time were not clear that it was also prohibited. Muslims thought that such alliances and cooperation were still permissible. This confusion arose because before Islam, treaties of friendship existed among these people, and such things also used to happen in the early days of Islam, especially in the early days of Madinah. Through these texts, Allah prohibited this and declared such treaties void. Especially since the Jews did not act upon the agreement made between Muslims and Jews according to the Charter of Madinah, and it became clear from this that a treaty between the people of Islam and them was no longer possible.

This meaning and implication is clearly evident from the expressions of the Quran. (See regarding the Muslims of Madinah and those Muslims who were still in Makkah and had not migrated: ﴿Mā lakum min walāyatihim min shay'in ḥattā yuhājirū﴾, meaning, there is no friendship and companionship between you and them until they migrate.) It is clear that by this walayah is not meant walayah fi al-din, that is, Islamic brotherhood. Here walayah means that friendship in which, by way of a treaty, mutual support and cooperation are pledged. This treaty cannot even be made with those who, although Muslims, have not yet migrated to the abode of Islam. This is the very kind that these verses prohibit the people of Islam from, that they should not make such friendship with the Jews and Christians, whereas in the early days of Madinah this bond was established.

Dealing with the People of the Book with tolerance is one thing, and making them your friends through treaties of friendship is another. But the people of Islam, in their minds, have not yet grasped the reality of the religion, and have not yet understood the duties and functions of the religion, that religion is an organized and realistic methodology. It remains in constant movement, and its purpose is to create a real situation on this earth that conforms to the Islamic conception of life. This conception of life differs from all the concepts that have been introduced among humanity. Thus, this Islamic situation then clashes with all the concepts and situations that are opposed to it. Furthermore, it also clashes with people's desires, with their sinfulness and their deviations, and this system also enters into such a struggle that there is no escape from it. This clash occurs because the Islamic system creates a new situation, and it continually moves positively towards its goal.

Those people in whose consciousness and feeling this aspect of the Islamic worldview is not clear, and in whose consciousness the great confrontation between Islam and other sects and creeds is not well understood, and who are heedless of these clear Quranic guidances, they do not distinguish between those guidances in which tolerance towards the People of the Book living in an Islamic society is commanded and all their rights are protected, and those treaties concerning alliance and mutual support, according to which walayah and friendship can be only with Allah, His Messenger and the Muslim community. They forget that when a confrontation arises between Islam and the People of the Book, the People of the Book and all other disbelievers are allies of one another, and this is their permanent policy and characteristic. They bear enmity towards Muslims merely because of their Islam, and they will never be pleased with any Muslim until he abandons his religion and adopts obedience to their religion. This is why all the People of the Book are constantly at war against Islam and Islamic communities. Yet sometimes this statement slips from their mouths, and what is hidden in their hearts is far greater. This and other such matters.

A Muslim has been guided in any case to adopt a tolerant attitude towards the People of the Book. But he has been prevented from making a treaty of friendship with them, that is, mutual support and allied friendship. The path on which he must walk in order to establish the religion and make it dominant over the world is very far from the path of the People of the Book, even if they display great tolerance and affection. This is because they will never be pleased that Muslims remain upon their religion and implement the Islamic system, and this tolerance will not stop them from uniting to fight against Islam. They always do so.

It would be a great naivety and a great heedlessness if we were to think that the path to the dominance of religion for us is the same path on which the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, are walking, and that by walking on that path we will confront the disbelievers and atheists, whereas the disbelievers and atheists nowadays are most of all these People of the Book. Thus, the confrontation now too is between Muslims and the People of the Book.

Among us, those simple-minded people do not grasp this whole reality, and in every age there have been Muslims who believe that Muslims and the People of the Book can together wage war against atheism and materialism, because the People of the Book too are people of religion and we too are people of religion. But these simple-minded people forget all the teachings of the Holy Quran, indeed they forget the entire Islamic history. The People of the Book are those very people who used to say to the polytheists and atheists: ﴿Hā'ulā'i ahdā min alladhīna āmanū sabīlā﴾ (These polytheists are more guided on the path than those who have believed). And it was the People of the Book who gathered the factions against the Muslims and marched upon Madinah. They used to give protection to all the factions. It was the People of the Book who waged the Crusades against Islam for two hundred years, and it was these same People of the Book who committed unimaginable crimes against Muslims in Andalusia. It is these People of the Book who recently expelled Arab Muslims from Palestine and settled Jews in their place, and in this matter they continued to cooperate with all atheists and heretics. It is these People of the Book who are expelling Muslims from every place: in Abyssinia, in Somalia, in Eritrea and in Algeria; in short, everywhere they are cooperating with atheists, polytheists and idol-worshippers in this expulsion and this oppression. In Yugoslavia, China, Turkestan and India, and everywhere, they are supporters of the enemies of Islam.

After these complete and comprehensive guidances and decisions of the Holy Quran, there still arise among us people who say that there can be cooperation and friendship between Muslims and these People of the Book against atheistic materialism. Such people have in reality not studied the Holy Quran well, and if they have studied it, then there has occurred a confusion in their minds between the Islamic concept of religious tolerance and the concept of walayah and friendship.

These are the kinds of people in whose consciousness Islam does not hold the status that Islam is a worldview which does not accept any other worldview from people. Nor is it in their minds that Islam is a positive movement which wants to completely change the situation of this world, and that the People of the Book have always blocked the path of Islam, just as they are standing blocking the path of Islam even today. And this is the position of the People of the Book which never changes, because it is for them the only natural position.

We leave these people in their very position, to remain heedless or feigning heedlessness, and we ourselves reflect upon the guidances of Allah, which are entirely clear and explicit.

﴿Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū lā tattakhidhū al-yahūda wa al-naṣārā awliyā'a ba'ḍuhum awliyā'u ba'ḍin wa man yatawallahum minkum fa-innahu minhum inna Allāha lā yahdī al-qawma al-ẓālimīn﴾ (51)

"O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."

This address is directed to the Muslim community working in the city of Madinah, but these same guidances are also for all the communities that work anywhere on this earth, and these same guidances will remain until the Day of Resurrection, for all those upon whom this title is rightly applied, ﴿Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū﴾. The need for these guidances arose at the time of the revelation of the Quran, and these guidances were given to the believers because at that time there was no complete severance between Muslims and the Jews living around Madinah. Alliance and allied relations of walayah still remained among them. Economic and other dealings took place with one another, and relations of neighbourhood and companionship also existed between the two. This situation was the natural result of the historical and economic conditions of Madinah, because there were relations between the Arabs and the Jews there. Due to these circumstances, the Jews were getting the opportunity to conspire against the Muslims and to continue their activities against the religion of Islam. These conspiracies are of various kinds, and their full details have been given in the commentary of the previous five parts, and in this section too some aspects of that conspiracy have been taken up.

The revelation of the Quran continued solely for the purpose that the Muslim's thinking and, to the necessary extent, his consciousness regarding the struggle that confronts him in this world concerning his creed and worldview, and the goal of establishing the religion in view of it, should become firm. Furthermore, there should be a complete chasm between the Muslim consciousness and all those people and forces that block this religion and its system, and who in no way wish to come under the Islamic banner. Yes, it is another matter that moral tolerance or social boycott does not fall within the scope of this complete boycott. Moral conduct and social relations are, in any case, qualities of a good Muslim, which are never separated from him at any time. Yes, in these guidances, friendship and allied relations with them are prohibited, which can only be with Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and this is the consciousness of separation that should exist within a Muslim everywhere, in every age and in every generation. Reflect carefully upon the words of the Quran.

"O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."

These people are allies of one another themselves. This is a reality which is beyond the bounds of time and place, because this reality is a natural reality and it is the demand of their temperament. These people have never become friends of the believers in any place or in any era. Centuries have passed, and not a single example of their friendship has come to light, and this statement of Allah has remained true. Even in the war against the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), the People of the Book were united among themselves. After him, they have remained united in enmity against every Islamic community, and throughout the long chain of history they have remained united against Islam across the entire globe. Not once has this rule admitted an exception, and in the world there has always been what the Holy Quran has used here as a description of the People of the Book. The Holy Quran did not describe this attribute of theirs in connection with scattered incidents. The manner in which the Quran has used this nominal sentence here: ﴿Ba'ḍuhum awliyā'u ba'ḍin﴾ (5:51). This is not merely a mode of expression, but rather it is intended to show that this mutual walayah and friendship is their permanent attribute.

After this, the Quran draws the natural consequences of this reality. When the Jews and Christians are only friends of one another, then any Muslim who makes friends with them will be counted among them. Whoever among the ranks of Islam is their friend will remain in the Islamic ranks? He in practice negates the attribute "Islamic" from himself. He in practice wraps upon himself the attribute of Judaism and Christianity. Yet this is a natural result: ﴿Wa man yatawallahum minkum fa-innahu minhum﴾ (5:51) (And whoever among you allies with them, then indeed he is one of them).

Such a person wrongs himself and wrongs his religion, because he has given his love to them. Then Allah does not guide such a person, nor does He accept him back into the Islamic ranks: ﴿Inna Allāha lā yahdī al-qawma al-ẓālimīn﴾ (5:51) (Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people).

This is a translation of the Urdu passage, following the rules you set (quotations of the Qur'an in ﴿ ﴾, transliteration of technical terms with glosses on first mention, honorifics as (ﷺ)).

The community of Madinah was faced with an extremely frightening warning. This warning, though severe, is entirely natural, and there is no artificial harshness in it. Therefore whoever commits this prohibited act is one of them; had he not been one of them, a Muslim could never under any circumstances become a wali (protector) and friend of the Jews and Christians. Nor can such a person remain a member of the ranks of Islam, because the friendship and alliance of the members of any Islamic community is exclusively with Allah, His Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers. This is a crossroads and a point that demands a decision.

In the matter of complete separation between a Muslim and the opponents of the Islamic system and the advocates of other systems, no leniency can be adopted. One has raised the flag of Islam, and the other has raised a flag opposed to Islam. If he (the Muslim) does so, he will not be able to establish the unique system of Islam on this earth, nor will he be able to show any noteworthy activity in this regard.

When a Muslim has the firm conviction that his religion is the only religion that Allah will accept from people, then within that conviction there remains no flaw and no leniency. He also believes that after the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) there is no further prophethood, and that this Islamic way of life is the unique system which he must establish in people's lives, and that no system of the world is viable in comparison to it. The life of humanity on this earth cannot be set right until Muslims establish this system; and that Allah will not forgive him if he does not exert his full strength in the path of the establishment and dominance of this religion. The truth is that Allah does not accept any other system as a substitute for this system, rather He does not accept any substitute for any part of the Islamic system. And that until he purifies the Islamic beliefs and concepts, removing every error and admixture from among them, and until he removes all admixtures from the detailed system and legal matters, Islam cannot attain dominance, except where Allah has preserved something from the earlier shariahs. In short, until a believer is completely single-minded and holds firm conviction in all these matters, he cannot bear this burden, nor can he practically establish the way of life whose heavy duty Allah has placed upon his shoulders.

The truth is that the obligation of establishing the religion (iqamat-e-deen) is a difficult duty. Its path has severe difficulties, and the responsibilities of this path are back-breaking. On this path sit spiteful enemies, hidden snares are laid, and there are places of grief and sorrow which at times become unbearable. If this were not the case, then what hardship would there be in the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) that exists now? Whether it is the idolatrous jahiliyyah, the mixed jahiliyyah of the People of the Book, or the modern jahiliyyah of atheism and heresy. Furthermore, if by adopting a policy of give-and-take within the Islamic system, the very distinction between it and the systems established by the People of the Book and others were eliminated, or if a system were brought forth through a fusion and unity of Islam with the jahiliyyah of the modern or ancient age and a compromise were reached upon it, then certainly there would be no difficulties in this path.

This is a decisive separation and distinction. Those who wish to erase these boundaries and continue their efforts under the appealing banner of tolerance and "rapprochement between the heavenly religions" are following a most mistaken path. These people have understood neither the meaning of "religions" nor the meaning of "tolerance" (tasamuh) and forbearance. Let it be remembered that tolerance exists only in personal and individual matters. Within the Islamic beliefs and concepts and the structure of the Islamic social system, no tolerance is possible. These people actually want to shake the conviction that exists among Muslims. Allah does not accept any religion other than Islam, and it is obligatory upon every Muslim to strive for the establishment of the religion and not to accept any alternative religion against Islam, nor to accept any change or amendment in it, even if that amendment is extremely minor. The Qur'an repeatedly seeks to instill this conviction in the heart and mind of a believer. Allah, the Exalted, says: (Verse) "Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam" (Surah Al 'Imran 3:19). (Verse) "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, never will it be accepted from him" (Surah Al 'Imran 3:85). (Verse) "And beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you" (5:49). (Verse) "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them is then one of them" (5:51).

The Qur'an presents a glimpse of the situation that existed at the time, and because of which these verses of the Qur'an were revealed:

(Verse) "So you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening toward them, saying, 'We fear that a misfortune may befall us'" (5:52). You see that those in whose hearts is the disease of hypocrisy run about among them, saying, "We fear lest a calamity overtake us."

Ibn Jarir narrated, through his chain, this report of Ibn Sa'd. He said: 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who was from the descendants of al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! I have countless friends among the Jews, and I disassociate myself from the friendship of the Jews and adopt the friendship of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ)." Upon this, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites, said: "I am a man who fears various misfortunes. I do not declare disassociation from my allies and friends."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abdullah ibn Ubayy mentioned above: "Abu al-Habbab, you had a rivalry with 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit regarding friendship with the Jews, so now accept that friendship too." Upon this the chief of the hypocrites said, "I accept it." On this occasion these verses were revealed: (Verse) "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies" (5:51).

Ibn Jarir also narrated, with his chain, this report of al-Zuhri: that when the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish friends, "It is appropriate that you accept Islam before a day like the day of the people of Badr comes upon you too." Upon this Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "This matter has deceived you greatly, that you defeated some people of Quraysh who had no knowledge of war. If we had girded ourselves and gathered against you, you would not have had the strength to fight against all of us." Upon this, 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I have friends among the Jews; they are extremely strong people, and they possess a great deal of weapons, and they are very formidable. But I declare disassociation from their friendship and their covenant and alliance. Now I have no friend or ally other than Allah and His Messenger." Upon this Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: "I cannot declare disassociation from the friendship of the Jews. I am a man for whom they are very necessary." Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu al-Habbab, you know that you had a rivalry with 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit because the Jews had more friends than him. Now these friendships are yours." Upon this he too said: "Very well, then I accept."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq writes that the first Jewish tribe that broke the covenant and pact existing between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and themselves was the Banu Qaynuqa'. Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them. These people laid down their arms upon the decision of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Upon this Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul stood up (when these people had fallen under the control of the Prophet (ﷺ)), and said: "O Muhammad (ﷺ), treat my friends well. These people were allies of the Khazraj." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave no answer to him. He said again: "O Muhammad, be gentle with my friends." Upon this the Prophet (ﷺ) again turned away from him. He put his hand into the collar of the Prophet's (ﷺ) coat of mail. Upon this the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Let me go!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became very angry, to the extent that its effect appeared on his face. After this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) again said: "May your ruin come, let me go!" After this he said: "By Allah, I will not let you go until you treat my friends well. Four hundred unarmed men and three hundred armoured men protected me against the red and the black peoples, and you wish to let them go so that you may cut down their harvest in a single morning? I am a man who fears various misfortunes." Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Very well, they are all yours."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated a report of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit: that when the Banu Qaynuqa' fought with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul advanced on their behalf and stood before them, and 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He too was from Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, and he had as many allies among the Banu Qaynuqa' as Abdullah ibn Ubayy had. 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit placed their matter in the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said that he declared disassociation from their friendship, and that now his friend and ally were only Allah and His Messenger, and that he now loved only Allah and His Messenger and declared the end of alliance with the disbelievers. Then Allah revealed this verse concerning 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Abdullah ibn Ubayy: (Verse) "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another... up to... And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies, then indeed the party of Allah will be the victorious" (5:51–56).

Imam Ahmad narrated, through his chain, the report of Usamah ibn Zayd: "I went with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Abdullah ibn Ubayy. He was going to visit him when he was ill. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'I had forbidden you to keep affection for the Jews.' Upon this Abdullah said: 'As'ad ibn Zurarah bore enmity toward them, and he died.'"

These reports clearly explain the circumstances that were in fact present in the Islamic society at that time. This society was opposed to the customs that existed in Madinah before Islam. Moreover, these reports also show that this thinking had not yet reached the decisive stage regarding how relations should or should not be maintained with the Jews scattered around Madinah. Yes, one thing is evident: all these reports concern the Jews, and no such report is mentioned about the Christians. The reason is that the Qur'an wished to give a permanent principle, standard and enduring outlook regarding the nature of relations between Muslims and all other communities, whether they are People of the Book or polytheists, as will be explained in detail when discussing this lesson. Yes, it is correct that there was a considerable difference between the attitude and conduct of the Jews toward Muslims and that of the Christians, and this difference existed in the Prophetic era. And in another place in this surah the Qur'an has also pointed to this matter. Allah, the Exalted, says:

(Verse) "You will surely find the most intense of the people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, 'We are Christians'" (5:82).

Despite the difference that existed at that time, in this verse the Jews and Christians are placed on one level, just as in the following verse the People of the Book and the disbelievers are also placed on one level. This equality is with respect to friendship and wilayah, and it is based on another principle of Islam. That principle is: a Muslim can establish a bond of friendship and alliance only with a Muslim, because every Muslim can establish relations of friendship only with Allah, His Messenger and the Islamic community; and under this principle all groups and sects are equal, even though in other circumstances their positions differ from one another in relation to the Muslims.

Furthermore, it should also be kept in view that in laying down this general and clear-cut principle, Allah, while knowing all eras and times, did not intend this rule only for the age of the Prophet (ﷺ), nor was it for the circumstances that existed at that time. Later events proved that the hostility of the Christians toward the religion of Islam and the Muslim community was no less than that of the Jews in various regions of the world. If we set aside the stance of the Christians of Arabia, who welcomed Islam warmly, then in the rest of the world, especially in Europe, the attitude the Christians adopted toward the people of Islam and the religion of Islam was very bad, or no less than that of the Jews. They showed intense malice toward Islam, plotted against it, and launched wars against it. Consider a land like Abyssinia, whose king of that very period gave refuge to Muslim emigrants and welcomed Islam. Even there, severe persecutions were inflicted upon the people of Islam, which were no less than those of the Jews.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 51–52 (part 3 of 3):

Allah, the Exalted, has knowledge of all eras. For this reason He laid down this general rule for the Muslims. In it He disregarded the circumstances that existed in the first era, because those circumstances were not permanent or lasting. While acting upon this general rule, Islam may also disregard the policies of certain countries whose attitude is not, or will not be, opposed to Islam, until the Last Day.

Until today, a great struggle has been carried on by the Jews and Christians against Islam and against those people who give themselves Muslim names and are described with the attribute of Islam, even though they have no real connection with Islam. This struggle is directed against their own selves and their own religion, and it continues in every part of the world. It also confirms this fact: ﴿Some of them are allies of others﴾. It makes it obligatory upon every intelligent person to take to heart Allah's advice. It is not merely advice, but a definitive prohibition from Allah to act upon: the true servants of Allah may only have friendship with the friends of Allah and with the Messenger of Allah. Whatever camps there may be against Islam and the Muslims, and whichever do not raise the banner of Islam, there shall be no friendly relationship with them, nor any alliance with them. This is Allah's clear decision and definitive command.

Islam guides Muslims to establish their relations with other people solely on the basis of creed and ideology. Within a Muslim's worldview, a covenant of friendship, an alliance, or enmity can exist only on the basis of principles. For this reason, the establishment of a pact of mutual support and assistance (i.e., wilayah, a binding alliance of guardianship and support) between a Muslim and a non-Muslim is not permissible, because between a Muslim and a disbeliever there can be no cooperation or support in the realm of beliefs and concepts. They also cannot unite against atheism, as some simple-minded people among us think. Some Muslims who think along these lines do not even read the Quran, because there is no common ground between the two. So on what basis could they become allies?

Some people who do not study the Quran, and who have no understanding of the reality of Islam, and some who have been deceived, think that all religions are religion, just as atheism is atheism. It is possible that all followers of religion stand together against atheism, because atheism denies religion in general and opposes religiosity as such.

However, according to the Islamic worldview, the matter is not like this, nor does the consciousness of a Muslim who has truly tasted Islam accept it. Only the person who accepts Islam as a way of life can taste Islam. After that, he remains constantly active for this way of life, and his aim is to establish the Islamic system.

For a Muslim of sound thought, it is absolutely clear and definite that in Allah's sight religion is only the Islamic system of life. Allah does not regard any thought or system without Islam as religion, because the phrase Allah has used is: ﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam﴾. ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾. After the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), no religion remains that is acceptable to Allah. Now the whole world must accept Islam, and it must be accepted in the form in which Muhammad (ﷺ) conveyed it to us. The religion of the Christians, which was considered correct before the Prophet (ﷺ), will no longer be acceptable, just as the religion of the Jews was declared unacceptable after the mission of Isa (peace be upon him).

The existence of the Jews and Christians after the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ) does not mean that the religion they follow is acceptable to Allah, or that Allah accepts that they are also upon a divine religion. Certainly their religion was divine, but the situation before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ) and after it is this, and all Muslims acknowledge that now only Islam has the status of religion. The verse mentioned above is a definitive text in this matter, admitting of no interpretation of any kind.

Yes, it is among the established principles that Islam does not force the Jews and Christians, through coercion, to acknowledge the religion of Islam, because the principle is: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾. But this does not mean that the things they practise are religion, or that Allah regards them as a correct religion.

Therefore Islam cannot even think of a front that is a religious front, in which Islam is included and which is fighting against atheism. Religion is only one, and its name is Islam, and all other fronts are non-religious, separate from Islam. Now, whether this non-religious system is originally a divine religion that has been corrupted by deviation, or is an idolatrous religion that maintains its idol-worship, or is atheism that denies all religions outright, and whether they have entered into an alliance among themselves, all these non-religious systems are contrary to the religion of Islam, and no alliance can be established between them and Islam, nor can friendship exist between them.

A Muslim may have dealings with the People of the Book, and Islam requires him to base those dealings on righteousness and kindness, so long as they do not harass him in matters of religion. Islam also permits a Muslim to marry chaste women from among them. However, there is a difference of jurisprudential opinion regarding those among them who regard Isa (peace be upon him) as the son of Allah, and those who believe in the Trinity: whether such women are considered People of the Book and therefore lawful, or whether they are to be regarded as idolaters and therefore forbidden. Nevertheless, even if we take the general principle that marriage is permissible, good treatment or the permissibility of marriage cannot be taken as proof that alliances and friendships in religion can be established with them. Nor does it mean that the religion of the People of the Book is still considered valid by Islam after the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), so that a Muslim and they could then stand together on one front to confront atheism.

Islam came precisely to correct the beliefs of the People of the Book, and it also came to correct the wrong beliefs of idolaters. When the Jews understood that the Prophet (ﷺ) was inviting them too to the religion of Islam, it seemed extremely burdensome to them that the Prophet (ﷺ) should invite them to Islam. The Quran removed this misunderstanding and said that Allah calls them to Islam, and that if they turn away, they too are disbelievers.

A Muslim is obligated to invite the People of the Book to Islam, just as he is obligated to invite idolaters and atheists to the religion of Islam. Yes, if he is not obligated to do so, then it is not that he should forcibly bring these people into Islam, because beliefs do not take root in the heart and mind through coercion and compulsion. "No compulsion in religion" does not only mean that, according to the Quran, it is prohibited. Even if it were not prohibited, it would have no benefit.

It would not be correct for a Muslim, after the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ), to acknowledge that among the People of the Book there is an acceptable religion, and yet still invite them to come to Islam. A Muslim can be obligated only on the basis that he invites them to accept that their religion is not a religion. If he does so, then logically he is not obligated, because that too is a religion and this too is a religion. If this is accepted as a basic premise, then a front between a Muslim and a People of the Book whose aim is to make the religion of Islam dominant would be an illogical front, because they do not even acknowledge the religion of Islam as a religion. In short, in Islam this is a matter of religion and faith, and it is also a matter of logical and natural unity and organisation.

As far as belief and creed are concerned, the matter is entirely clear. We have already discussed this at great length, and above we have proven from Quranic verses that no friendship or alliance can be established between Muslims and the People of the Book.

As for the fact that this is also an administrative and movement-related matter, this too has become clear from the discussion above. Therefore, the entire struggle of a believer will be to implement the Islamic system of life in all the affairs of life, and to implement it with the details that Muhammad (ﷺ) has explained, in all its aspects and dimensions. In the arena of all the affairs of life, how can a Muslim be united with and walk alongside a person who does not regard Islam as religion at all, who does not regard the Islamic Shariah as a law, and whose goals and objectives are different? Although these goals and objectives may not be opposed to Islam, they are not the goals of Islam either, because Islam does not accept any goal or any action unless it is founded upon Islamic belief.

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day﴾ (14:18).

Islam imposes the duty upon a Muslim that he should direct his struggle solely for Islam. In the struggle of night and day, no part of his life should be given to anything that does not understand the nature of Islam or the religion of Islam. It cannot be imagined that a part of a Muslim's life could lie outside Islam, in which he cooperates with those who are enemies of Islam, enemies who could only be pleased with Muslims if they renounce Islam. It should be remembered that the Quran has given clear and explicit instructions on this point: that the Jews and Christians will never be pleased with you until you adopt their religion and community. Thus this unity is impossible both on the level of belief and ideology, just as it is not possible in practice.

Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul made an excuse (he was among those in whose hearts there was a disease), and went further by establishing friendship and alliance with the Jews. He said that he could not break his alliance with the Jews, because he was a man who feared turns of fortune, meaning that he feared circumstances might arise in which he himself would face hardship. This excuse shows that there was a disease in his heart and that he was weak in faith, because the true protector and helper is only Allah. The Helper is only Allah. Seeking support from anyone other than Allah is misguidance. If someone seeks it, his action is futile and will yield no benefit. But the argument and excuse of Ibn Ubayy is the excuse of every person who, in any era, plays the role of Ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Its outlook is also the outlook of every hypocrite who has a diseased heart and who has not attained the reality of faith.

On the other hand, the heart of Ubadah ibn al-Samit was filled with disgust at Jewish friendship when he saw that these people were treacherous, because he himself was a true believer. He terminated the Jewish friendships and alliances. Whereas Abdullah ibn Ubayy received those pacts eagerly, embraced them, and held them firmly in his teeth, because he was a hypocrite.

These are two methods and two patterns of conduct, which arose from two different beliefs and concepts. Beneath these two, two different consciousnesses were at work, and this very difference will continue until the Day of Resurrection between two different patterns of conduct. One will be a believing heart, and the other will be a heart that has not recognised faith.

Those who establish friendly relations with such enemies of the religion, and gather with them, who are hypocrites, whose outlook, friendships, and trust are not sincere for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, Allah admonishes them with great severity: either victory will be granted to the people of Islam by Allah, or some other matter will be made manifest that will be decisive, and thus their hypocrisy will be revealed. And then they will be deeply ashamed.

﴿So perhaps Allah will bring the victory or a command from Him, and they will become regretful for what they had concealed within themselves﴾ (5:52).

﴿It may be that Allah will bring a decisive victory or a command from Him, and then they will regret the hypocrisy they have kept hidden in their hearts.﴾

At that time, that is, close to complete victory, as with the conquest of Makkah, or at the time of the decision between truth and falsehood through some other means, and at the arrival of the command of Allah, those whose hearts have the disease of hypocrisy will be extremely ashamed, that they hastened and entered into friendship and alliance pacts with the Jews and Christians. They were practising hypocrisy, and now their secret has been exposed. In such circumstances, the believers will then be astonished at the state of the hypocrites, how these people kept hypocrisy in their hearts, and how now these people are in such a loss.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Ma'idah, verses 51–52 (part 1 of 3):

Verses 51 to 53.

It seems appropriate here to define the concept of walayah (alliance and close friendship) and rafaqah (companionship), from which Allah strictly forbids the believers, saying that there should be no companionship with the Jews and Christians.

The meaning of this companionship is that there should be no treaty of alliance, mutual cooperation and mutual support with the Jews and Christians. It does not mean that you follow their religion. This is because it is not even possible to imagine that there could be a Muslim who follows the religion of the Jews and Christians. In reality, this was a friendship of mutual alliance and cooperation, concerning which the minds of Muslims at that time were not clear that it was also prohibited. Muslims thought that such alliances and cooperation were still permissible. This confusion arose because before Islam, treaties of friendship existed among these people, and such things also used to happen in the early days of Islam, especially in the early days of Madinah. Through these texts, Allah prohibited this and declared such treaties void. Especially since the Jews did not act upon the agreement made between Muslims and Jews according to the Charter of Madinah, and it became clear from this that a treaty between the people of Islam and them was no longer possible.

This meaning and implication is clearly evident from the expressions of the Quran. (See regarding the Muslims of Madinah and those Muslims who were still in Makkah and had not migrated: ﴿Mā lakum min walāyatihim min shay'in ḥattā yuhājirū﴾, meaning, there is no friendship and companionship between you and them until they migrate.) It is clear that by this walayah is not meant walayah fi al-din, that is, Islamic brotherhood. Here walayah means that friendship in which, by way of a treaty, mutual support and cooperation are pledged. This treaty cannot even be made with those who, although Muslims, have not yet migrated to the abode of Islam. This is the very kind that these verses prohibit the people of Islam from, that they should not make such friendship with the Jews and Christians, whereas in the early days of Madinah this bond was established.

Dealing with the People of the Book with tolerance is one thing, and making them your friends through treaties of friendship is another. But the people of Islam, in their minds, have not yet grasped the reality of the religion, and have not yet understood the duties and functions of the religion, that religion is an organized and realistic methodology. It remains in constant movement, and its purpose is to create a real situation on this earth that conforms to the Islamic conception of life. This conception of life differs from all the concepts that have been introduced among humanity. Thus, this Islamic situation then clashes with all the concepts and situations that are opposed to it. Furthermore, it also clashes with people's desires, with their sinfulness and their deviations, and this system also enters into such a struggle that there is no escape from it. This clash occurs because the Islamic system creates a new situation, and it continually moves positively towards its goal.

Those people in whose consciousness and feeling this aspect of the Islamic worldview is not clear, and in whose consciousness the great confrontation between Islam and other sects and creeds is not well understood, and who are heedless of these clear Quranic guidances, they do not distinguish between those guidances in which tolerance towards the People of the Book living in an Islamic society is commanded and all their rights are protected, and those treaties concerning alliance and mutual support, according to which walayah and friendship can be only with Allah, His Messenger and the Muslim community. They forget that when a confrontation arises between Islam and the People of the Book, the People of the Book and all other disbelievers are allies of one another, and this is their permanent policy and characteristic. They bear enmity towards Muslims merely because of their Islam, and they will never be pleased with any Muslim until he abandons his religion and adopts obedience to their religion. This is why all the People of the Book are constantly at war against Islam and Islamic communities. Yet sometimes this statement slips from their mouths, and what is hidden in their hearts is far greater. This and other such matters.

A Muslim has been guided in any case to adopt a tolerant attitude towards the People of the Book. But he has been prevented from making a treaty of friendship with them, that is, mutual support and allied friendship. The path on which he must walk in order to establish the religion and make it dominant over the world is very far from the path of the People of the Book, even if they display great tolerance and affection. This is because they will never be pleased that Muslims remain upon their religion and implement the Islamic system, and this tolerance will not stop them from uniting to fight against Islam. They always do so.

It would be a great naivety and a great heedlessness if we were to think that the path to the dominance of religion for us is the same path on which the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, are walking, and that by walking on that path we will confront the disbelievers and atheists, whereas the disbelievers and atheists nowadays are most of all these People of the Book. Thus, the confrontation now too is between Muslims and the People of the Book.

Among us, those simple-minded people do not grasp this whole reality, and in every age there have been Muslims who believe that Muslims and the People of the Book can together wage war against atheism and materialism, because the People of the Book too are people of religion and we too are people of religion. But these simple-minded people forget all the teachings of the Holy Quran, indeed they forget the entire Islamic history. The People of the Book are those very people who used to say to the polytheists and atheists: ﴿Hā'ulā'i ahdā min alladhīna āmanū sabīlā﴾ (These polytheists are more guided on the path than those who have believed). And it was the People of the Book who gathered the factions against the Muslims and marched upon Madinah. They used to give protection to all the factions. It was the People of the Book who waged the Crusades against Islam for two hundred years, and it was these same People of the Book who committed unimaginable crimes against Muslims in Andalusia. It is these People of the Book who recently expelled Arab Muslims from Palestine and settled Jews in their place, and in this matter they continued to cooperate with all atheists and heretics. It is these People of the Book who are expelling Muslims from every place: in Abyssinia, in Somalia, in Eritrea and in Algeria; in short, everywhere they are cooperating with atheists, polytheists and idol-worshippers in this expulsion and this oppression. In Yugoslavia, China, Turkestan and India, and everywhere, they are supporters of the enemies of Islam.

After these complete and comprehensive guidances and decisions of the Holy Quran, there still arise among us people who say that there can be cooperation and friendship between Muslims and these People of the Book against atheistic materialism. Such people have in reality not studied the Holy Quran well, and if they have studied it, then there has occurred a confusion in their minds between the Islamic concept of religious tolerance and the concept of walayah and friendship.

These are the kinds of people in whose consciousness Islam does not hold the status that Islam is a worldview which does not accept any other worldview from people. Nor is it in their minds that Islam is a positive movement which wants to completely change the situation of this world, and that the People of the Book have always blocked the path of Islam, just as they are standing blocking the path of Islam even today. And this is the position of the People of the Book which never changes, because it is for them the only natural position.

We leave these people in their very position, to remain heedless or feigning heedlessness, and we ourselves reflect upon the guidances of Allah, which are entirely clear and explicit.

﴿Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū lā tattakhidhū al-yahūda wa al-naṣārā awliyā'a ba'ḍuhum awliyā'u ba'ḍin wa man yatawallahum minkum fa-innahu minhum inna Allāha lā yahdī al-qawma al-ẓālimīn﴾ (51)

"O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."

This address is directed to the Muslim community working in the city of Madinah, but these same guidances are also for all the communities that work anywhere on this earth, and these same guidances will remain until the Day of Resurrection, for all those upon whom this title is rightly applied, ﴿Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū﴾. The need for these guidances arose at the time of the revelation of the Quran, and these guidances were given to the believers because at that time there was no complete severance between Muslims and the Jews living around Madinah. Alliance and allied relations of walayah still remained among them. Economic and other dealings took place with one another, and relations of neighbourhood and companionship also existed between the two. This situation was the natural result of the historical and economic conditions of Madinah, because there were relations between the Arabs and the Jews there. Due to these circumstances, the Jews were getting the opportunity to conspire against the Muslims and to continue their activities against the religion of Islam. These conspiracies are of various kinds, and their full details have been given in the commentary of the previous five parts, and in this section too some aspects of that conspiracy have been taken up.

The revelation of the Quran continued solely for the purpose that the Muslim's thinking and, to the necessary extent, his consciousness regarding the struggle that confronts him in this world concerning his creed and worldview, and the goal of establishing the religion in view of it, should become firm.
