Furthermore, there should be a complete chasm between the Muslim consciousness and all those people and forces that block this religion and its system, and who in no way wish to come under the Islamic banner. Yes, it is another matter that moral tolerance or social boycott does not fall within the scope of this complete boycott. Moral conduct and social relations are, in any case, qualities of a good Muslim, which are never separated from him at any time. Yes, in these guidances, friendship and allied relations with them are prohibited, which can only be with Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and this is the consciousness of separation that should exist within a Muslim everywhere, in every age and in every generation. Reflect carefully upon the words of the Quran.

"O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them, then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."

These people are allies of one another themselves. This is a reality which is beyond the bounds of time and place, because this reality is a natural reality and it is the demand of their temperament. These people have never become friends of the believers in any place or in any era. Centuries have passed, and not a single example of their friendship has come to light, and this statement of Allah has remained true. Even in the war against the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), the People of the Book were united among themselves. After him, they have remained united in enmity against every Islamic community, and throughout the long chain of history they have remained united against Islam across the entire globe. Not once has this rule admitted an exception, and in the world there has always been what the Holy Quran has used here as a description of the People of the Book. The Holy Quran did not describe this attribute of theirs in connection with scattered incidents. The manner in which the Quran has used this nominal sentence here: ﴿Ba'ḍuhum awliyā'u ba'ḍin﴾ (5:51). This is not merely a mode of expression, but rather it is intended to show that this mutual walayah and friendship is their permanent attribute.

After this, the Quran draws the natural consequences of this reality. When the Jews and Christians are only friends of one another, then any Muslim who makes friends with them will be counted among them. Whoever among the ranks of Islam is their friend will remain in the Islamic ranks? He in practice negates the attribute "Islamic" from himself. He in practice wraps upon himself the attribute of Judaism and Christianity. Yet this is a natural result: ﴿Wa man yatawallahum minkum fa-innahu minhum﴾ (5:51) (And whoever among you allies with them, then indeed he is one of them).

Such a person wrongs himself and wrongs his religion, because he has given his love to them. Then Allah does not guide such a person, nor does He accept him back into the Islamic ranks: ﴿Inna Allāha lā yahdī al-qawma al-ẓālimīn﴾ (5:51) (Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people).

This is a translation of the Urdu passage, following the rules you set (quotations of the Qur'an in ﴿ ﴾, transliteration of technical terms with glosses on first mention, honorifics as (ﷺ)).

The community of Madinah was faced with an extremely frightening warning. This warning, though severe, is entirely natural, and there is no artificial harshness in it. Therefore whoever commits this prohibited act is one of them; had he not been one of them, a Muslim could never under any circumstances become a wali (protector) and friend of the Jews and Christians. Nor can such a person remain a member of the ranks of Islam, because the friendship and alliance of the members of any Islamic community is exclusively with Allah, His Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers. This is a crossroads and a point that demands a decision.

In the matter of complete separation between a Muslim and the opponents of the Islamic system and the advocates of other systems, no leniency can be adopted. One has raised the flag of Islam, and the other has raised a flag opposed to Islam. If he (the Muslim) does so, he will not be able to establish the unique system of Islam on this earth, nor will he be able to show any noteworthy activity in this regard.

When a Muslim has the firm conviction that his religion is the only religion that Allah will accept from people, then within that conviction there remains no flaw and no leniency. He also believes that after the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) there is no further prophethood, and that this Islamic way of life is the unique system which he must establish in people's lives, and that no system of the world is viable in comparison to it. The life of humanity on this earth cannot be set right until Muslims establish this system; and that Allah will not forgive him if he does not exert his full strength in the path of the establishment and dominance of this religion. The truth is that Allah does not accept any other system as a substitute for this system, rather He does not accept any substitute for any part of the Islamic system. And that until he purifies the Islamic beliefs and concepts, removing every error and admixture from among them, and until he removes all admixtures from the detailed system and legal matters, Islam cannot attain dominance, except where Allah has preserved something from the earlier shariahs. In short, until a believer is completely single-minded and holds firm conviction in all these matters, he cannot bear this burden, nor can he practically establish the way of life whose heavy duty Allah has placed upon his shoulders.

The truth is that the obligation of establishing the religion (iqamat-e-deen) is a difficult duty. Its path has severe difficulties, and the responsibilities of this path are back-breaking. On this path sit spiteful enemies, hidden snares are laid, and there are places of grief and sorrow which at times become unbearable. If this were not the case, then what hardship would there be in the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) that exists now? Whether it is the idolatrous jahiliyyah, the mixed jahiliyyah of the People of the Book, or the modern jahiliyyah of atheism and heresy. Furthermore, if by adopting a policy of give-and-take within the Islamic system, the very distinction between it and the systems established by the People of the Book and others were eliminated, or if a system were brought forth through a fusion and unity of Islam with the jahiliyyah of the modern or ancient age and a compromise were reached upon it, then certainly there would be no difficulties in this path.

This is a decisive separation and distinction. Those who wish to erase these boundaries and continue their efforts under the appealing banner of tolerance and "rapprochement between the heavenly religions" are following a most mistaken path. These people have understood neither the meaning of "religions" nor the meaning of "tolerance" (tasamuh) and forbearance. Let it be remembered that tolerance exists only in personal and individual matters. Within the Islamic beliefs and concepts and the structure of the Islamic social system, no tolerance is possible. These people actually want to shake the conviction that exists among Muslims. Allah does not accept any religion other than Islam, and it is obligatory upon every Muslim to strive for the establishment of the religion and not to accept any alternative religion against Islam, nor to accept any change or amendment in it, even if that amendment is extremely minor. The Qur'an repeatedly seeks to instill this conviction in the heart and mind of a believer. Allah, the Exalted, says: (Verse) "Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam" (Surah Al 'Imran 3:19). (Verse) "And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, never will it be accepted from him" (Surah Al 'Imran 3:85). (Verse) "And beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you" (5:49). (Verse) "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. And whoever among you allies with them is then one of them" (5:51).

The Qur'an presents a glimpse of the situation that existed at the time, and because of which these verses of the Qur'an were revealed:

(Verse) "So you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening toward them, saying, 'We fear that a misfortune may befall us'" (5:52). You see that those in whose hearts is the disease of hypocrisy run about among them, saying, "We fear lest a calamity overtake us."

Ibn Jarir narrated, through his chain, this report of Ibn Sa'd. He said: 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who was from the descendants of al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah! I have countless friends among the Jews, and I disassociate myself from the friendship of the Jews and adopt the friendship of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ)." Upon this, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the chief of the hypocrites, said: "I am a man who fears various misfortunes. I do not declare disassociation from my allies and friends."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abdullah ibn Ubayy mentioned above: "Abu al-Habbab, you had a rivalry with 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit regarding friendship with the Jews, so now accept that friendship too." Upon this the chief of the hypocrites said, "I accept it." On this occasion these verses were revealed: (Verse) "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies" (5:51).

Ibn Jarir also narrated, with his chain, this report of al-Zuhri: that when the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish friends, "It is appropriate that you accept Islam before a day like the day of the people of Badr comes upon you too." Upon this Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "This matter has deceived you greatly, that you defeated some people of Quraysh who had no knowledge of war. If we had girded ourselves and gathered against you, you would not have had the strength to fight against all of us." Upon this, 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I have friends among the Jews; they are extremely strong people, and they possess a great deal of weapons, and they are very formidable. But I declare disassociation from their friendship and their covenant and alliance. Now I have no friend or ally other than Allah and His Messenger." Upon this Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: "I cannot declare disassociation from the friendship of the Jews. I am a man for whom they are very necessary." Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu al-Habbab, you know that you had a rivalry with 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit because the Jews had more friends than him. Now these friendships are yours." Upon this he too said: "Very well, then I accept."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq writes that the first Jewish tribe that broke the covenant and pact existing between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and themselves was the Banu Qaynuqa'. Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them. These people laid down their arms upon the decision of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Upon this Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul stood up (when these people had fallen under the control of the Prophet (ﷺ)), and said: "O Muhammad (ﷺ), treat my friends well. These people were allies of the Khazraj." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave no answer to him. He said again: "O Muhammad, be gentle with my friends." Upon this the Prophet (ﷺ) again turned away from him. He put his hand into the collar of the Prophet's (ﷺ) coat of mail. Upon this the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Let me go!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became very angry, to the extent that its effect appeared on his face. After this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) again said: "May your ruin come, let me go!" After this he said: "By Allah, I will not let you go until you treat my friends well. Four hundred unarmed men and three hundred armoured men protected me against the red and the black peoples, and you wish to let them go so that you may cut down their harvest in a single morning? I am a man who fears various misfortunes." Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Very well, they are all yours."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated a report of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit: that when the Banu Qaynuqa' fought with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul advanced on their behalf and stood before them, and 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He too was from Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, and he had as many allies among the Banu Qaynuqa' as Abdullah ibn Ubayy had. 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit placed their matter in the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said that he declared disassociation from their friendship, and that now his friend and ally were only Allah and His Messenger, and that he now loved only Allah and His Messenger and declared the end of alliance with the disbelievers. Then Allah revealed this verse concerning 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Abdullah ibn Ubayy: (Verse) "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another... up to... And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies, then indeed the party of Allah will be the victorious" (5:51–56).

Imam Ahmad narrated, through his chain, the report of Usamah ibn Zayd: "I went with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Abdullah ibn Ubayy. He was going to visit him when he was ill. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'I had forbidden you to keep affection for the Jews.' Upon this Abdullah said: 'As'ad ibn Zurarah bore enmity toward them, and he died.'"

These reports clearly explain the circumstances that were in fact present in the Islamic society at that time. This society was opposed to the customs that existed in Madinah before Islam. Moreover, these reports also show that this thinking had not yet reached the decisive stage regarding how relations should or should not be maintained with the Jews scattered around Madinah. Yes, one thing is evident: all these reports concern the Jews, and no such report is mentioned about the Christians. The reason is that the Qur'an wished to give a permanent principle, standard and enduring outlook regarding the nature of relations between Muslims and all other communities, whether they are People of the Book or polytheists, as will be explained in detail when discussing this lesson. Yes, it is correct that there was a considerable difference between the attitude and conduct of the Jews toward Muslims and that of the Christians, and this difference existed in the Prophetic era. And in another place in this surah the Qur'an has also pointed to this matter. Allah, the Exalted, says:

(Verse) "You will surely find the most intense of the people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, 'We are Christians'" (5:82).

Despite the difference that existed at that time, in this verse the Jews and Christians are placed on one level, just as in the following verse the People of the Book and the disbelievers are also placed on one level. This equality is with respect to friendship and wilayah, and it is based on another principle of Islam. That principle is: a Muslim can establish a bond of friendship and alliance only with a Muslim, because every Muslim can establish relations of friendship only with Allah, His Messenger and the Islamic community; and under this principle all groups and sects are equal, even though in other circumstances their positions differ from one another in relation to the Muslims.

Furthermore, it should also be kept in view that in laying down this general and clear-cut principle, Allah, while knowing all eras and times, did not intend this rule only for the age of the Prophet (ﷺ), nor was it for the circumstances that existed at that time. Later events proved that the hostility of the Christians toward the religion of Islam and the Muslim community was no less than that of the Jews in various regions of the world. If we set aside the stance of the Christians of Arabia, who welcomed Islam warmly, then in the rest of the world, especially in Europe, the attitude the Christians adopted toward the people of Islam and the religion of Islam was very bad, or no less than that of the Jews. They showed intense malice toward Islam, plotted against it, and launched wars against it. Consider a land like Abyssinia, whose king of that very period gave refuge to Muslim emigrants and welcomed Islam. Even there, severe persecutions were inflicted upon the people of Islam, which were no less than those of the Jews.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 51–52 (part 3 of 3):

Allah, the Exalted, has knowledge of all eras. For this reason He laid down this general rule for the Muslims. In it He disregarded the circumstances that existed in the first era, because those circumstances were not permanent or lasting. While acting upon this general rule, Islam may also disregard the policies of certain countries whose attitude is not, or will not be, opposed to Islam, until the Last Day.

Until today, a great struggle has been carried on by the Jews and Christians against Islam and against those people who give themselves Muslim names and are described with the attribute of Islam, even though they have no real connection with Islam. This struggle is directed against their own selves and their own religion, and it continues in every part of the world. It also confirms this fact: ﴿Some of them are allies of others﴾. It makes it obligatory upon every intelligent person to take to heart Allah's advice. It is not merely advice, but a definitive prohibition from Allah to act upon: the true servants of Allah may only have friendship with the friends of Allah and with the Messenger of Allah. Whatever camps there may be against Islam and the Muslims, and whichever do not raise the banner of Islam, there shall be no friendly relationship with them, nor any alliance with them. This is Allah's clear decision and definitive command.

Islam guides Muslims to establish their relations with other people solely on the basis of creed and ideology. Within a Muslim's worldview, a covenant of friendship, an alliance, or enmity can exist only on the basis of principles. For this reason, the establishment of a pact of mutual support and assistance (i.e., wilayah, a binding alliance of guardianship and support) between a Muslim and a non-Muslim is not permissible, because between a Muslim and a disbeliever there can be no cooperation or support in the realm of beliefs and concepts. They also cannot unite against atheism, as some simple-minded people among us think. Some Muslims who think along these lines do not even read the Quran, because there is no common ground between the two. So on what basis could they become allies?

Some people who do not study the Quran, and who have no understanding of the reality of Islam, and some who have been deceived, think that all religions are religion, just as atheism is atheism. It is possible that all followers of religion stand together against atheism, because atheism denies religion in general and opposes religiosity as such.

However, according to the Islamic worldview, the matter is not like this, nor does the consciousness of a Muslim who has truly tasted Islam accept it. Only the person who accepts Islam as a way of life can taste Islam. After that, he remains constantly active for this way of life, and his aim is to establish the Islamic system.

For a Muslim of sound thought, it is absolutely clear and definite that in Allah's sight religion is only the Islamic system of life. Allah does not regard any thought or system without Islam as religion, because the phrase Allah has used is: ﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam﴾. ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾. After the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), no religion remains that is acceptable to Allah. Now the whole world must accept Islam, and it must be accepted in the form in which Muhammad (ﷺ) conveyed it to us. The religion of the Christians, which was considered correct before the Prophet (ﷺ), will no longer be acceptable, just as the religion of the Jews was declared unacceptable after the mission of Isa (peace be upon him).

The existence of the Jews and Christians after the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ) does not mean that the religion they follow is acceptable to Allah, or that Allah accepts that they are also upon a divine religion. Certainly their religion was divine, but the situation before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ) and after it is this, and all Muslims acknowledge that now only Islam has the status of religion. The verse mentioned above is a definitive text in this matter, admitting of no interpretation of any kind.

Yes, it is among the established principles that Islam does not force the Jews and Christians, through coercion, to acknowledge the religion of Islam, because the principle is: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾. But this does not mean that the things they practise are religion, or that Allah regards them as a correct religion.

Therefore Islam cannot even think of a front that is a religious front, in which Islam is included and which is fighting against atheism. Religion is only one, and its name is Islam, and all other fronts are non-religious, separate from Islam. Now, whether this non-religious system is originally a divine religion that has been corrupted by deviation, or is an idolatrous religion that maintains its idol-worship, or is atheism that denies all religions outright, and whether they have entered into an alliance among themselves, all these non-religious systems are contrary to the religion of Islam, and no alliance can be established between them and Islam, nor can friendship exist between them.

A Muslim may have dealings with the People of the Book, and Islam requires him to base those dealings on righteousness and kindness, so long as they do not harass him in matters of religion. Islam also permits a Muslim to marry chaste women from among them. However, there is a difference of jurisprudential opinion regarding those among them who regard Isa (peace be upon him) as the son of Allah, and those who believe in the Trinity: whether such women are considered People of the Book and therefore lawful, or whether they are to be regarded as idolaters and therefore forbidden. Nevertheless, even if we take the general principle that marriage is permissible, good treatment or the permissibility of marriage cannot be taken as proof that alliances and friendships in religion can be established with them. Nor does it mean that the religion of the People of the Book is still considered valid by Islam after the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), so that a Muslim and they could then stand together on one front to confront atheism.

Islam came precisely to correct the beliefs of the People of the Book, and it also came to correct the wrong beliefs of idolaters. When the Jews understood that the Prophet (ﷺ) was inviting them too to the religion of Islam, it seemed extremely burdensome to them that the Prophet (ﷺ) should invite them to Islam. The Quran removed this misunderstanding and said that Allah calls them to Islam, and that if they turn away, they too are disbelievers.

A Muslim is obligated to invite the People of the Book to Islam, just as he is obligated to invite idolaters and atheists to the religion of Islam. Yes, if he is not obligated to do so, then it is not that he should forcibly bring these people into Islam, because beliefs do not take root in the heart and mind through coercion and compulsion. "No compulsion in religion" does not only mean that, according to the Quran, it is prohibited. Even if it were not prohibited, it would have no benefit.

It would not be correct for a Muslim, after the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ), to acknowledge that among the People of the Book there is an acceptable religion, and yet still invite them to come to Islam. A Muslim can be obligated only on the basis that he invites them to accept that their religion is not a religion. If he does so, then logically he is not obligated, because that too is a religion and this too is a religion. If this is accepted as a basic premise, then a front between a Muslim and a People of the Book whose aim is to make the religion of Islam dominant would be an illogical front, because they do not even acknowledge the religion of Islam as a religion. In short, in Islam this is a matter of religion and faith, and it is also a matter of logical and natural unity and organisation.

As far as belief and creed are concerned, the matter is entirely clear. We have already discussed this at great length, and above we have proven from Quranic verses that no friendship or alliance can be established between Muslims and the People of the Book.

As for the fact that this is also an administrative and movement-related matter, this too has become clear from the discussion above. Therefore, the entire struggle of a believer will be to implement the Islamic system of life in all the affairs of life, and to implement it with the details that Muhammad (ﷺ) has explained, in all its aspects and dimensions. In the arena of all the affairs of life, how can a Muslim be united with and walk alongside a person who does not regard Islam as religion at all, who does not regard the Islamic Shariah as a law, and whose goals and objectives are different? Although these goals and objectives may not be opposed to Islam, they are not the goals of Islam either, because Islam does not accept any goal or any action unless it is founded upon Islamic belief.

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day﴾ (14:18).

Islam imposes the duty upon a Muslim that he should direct his struggle solely for Islam. In the struggle of night and day, no part of his life should be given to anything that does not understand the nature of Islam or the religion of Islam. It cannot be imagined that a part of a Muslim's life could lie outside Islam, in which he cooperates with those who are enemies of Islam, enemies who could only be pleased with Muslims if they renounce Islam. It should be remembered that the Quran has given clear and explicit instructions on this point: that the Jews and Christians will never be pleased with you until you adopt their religion and community. Thus this unity is impossible both on the level of belief and ideology, just as it is not possible in practice.

Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul made an excuse (he was among those in whose hearts there was a disease), and went further by establishing friendship and alliance with the Jews. He said that he could not break his alliance with the Jews, because he was a man who feared turns of fortune, meaning that he feared circumstances might arise in which he himself would face hardship. This excuse shows that there was a disease in his heart and that he was weak in faith, because the true protector and helper is only Allah. The Helper is only Allah. Seeking support from anyone other than Allah is misguidance. If someone seeks it, his action is futile and will yield no benefit. But the argument and excuse of Ibn Ubayy is the excuse of every person who, in any era, plays the role of Ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Its outlook is also the outlook of every hypocrite who has a diseased heart and who has not attained the reality of faith.

On the other hand, the heart of Ubadah ibn al-Samit was filled with disgust at Jewish friendship when he saw that these people were treacherous, because he himself was a true believer. He terminated the Jewish friendships and alliances. Whereas Abdullah ibn Ubayy received those pacts eagerly, embraced them, and held them firmly in his teeth, because he was a hypocrite.

These are two methods and two patterns of conduct, which arose from two different beliefs and concepts. Beneath these two, two different consciousnesses were at work, and this very difference will continue until the Day of Resurrection between two different patterns of conduct. One will be a believing heart, and the other will be a heart that has not recognised faith.

Those who establish friendly relations with such enemies of the religion, and gather with them, who are hypocrites, whose outlook, friendships, and trust are not sincere for the sake of Allah and His Messenger, Allah admonishes them with great severity: either victory will be granted to the people of Islam by Allah, or some other matter will be made manifest that will be decisive, and thus their hypocrisy will be revealed. And then they will be deeply ashamed.

﴿So perhaps Allah will bring the victory or a command from Him, and they will become regretful for what they had concealed within themselves﴾ (5:52).

﴿It may be that Allah will bring a decisive victory or a command from Him, and then they will regret the hypocrisy they have kept hidden in their hearts.﴾

At that time, that is, close to complete victory, as with the conquest of Makkah, or at the time of the decision between truth and falsehood through some other means, and at the arrival of the command of Allah, those whose hearts have the disease of hypocrisy will be extremely ashamed, that they hastened and entered into friendship and alliance pacts with the Jews and Christians. They were practising hypocrisy, and now their secret has been exposed. In such circumstances, the believers will then be astonished at the state of the hypocrites, how these people kept hypocrisy in their hearts, and how now these people are in such a loss.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 53:

(Verse) "And those who believe will say, 'Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that they were with you?' Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers."

And the believers will say: "Are these the same people who swore by Allah with their most solemn oaths, assuring you that they were with you?" Their deeds have been rendered void, and in the end they have become failed and disappointed.

Then a day came when victory was granted. The secret intentions of many people were exposed, their deeds were rendered void, and several groups remained in severe loss. And even today we await the promise of Allah that victory will come, on condition that we hold firmly to the rope of Allah. On condition that our friendship is with Allah alone; on condition that we understand the Islamic system and build our thoughts and our actions in accordance with it; on condition that we enter the battle under the guidance and direction of Allah, and that we take none as friends except Allah and His Messenger.

The first call to the believers was that they should refrain from friendship with the Jews and Christians and from forming allied relations with them, otherwise they should remember that they too would be counted among them, and thus they would apostatise from Islam. They will not even realise what they have become, entirely unintentionally. Now here a second call is given to them: beware, lest any of them apostatise. This apostasy may come through that friendship, and it may also come through other causes. If they apostatise, they will have no standing with Allah. And let it also be noted that their apostasy and turning back neither can compel Allah nor can it harm the religion of Allah. Allah's religion may have many other friends and supporters who are known to Allah. If all the Muslims were to turn back, then those people would come forward. And here some of the features of those people, who are known to Allah and are in reserve, and who will be the supporters and helpers of His religion, are also described; and these features are extremely pleasing, attractive, beautiful and radiant. And the direction (qiblah) is also shown toward which a Muslim will turn his friendship and love. And in this second call the ultimate outcome of this battle, which is ongoing among the Party of Allah and all other parties, is also mentioned. Only those people, and none but they, will reach that outcome whose love is solely for Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 5, verse 54 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 54 to 56.

In this context, the warning to Muslims not to apostatise indicates a deep connection between apostasy and taking the People of the Book and the Christians as allies (muwalat). This is especially so after the remark that whoever establishes a bond of love and alliance with them will be counted among them. Such a person is regarded as outside the community of Muslims, and is considered to be one of them. (Verse) "And whoever among you takes them as allies, then he is indeed one of them" (5:51). In light of this meaning, this second call is a confirmation and reinforcement of the first. The third call that follows also points to this same meaning, because there the prohibition of alliance with both the People of the Book and the disbelievers is mentioned together, placing them in one row: the status of alliance with the People of the Book is the same as with the disbelievers. Likewise, the distinctions that Islam makes in some dealings between the People of the Book and other disbelievers do not apply to the guidance on alliance; alliance is not included in them.

(Verse) "O you who have believed, whoever of you apostatises from his religion - Allah will bring forth a people He will love and who will love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty over the disbelievers, striving in the cause of Allah and not fearing the blame of a critic. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing" (5:54).

Assigning a particular group and community to the work of Allah is the fulfilment of Allah's will. If such a group becomes the instrument of His power on this earth for the establishment of the religion of Allah, and through it the rule of Allah is established over the common people, the commands and guidance of Allah are enforced in their lives, their administration conforms to them, the Islamic Shariah is enforced in their courts, and goodness, virtue, purity and progress prevail, and the world attains this through the Islamic system, then the selection and appointment of this group to this task is itself a great bounty and grace of Allah the Exalted. Now, if someone deprives himself of this bounty and grace of Allah, it will be his own misfortune. Allah the Exalted is the Self-Sufficient King, and apart from those who are deprived, there are people in Allah's knowledge who deserve this bounty and grace.

Here, the portrait that Allah the Exalted draws of these chosen servants of His has very clear features, and their qualities are also described very clearly. This portrait is extremely bright and attractive.

(Verse) "Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him" (5:54). That is, the bond and relationship between them and their Lord will be the gift of love in exchange. What is love? It is a spirit, extremely subtle, luminous, radiant and exceedingly cheerful, which serves as the link between that people and Allah the Exalted.

Allah the Exalted loves His servants. This is a matter whose worth can be realised only by the person who has been granted divine knowledge and who has been characterised by the qualities that Allah Himself has described. Likewise, only the person upon whose senses, consciousness and self and personality the imprint of these qualities has fallen can conceive of it. This bounty and grace can enter the comprehension only of the person who knows the reality of that Giver, who knows who Allah is, who is the owner and creator of this great universe, and who is also the Creator of this small insect, man, who lives under the authority of the One of exceedingly lofty greatness, and who serves Him who is purely His and is in His kingdom. And who is that Being, and what is this human being upon whom that Being bestows grace and bounty, and with whom He has love, although man is himself made by Him? He is Pure, Majestic in worth, Exalted in rank, the Living, the Everlasting, the Most High, the Eternal, the First, the Last, and the Outward and the Inward.

A servant's love for his Allah is a blessing for that servant, and only the person who has a taste for it can understand it. And Allah's love for a servant is indeed a great matter, and surely a great, complete and abundant grace. Similarly, Allah's guidance of His servants and His praise of them is also a very great honour. That such a beautiful disposition should arise within them, and such a love be born in them as has no parallel in the loves of this world, is also a great reward and a great grace and bounty.

Just as Allah's love for the servant is beyond expression, so too the servant's love for Allah is beyond expression. It cannot be made manifest in the speech of worldly lovers or in acts of worship. And in this field, among the Sufis, it is those who have attained union with Allah (wasil billah) who hold the superior rank. But among those who wear the garb of Sufis, the armies of so-called Sufis that are seen roaming about and are well known among the masses, very few such people who have attained union with Allah will be seen. In this connection, some verses of Rabi'a al-Adawiyya come to the screen of my mind. She says:

"Would that you were sweet and life were bitter, and would that you were pleased while all people were angry with me."

"Would that the bond between me and you remained inhabited, and the bond between me and all the worlds were ruined." That is, the relationship and connection.

"When love from you becomes true, then everything is easy, and everything that is above the dust is dust."

Allah the Exalted's manifestation of love toward one servant among His servants in this way, and a humble servant's manifestation of love toward Allah, who is the true Bestower and the true Doer of grace, is a blessing. This love spreads throughout the whole universe, and this love becomes the very nature of every living thing. Then there is an atmosphere and a shade that covers the whole existence of the universe, and man, who is both lover and beloved, his measure of life is entirely filled with that love.

The Islamic conception of life establishes between a believer and his Lord such a beloved bond, which is extremely wondrous and extremely lovely. This bond of lasting love is not such that it is established suddenly, or that a flash appears and then departs. It is a fundamental and real element in the Islamic conception of life. Allah the Exalted says:

(Verse) "Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, the Most Merciful will bring about for them love" (19:96). And elsewhere: (Verse) "Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving" (11:90). And elsewhere: (Verse) "And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near; I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me" (2:186). (Verse) "And those who believe are stronger in love for Allah" (2:165).

And elsewhere: (Verse) "Say, if you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you" (3:31), and so on, and countless other verses express this theme.

It is astonishing that those who recite verses of this theme still say that the Islamic conception of life is a dry, harsh and rough conception, and that in it the relationship between God and the servant is one of wrath, anger, punishment, chastisement, severity and distance. There is no such concept in it, as in the Christian conception where Christ is regarded as one of the hypostases of divinity, and between people and Allah a deep bond arises, indeed the notion of "you are I and I am you."

The truth is that because of the purity of the Islamic conception of life, and its complete distinction between the reality of divinity and the station of servanthood, there is no decrease in the tender atmosphere of affection and love. Between Allah and the servant, in this conception, there is a very deep bond, but this bond and relationship is a relationship of mercy and justice. One aspect of this relationship is mutual love, while the other aspect is complete purity. On one side is love, and on the other side is purity for the Being of Allah. This is an extremely comprehensive and precise conception, and through it all the human requirements that man needs in relation to his Lord are fulfilled.

Accordingly, concerning the attribute of this "believing regiment" which has been raised for this religion, these words appear in this verse and repeatedly come to mind: (Verse) "He loves them and they love Him" (5:54).

In this atmosphere of love, when this regiment goes forth to perform its great duties and bears this burden, there is in its heart the awareness that Allah the Exalted has enlisted it for this special service, and that it is the special regiment of Allah, the Exalted in majesty.

After this, the remaining characteristics of this regiment are stated. (Verse) "Humble toward the believers" (5:54). This is a quality derived from obedience, gentleness and ease, and the wording used is that they will humble themselves before the believers. But if someone humbles his self before the believers, that is not humiliation, nor is there in it any aspect of disgrace, because a believer, in relation to another believer, is extremely gentle, not harsh or disobedient; he is easy and gentle, quick to respond, tolerant and loving. Therefore, in the use of this word for him, there is no meaning of humiliation in the sense of contempt; rather, it expresses brotherhood, love, absence of formality, psychological unity and ideological attachment. Between one believer and another believer no veil or secret remains.

When a person keeps certain things for his own self, this impulse makes him more conspicuous, miserly and stingy toward his other brother. But when a person makes himself a member of a company or regiment, he sacrifices everything for it, and the circle of his individuality becomes limited. Then he keeps nothing for himself apart from that company, whereas their company is the company of Islamic brotherhood, and they have gathered in the name and system of Allah. Allah loves them and they love Allah. Only the love of Allah is shared among them, and they divide it among themselves.

(Verse) "Mighty over the disbelievers" (5:54). That is, toward the disbelievers they possess superiority, displeasure and feelings of superiority, and since the confrontation is with the disbelievers, it is fitting that these feelings be present toward them. The expression of these feelings is not merely for the display of personal honour, nor is it intended merely to raise their own self; rather, their expression of honour will be an expression of honour from the Islamic ideology, the superiority of the banner under which the people of faith stand and face the people of disbelief. It will show that what they possess is good, and that their station is that they should bring others with them and subordinate them to that goodness, not that they should join with others and submit to that thing which others possess and which is not good. This manifestation of superiority and firmness also shows that these people have self-confidence in religion, and that they have overcome the religion of whims and desires. Among them the power of Allah prevails over all other powers, and the community of Allah prevails over all factions. Even if they are defeated in some battles, they still hold high resolve, because in the long path of Islamic striving, slips may also occur.

(Verse) "They will strive in the way of Allah and will not fear the blame of any blamer" (5:54). This striving will be in the way of Allah; it will be for the establishment of the Islamic system on earth; it will be for the proclamation of Allah's sovereignty over people; it will be so that judgments within the country are made according to Islamic Shariah, and that goodness, progress and reform among people prevail within the land. This is the second attribute of the Islamic regiment, and Allah the Exalted has established it solely so that it may carry out on His earth the duty that Allah desires.

This regiment will strive in the way of Allah; it will not strive for its own personal purpose. It will not fight for any purpose of its own people, nor fight for any of its national aims, nor fight for any of its territorial aims, nor work for any race. The members of this regiment will strive only in the way of Allah, and this striving is for the establishment of the Islamic system of life, for the establishment of the government of Allah, and for the enforcement of the Shariah of Allah, and in this path there is the good of all people. In it they have no personal interest, nor any share of their own. This group is for Allah alone, and no one else is a partner in it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 5, verse 54 (part 2 of 2):

This regiment will not heed the blame of any blamer in fighting and dying in the way of Allah. What will it fear from people, and what will it care for? It will be overflowing with the love of Allah, and this love is its guarantor (imam zamin). It will not stop at the places of halt that are customary among people. The values of society will be worthless in its eyes, and what is known (ma'ruf) among the Jahiliyyah will not be known to it. It will be the regiment of the Sunnah of Allah, and it will be the bearer of the Islamic system of life.

It is those who shape their values and guidance according to the desires of people who fear the blame of people, those whose source of strength and power is the masses. But the party whose direction is toward the values and standards of Allah will strive to make the word of truth prevail over the values and standards of the masses, and will act contrary to the desires of people. So why would it fear people? For one whose source of strength and values is the Divine Being, what concern can there be about what people say and do? Such a person will regard it as though people did not exist at all. Whatever the condition of those people may be, whatever their civilization and culture may be, it will continue on its own path.

We see what people say, what people do, what fikr and amal they possess, what terminology they speak in, what their practical life is, and what values and standards they hold. Our attitude is this because we have forgotten the fundamental principle according to which we must set a standard against these considerations, according to which we must correct our accounts, and according to which we must weigh ourselves. That principle is the Islamic system of life, the Islamic Shariah, and the commands of Allah. The truth of the matter is that this is the principle of truth, and everything apart from it is falsehood, even if it is known and current among millions and tens of millions, and even if several generations have accepted it for centuries.

The fact that a situation, a custom, a habit or a value exists, or that it is a fact, or that millions adhere to it, or that millions live their lives in this manner, or that all people accept it as a principle of life, does not constitute its value (value). Islamic conceptions of life do not accept such a standard. Rather, the value of any situation, custom, habit or value is determined by whether it has any worth in the Islamic conception of life or not, because the standard of all values and standards is the Islamic system.

This is why this Islamic regiment will wage jihad in the way of Allah, and it will not fear the blame of any blamer. This is the sign of the believers whom Allah has enlisted in this regiment. And this enlistment too will be done by Allah, and then Allah will have a very deep love for the soldiers of this regiment. This is why Allah is describing the signs of His brave ones, pointing out their addresses... The tranquility that will be in the hearts of these brave ones, and the steadfastness with which they will proceed on the path of jihad, is also the grace and bounty of Allah.

﴿That is the grace of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ (5:54) Now, after the warning, Allah determines who the friendship and loyalty (muwalat) of the believers will be with, and this is explicitly stated.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 55:

(Verse) "Your only Walī (guardian, patron and ally) is Allah, and His Messenger, and those who believe, who establish the Ṣalāh (prayer) and give the Zakāh (obligatory charity), and bow down (in rukūʿ)." (5:55)

Your friends indeed are, in truth, only Allah and His Messenger and the believers, who establish prayer, pay zakah, and are those who bow before Allah.

A decision is given in the exclusive (ḥaṣr) form, in which no room is left for interpretation or whitewashing, and no room is left for melting the Islamic movement or loosening the Islamic conception of life.

No other statement was even possible, because this matter, in its essential nature, is an ideological matter. Then there is the matter of raising a movement on the basis of this ideology, and in it friendship and alliance (muwālāt) must be purely for the sake of Allah, and reliance must be placed on Allah alone, so that religion becomes Islam alone, and there is complete separation between the Islamic ranks and those ranks which do not accept Islam as a religion and do not describe Islam as a way of life. All these clear-cut policies exist so that the Islamic movement may have seriousness and its own system. In it, friendship and loyalty should be for only one leadership, and unity and conviction should exist among the members of one regiment, because this unity is among the group that has been raised upon the foundation of principles.

Now some other attributes of this regiment are enumerated. These are its distinguishing attributes, and they are enumerated so that Islam is not merely a title, not merely a flag and symbol, not merely verbal talk, nor such that it is transmitted from generation to generation like a lineage, nor merely a quality found in good people, but rather that it is a living religion.

(Verse) "Those who establish the prayer, give zakah, and bow down in rukūʿ." One of their attributes is that they establish prayer. They do not merely perform prayer but establish it. The meaning of iqāmat al-ṣalāh is that they perform the prayer fully, and from their prayer those effects appear which Allah has mentioned.

(Verse) "Indeed, prayer forbids indecency and evil" (29:45). The one whose prayer does not restrain him from indecency and wrongdoing has, as it were, not performed the prayer. If he had established the prayer, the prayer would have restrained him from evils.

One of their attributes is that they give zakah, that is, while worshipping Allah they discharge Allah's right from their wealth. This is a kind of financial worship, and it should be paid with heartfelt willingness and consent, because zakah is not merely a tax that is to be paid unwillingly. Zakah is also worship, indeed it is financial worship, and it is a special feature of the Islamic system that through a single command it achieves various objectives. As for systems devised by human beings, they have no such distinction that they fulfil one aspect of the goal while another aspect is entirely absent.

The reform of a society is not achieved merely by taking wealth from people as a tax, or taking wealth from the rich and giving it to the poor, and doing this in the name of the government and the nation, or calling it a levy. In such forms only one objective is achieved: a portion of wealth reaches the needy. But zakah, both in its name and its meaning, expresses purity and growth. On one hand it brings purity to the human conscience, and on the other hand it brings purity to wealth, because it is the worship of Allah, and in it the feelings of the giver towards his poor brothers are full of love. The one who pays zakah is performing an act of worship, and for it he receives reward and recompense on the Day of Resurrection. Moreover, through it there is economic growth in this world too, and blessing and increase in wealth. Furthermore, the poor who receive wealth through it do not have their feelings wounded, because they consider it the grace of Allah that He has set aside a share for them in the wealth of the rich. Thus no enmity and hatred against the rich arises in their hearts. (And it should be kept in mind here that in an Islamic society the rich also earn wealth through lawful means; they do not usurp anyone's right; they gather their own portion.) Finally, through zakah, a financial tax is also imposed in a very pleasant manner, and with the utmost purity, sanctity and growth.

In short, the payment of zakah is the distinguishing sign of those who follow the Sharīʿah. It is their practical affirmation that they acknowledge the sovereignty of Allah and His supreme authority.

(Verse) "And they bow in rukūʿ" (5:55). This is their station and attribute; that is, it is, as it were, a necessary quality of theirs, and their original state is that they are in rukūʿ. For this reason, it was not confined to "yuqīmūn al-ṣalāh" but also "rāki'ūn" was said, because rāki'ūn is, as it were, a unique and most distinguished attribute of theirs. By mentioning this attribute in the active participle form, the impression is given that they constantly do so, and therefore it has been highlighted and stated prominently... In such places there is very deep allusiveness in the expressions of the Qur'an, for one who possesses literary taste.

Now, what is Allah's promise to this regiment? It places its trust in Allah, it supplicates to Allah, it takes Allah as its walī, it is the friend of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers. Then, on the other hand, it has cut ties with all ranks except the Islamic ranks, and has become purely for Allah. What promise is there with it now?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 56:

(Verse) "And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies—then indeed, the party of Allah, they are the ones who will be victorious." (5:55–56)

After stating the principles of faith, Allah promises victory. The foundational principle of faith is that loyalty (muwalat) and friendship should be only for Allah, His Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers. Earlier, it was commanded that if you take the Jews as allies, this would mean that you are considered outside the ranks of the Muslims, your reckoning would be among the Jews and Christians, and in terms of meaning, this act of yours would be apostasy from the religion.

This is a thought-provoking point that recurs repeatedly in the Qur'an: Allah expects a Muslim to regard Islam as absolutely good and to follow it. Not because it will prevail or because he will be granted sovereign authority on earth. Establishment (tamkin) in the land and dominance are signs of faith, and they certainly appear in their time, and they appear so that the decree of Allah may be manifested from behind the veil that He has decreed to make this religion prevail on this earth. This promise of dominance is not given so that people enter the religion relying on this promise. Dominance is not the goal in itself, nor is there any benefit in it for their persons or personalities. It is Allah's decree that appears through the hands of the Muslims from behind the veil of destiny. If dominance is granted to them, it is for their way of life, not for their persons. For them, if there is anything, it is the otherworldly reward for striving on this path, and this otherworldly reward they will also receive for the results of that striving. For example, if religion prevails on the earth, they will receive the reward for all the reformative work done on this earth.

Sometimes Allah promises victory to the Muslims so that they remain steadfast and are freed from the effects of the terrible difficulties that stand before them in frightful form. Some of these difficulties are extremely destructive. When they attain certainty of the outcome, their hearts become strong, and they overcome the difficulties. They traverse the difficult pass and become hopeful that Allah will, through their hands, establish some good for this ummah. They will receive the reward of jihad, the reward of the dominance of religion, and the reward of the consequences that follow from it.

In short, the bringing of this verse at this point shows what the daily life of the community of Muslims was in that period, and that such glad tidings were needed. Accordingly, the decision was given that victory belongs to the party of Allah. This matter indicates the period in which these verses were revealed.

In these circumstances, the summary of all the results is given for us in this brief decision: that the party of Allah will be victorious. A believer becomes content, knowing that this is the sunnah of Allah: that the party of Allah will prevail, even if in some battles it may apparently suffer defeat, because despite some apparent circumstances, Allah's promise is true. Yes, in some stages of the movement, defeat also appears. But the path to the realization of this promise is in any case one: that loyalty be only to Allah, His Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers.

Now let us reflect on the fact that the Qur'an has repeatedly forbidden the believers from forming ties of loyalty with those who oppose the belief of the believers, and has adopted new modes for this, so that this matter becomes part of their awareness and perception, and this principle becomes part of their faith. From this one can gauge how great the importance of this principle is in the Islamic conception of life.

In this connection, when the first call to the believers was issued, it was direct, and in it they were forbidden to form ties of loyalty with the People of the Book. If they did not do so, Allah would bring victory or issue some other command, and in this way all secrets would be exposed. In the second call, they were warned that if they took Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Allah's enemies as allies, they would become apostates; rather, you should be soldiers of a regiment which is Allah's special regiment, which Allah loves and which loves Allah. And this is Allah's party, which will be granted victory.

Now here a third call comes before us. In it the zeal for religion among the believers is aroused: see, these people are not only opposed to your religion and your manner of worship, but they also mock your practices severely. In this third call, Allah forbade them to keep ties of loyalty not only with the People of the Book but also with the other disbelievers, and to adopt an attitude of fear of Allah. If they are believers, let them reflect well upon Allah's instructions. And in this call, He mentions a permanent characteristic of the People of the Book and the disbelievers: that these people lack understanding.

Yes, this situation would be deeply provoking to anyone who has a sense of faith-based honour, and who feels that if his religion is insulted, his worship is insulted, and his way of life and stance are insulted in his presence, then he has no honour or dignity left. Therefore, cutting ties with such people is itself a divine command. How can friendship or a bond of loyalty (*muwalat*) be established between the believers and such people? They commit these acts because there is a defect in their reason and understanding, for it is those whose intellect is unsound who mock the religion of Allah and the way the Muslims worship. When the intellect is healthy and correct, it continually receives the signs of faith from its environment, but when the intellect and understanding are disturbed, it cannot perceive the signs of faith spread around it. Because of this disturbance, the relationship between a person and the universe spread around him is also disturbed, for this entire universe itself bears witness to the fact that Allah alone deserves to be worshipped by man. And if the intellect is healthy and free of any defect, then within it arises the greatness of this universe and the majesty of its Creator. Therefore, no sound and upright intellect can mock the way of worship of the people of Islam.

This mockery of Islamic worship came from the People of the Book, the Jews, as well as from the disbelievers. This ridicule was taking place at the very time when this Qur'an was descending upon the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslim community was receiving it. However, there is no report in the biography of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of any such incident in which the Christians also mocked. But the Qur'an was laying down a permanent principle for the Muslim community; a lasting methodology and a lasting outlook for the life of the Muslims was being formed, and Allah also knew what the turns of time would be. And look how, in later eras, the enemies of the religion and the enemies of the Islamic movement treated this ummah. And this treatment was meted out by those who called themselves Christians, and these people were far more numerous than the Jews. Rather, they were more numerous even when combined with the Jews and other disbelievers. These people rose up against Islam and for centuries carried enmity towards Islam in their hearts. They continued their wars against Islam, and this hostility began from the time when, during the era of Hazrat Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), the Muslims clashed with the Roman Empire, and this clash continued in the form of the Crusades until the time of Salah al-Din Ayyubi. After that, all Western countries gathered together against the Muslim world and from here ended the Islamic Caliphate. After this, Western colonialism emerged, in whose embrace the spirit of the Cross was concealed, and occasionally this would be expressed through the tongue of that colonialism. Under the shadow of this colonialism came Christian missionary activity, and both Christian missionary work and colonialism were intertwined internally. Even today, the Jewish and Christian war continues against those who work anywhere for the revival of Islam and the renaissance of Islam, and in these attacks the Jews, the Christians and all the polytheists are participants as a single united nation.

The Qur'an came because it is a book of guidance for the Muslims and is for until the Day of Resurrection, and this very book shapes the concepts of this ummah. It creates a collective system for the ummah and lays down its movement-oriented guidelines. Therefore, here it established a permanent principle: that no individual of the Muslim ummah should establish a bond of loyalty with anyone other than Allah, the Messenger of Allah and the believers. This principle is placed before them in a negative form, so that they do not establish any bond of loyalty whatsoever with the Jews, the Christians and the disbelievers, and this matter is decided with great firmness and is brought up repeatedly in various ways.

The religion of Islam commands the people of Islam to show tolerance. In general, Islam commands good dealing with the People of the Book. Among the People of the Book, those who call themselves Christians, Islam especially commands tolerance towards them. But Islam also forbids a bond of loyalty with these people, because tolerance, good dealing and good conduct are moral matters, whereas loyalty (*muwalat*) is connected with the outlook on life and organization. A bond of loyalty is in essence a covenant of mutual cooperation, and through it both parties become bound to help and cooperate with one another, and cooperation between the Muslims and the People of the Book is not possible. The wealth of the disbelievers is even worse than that, as we have already explained earlier. Loyalty with the Muslims can only exist in religion, in the establishment of religion and in jihad, and in these matters cooperation with a non-Muslim is in no way possible.

This issue is ideological and clear-cut. In this matter only a decisive and firm stance can be adopted, and this is what befits a Muslim: clear-cut seriousness.

Having finished with these three stern calls addressed to the believers, now the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) is addressed, that you yourself should turn towards the People of the Book and ask them: Tell us, what are the reasons for this enmity from you towards us? Why are you angry with us? Merely because we have believed in Allah alone, and along with the present Book we have believed in those Books which were revealed to you before us, and now that the rain of mercy is coming, we benefit from it. The enmity is simply this: that we Muslims believe fully, and you People of the Book are immersed in wickedness and immorality. This address of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is extremely humiliating for them, yet through this address the matter is also clearly explained, and it is a decisive address, and through it it is determined what the point of separation is.

This question is being put to the People of the Book in accordance with the guidance of Allah the Exalted. On one hand, this question manifests the reality: what is the actual situation between the People of the Book and the believers, and what are the causes and reasons due to which the People of the Book have adopted this stance against the religion of Islam and the Muslim community. On the other hand, this question is rhetorical and denies, and it is shown that the stance they have adopted does not befit them. The reasons due to which they have set themselves on this enmity do not demand what they do. This is also an admonition for the people of Islam, and they are made to feel aversion so that they never establish a bond of loyalty with this people, and this is indirectly a confirmation of the stance that was earlier stated under the three calls: that under no circumstances should you establish such a relationship with these people.

Even during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the People of the Book held enmity towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Islamic movement merely because these people were steadfast in faith in Allah. They believed in the Holy Qur'an, and they also believed in the earlier Books, and apart from this the believers had no other crime. And even today they hold this same enmity.

These people hold enmity towards the Muslims merely because they are Muslims and are not Jews and Christians, and the condition of the Jews and Christians is that they themselves have turned away from those Books which were revealed to them. Besides their other proofs of wickedness and immorality, this is also a very strong proof: that they do not believe in the final Messengership, although this final Messengership confirms all previous Messengerships, and it is a guardian (*muhaymin*) over their guidance, except for those superstitions which they have adopted and those distortions which they themselves have introduced into it.

Why do they continue this blazing war against Islam which never cools down, and for the last fourteen centuries they have been fanning it? This war has been waged since the time when an Islamic state was established in Madinah, an Islamic identity emerged, and the Muslims took on a permanent existence on the map of the world. This existence emerged because of their religion, it was shaped by their concept of life, and it was built because of the Islamic system of life, and it was built for the establishment of the Islamic way of life.

In short, they are waging this multi-pronged battle against the Muslims because they are, above all, Muslims, and these people will not end this war until they have turned the Muslims back from their religion and until they have made them non-Muslims. Their desire for this is because they themselves have abandoned their religion and become wicked, so they do not like that anyone else in the world should remain a true believer who walks well upon the religion. And Allah the Exalted has stated this reality very clearly in another place, addressing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion.﴾

And this is why, in this context, Allah has clearly placed before the People of the Book their real aims and objectives, that is, why they hold enmity.
