(Ayat) "Number 59."

"Allah, in His true word, repeats this reality again and again, while the People of the Book want to melt it away, to suppress it and to deny it. And apart from the People of the Book, most of the so-called Muslims are also against this reality, and under the banner of materialism and atheism they want to establish friendship and alliance (muwalat) between the people of Islam and the People of the Book, which is contrary to the policy of the Quran.

Even today the People of the Book want to melt that same ice, or rather to suppress it and wipe out its traces. And they do this because they want to deceive the inhabitants of Islamic countries, or deceive those inhabitants whose forefathers were Muslims. These People of the Book want to destroy that understanding which the Divine (rabbani) method of training had produced among the Muslims, and as long as this understanding and consciousness remains alive among Muslims, the Crusader imperialism cannot stand against them, let alone establish colonies in the Islamic world. When the People of the Book suffered a crushing defeat in the Crusader wars, and after that also failed in the propagation of Christianity, they had no option but to adopt the path of deceit and cunning, and to spread among those populations, which are the heirs of the Muslims, the notion that now all fighting in the name of religion has ended, that the previous era was a dark age in which all nations fought religious wars, and that now the world has found a new light; now is the age of progress, and now fighting according to any religious way of life is neither lawful, nor appropriate, nor in the interest of this world. Today is the material age, and now wars will be fought over markets and raw materials. Therefore, the Muslims, or the heirs of the Muslims, should not think of any religious struggle or any movement for the revival of religion.

And when the People of the Book become satisfied that the people of Islam have now become careless about their borders, and this abandonment of alliance (tark muwalat) has vanished from their thought and consciousness, then they spread their imperialist net. Especially then they spread the imperialist net within the Islamic world with great freedom. Now they have become safe from the anger and wrath of Muslims in the Islamic world, and when they lulled the Muslims to sleep by patting them, then they not only gained an ideological victory, but also opened for themselves paths of every kind of plunder and looting in the Islamic world. Then they established their colonies, looted the wealth of the Muslims with both hands, and after the ideological victory they also took control of the material world, and the situation became such that there was no difference left between the Muslims and the People of the Book. Both became nearly alike. Agents of the People of the Book are now working within the Islamic world, whom the imperialist powers have placed everywhere. Some are openly placed, and some are their secret agents. They too repeat the same thing, because they are agents of the People of the Book, and these people carry out this work within Islamic boundaries. These agents even go so far as to say that the Crusades were not really Crusades; the Muslims who fought these wars under Islamic banners were not Muslims at all, they were merely nationalists. Subhan Allah.

A third party, which is a most foolish party, is invited by the imperialist powers that are the heirs of Crusaderism in the West, saying: come, let us become brothers, let us defend religion and refute the atheists. These deceived people accept their invitation, but they forget that this Western offspring of the Crusaders, whenever there is a war between Islam and atheism, lines up with the atheists; they stand in one row whenever Muslims confront the atheists. For centuries their conduct has continued exactly so. Even today, the war against materialism is no problem for them. They give most importance to the war they wage against Islam, because they know that the material and atheist enemy is a temporary and transient enemy, while Islam is a permanent and solid ideology which is for them a permanent enemy. They have started this war because they want to end the awakening that is apparently arising among the Islamic forces. Moreover, these people want to protect their own interest by throwing foolish Muslims into the war against atheism, because these atheists are the political opponents of Western and Crusader imperialism, and these two battles would in effect be against Islam. And remember that against both the Crusaders and the atheists, Muslims have only the ideological weapon, and that is the understanding and insight which the verses of the Holy Quran seek to produce in them.

This is a deep game, and it throws the people of Islam into deception. Outwardly the People of the Book and the Crusaders express friendship, and these deceived Muslims consider these People of the Book sincere. They invite the people of Islam to unity, brotherhood and alliance, and they state the aim as defending religion; but the deceived Muslims forget fourteen hundred years of history, in which their attitude has been one of hostility, and there is no exception to this. Moreover, history is a big matter and very long, but these people also forget the clear teachings of Allah which their Lord is giving them directly. This is such a teaching that it is undoubted, there is no doubt in it. No deviation from it is possible, provided there is trust in Allah and conviction that the command of Allah is most serious.

These deceivers and the deceived, in this matter, present in support of their policy those verses of the Holy Quran and those hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) which emphasize good dealing with the People of the Book and that they should be treated with tolerance in trade and conduct. But these people forget the warnings, cautions and decisive prohibitions of the Quran which it issues against establishing relations with the People of the Book, and which explain in detail the reasons for this command, and what the plan of the Islamic movement is in this regard and what it should be. On what lines the Islamic organization should be, and that friendship and alliance with them should be completely ended, because for Muslims mutual alliance and mutual support is only for the establishment of the Islamic system and for establishing Islam in practical life. Regarding the aim of the movement for the leadership (imamat) of religion, there is absolutely no point of commonality between us and the People of the Book. Although before their distortions, the religions of Muslims and the People of the Book had many points in common. But now the situation is that they are our enemies only because we are Muslims and bearers of the aim of establishing religion, and they can be pleased with us only if we abandon this aim and become Jews or Christians, as Allah has stated in explicit text (al-Baqarah: 120).

These people want to cut the Quran into pieces. They break it up and take from it those parts which they like and which support their call, and they keep Muslims heedless. Even though those verses may be correct, these people leave aside those verses which are completely contrary to their deceitful policy.

We prefer that we listen to Allah's word on this issue. Allah's speech in this regard is most clear and decisive. As for the speech of these deceivers, whether we listen to it or not is the same.

Pause for a few minutes! And reflect on this subject. Allah explains the reason for the eternal enmity of these people as being that, because of the comprehensive belief of Muslims in belief in Allah, belief in the Messenger and belief in the Books, these people have become their enemies. But Allah also mentions another important matter.

(Ayat) "And most of you are defiant (fasiqun)." (5:59) "And most of you are defiant." Their defiance and wickedness is also one of the causes of this enmity to Islam, because a crooked person finds an upright person very offensive. This is a psychological reality, and the Quran's phrase confirms it. This is a deep psychological hint, because a person who has taken a crooked path cannot bear to see others walking on that path. If he sees such people, he feels that he has fallen into defiance and wickedness and has deviated from the right path, and the fact that some other people remain steadfast on the path of truth is itself proof that he has deviated. That is why this deviant person becomes an enemy of the upright person who is straight on the path of truth, and then takes revenge against him merely because he is truthful. This act of revenge occurs so that this deviant person may, by coaxing and cajoling, bring that righteous person also onto his own path, and if he is very stubborn and does not accept, then he destroys him.

This is a permanent principle, and it is not only correct regarding the relations between the People of the Book and the people of Islam in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but it applies to the policies of the People of the Book and the people of Islam in general. Whoever leaves any righteous group or principled community, his effort is that he should turn all people away from that community, and in a society of the wicked, the sinners and the evil-doers, the war is always against the righteous. All the wicked gather together against the righteous, and all those who have deviated from principles become enemies of those who stand firm on principles. This war is a natural war, and it is fought on the same principle to which this Quranic verse points.

It was already known to Allah that from the side of evil there would always be enmity against good, that falsehood would always stand against truth, and that on seeing the displays of steadfastness the wicked and the defiant would burn with jealousy, and the deviators would be very angry with those who are firm on principles.

Allah also knew that goodness, truth, steadfastness and principled adherence would have to defend themselves, and that they would have to fight a decisive battle against evil, falsehood, wickedness and deviation. This would be such a final confrontation that for the people of truth there would be no alternative but to plunge into that battle and confront falsehood. If they do not engage in this battle, falsehood itself will attack them, and truth will not be able to escape from it in any way, because falsehood's aim is to wipe it out completely.

It would be a most heedless and foolish thought for any truth-seeking, reformist, steadfast and principled person to think that the callers to evil, falsehood and wickedness would leave him in peace, and that he would escape from this struggle between truth and falsehood, or that some compromise or treaty of peace could be made between truth and falsehood. If not, then their good lies in always being ready for this inevitable battle, remaining with careful thought, good preparation and company, and not falling for the enemy's tricks for an illusory peace, otherwise the enemy will devour them and lick them clean.

Then, as we continue our study, instructions are given to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for dealing with the People of the Book. It should be remembered that earlier it had been clearly stated why the People of the Book harbour such deep enmity towards the Islamic system and the Muslims. Now here some pages of the ancient history of the Children of Israel are turned over, and how they behaved towards their Lord?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 60:

(Verse) "No. 60."

Here we are now made to study the history of the Jews. These are the very people upon whom Allah's curse fell and upon whom Allah's wrath descended, and by distorting their forms, some of them were turned into apes and swine, and yet these people still adopted the worship of the Taghut (false authority, transgressor).

The stories of their being cursed and of Allah's wrath descending upon them are mentioned repeatedly in the Holy Qur'an. Moreover, the Qur'an also mentions those incidents in which some of them were transformed into the shape of apes and swine. However, the charge of worshipping the Taghut that is laid against them here is of great significance from the perspective of the themes of this Surah. We will give some detail about it, because this word has been used for a very important and specific meaning.

The word Taghut is used for every authority that is not derived from the Being of Allah Ta'ala; every command that is not derived from Islamic Shari'ah is a command of the Taghut, and every act that is not derived from the Islamic Shari'ah is Taghut. Every oppression that is not based on truth is Taghut. Moreover, encroaching upon Allah's sovereignty, Allah's divinity and His legislation is the greatest form of Taghut, and whatever word and meaning fits Taghut applies to it.

They used to worship... it was not that they worshipped them. The reality was that they had adopted the Shari'ah framed by their rabbis and monks and had abandoned the Shari'ah sent by Allah. Therefore Allah said that they had begun to worship the rabbis and monks, and that these people had become polytheists. This profound meaning is included in the word Taghut. That is, they were obedient to a government that was not based on Shari'ah and was rebellious. The reality is that these people did not perform prostrations before that government or the rabbis and monks; rather, they worshipped in the sense that they obeyed them. When someone obeys the Taghut, he goes outside the circle of Allah's religion and Allah's obedience.

Here Allah Ta'ala has directed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the fact that he should confront the People of the Book keeping in view their history, and that they deserve the same recompense they received in their history. It is as if these Jews, generation after generation, are the same people, because their nature is one, and this was bound to be their end.

(Verse) "Qul hal unabbi'kum bi-sharrin min dhalika mathubatan 'inda Allah." (5:60) "Say: Shall I inform you of something worse in recompense with Allah than that?"

That is, the hostility of the People of the Book toward the Muslims, which is more dangerous than their conspiracies against Islam and their punishing and tormenting believers merely for their faith, is an even worse matter, and that is enmity with Allah and the punishment of Allah. The enmity of Allah and His punishment against a servant is very dangerous. And His judgment is that they are mischief-makers, misguided, and strayed from the straight path.

(Verse) "Ula'ika sharrun makanan wa adallu 'an sawa'i as-sabil." (5:60) "Their station is worse, and they are further astray from the even path."

Here the Qur'an, by mentioning the attributes of their signs, makes the Muslims averse to befriending them and forming ties of alliance with them. Whereas earlier their historical role and their evil end were mentioned, now the Muslims are warned against them by exposing some of their secrets, and in this portrayal the Jews are highlighted more prominently, because the matter concerned the circumstances of that time, and the greatest fitnah at that time was indeed the Jewish fitnah.

The high values of life come to an end, evil comes to dominate society, and whenever a person gets the opportunity to observe such societies, it is found that in them people try to outdo one another in evil, sin and oppression. The powerful people of that society are oppressors within their own sphere, and the mighty are oppressors within their own sphere. Pollution with sin and oppression in such fallen, corrupt societies is not confined only to the powerful; rather, the weak too become involved in these crimes, until all people are swept away in the flood of sin and aggression. These weak people certainly are not able to oppress the mighty, but these weak people then oppress one another, and if they cannot even oppress one another, then they lay hands on the sanctities of Allah, because in corrupt societies only the limits of Allah remain, and before them lies an open field to break them. In such a situation, neither the powerful rulers nor the weak subjects protect the limits of Allah. In short, any society that falls victim to moral decay has a prevalence of a sinful life and oppressive conduct, rather a competition (musara'at) in running toward sin and oppression takes place.

(Verse 62) "Why do their rabbis and scholars not forbid them from uttering sin and from consuming what is unlawful? Indeed, evil is what they have been doing."

When a society has fallen into moral decay and corruption, one of its major signs is that the guardians of its law encourage the violation of the law. The scholars ('ulama') and moral guides (mashayikh) remain silent over immorality and injustice. And what were the characteristics of the Children of Israel? "They did not forbid one another from the wrongs they committed." This is what the Qur'an itself has said about them elsewhere.

A healthy, living, strong and virtuous society is characterised by the prevalence everywhere of enjoining good (amr bil-ma'ruf) and forbidding evil (nahy 'an al-munkar). In it there are always people whose mission is enjoining good and forbidding evil, and among its common people too, such elements prevail who give ear to enjoining good and forbidding evil. And the society is so governed by its traditions that enjoining good and forbidding evil cannot be eliminated, nor can those who carry out this task be harmed in the least. This is what Allah has said about a healthy society that arose in the form of the Muslim ummah.

"You are the best nation brought forth for mankind: you enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah." (3:110) "You are the best ummah, you command good, forbid evil and believe in Allah." And regarding the Children of Israel, who were accustomed to a corrupt society: "They did not forbid one another from the wrongs they committed." This, as it were, is the distinguishing mark between two kinds of societies.

Here the scholars and mashayikh of the Jews are being rebuked: why have they become tongue-tied, and why do they not raise their voice against those who are advancing in a life of sin, mutual oppression and consuming what is unlawful, and do not fulfil the duty of guarding the Book of Allah that was imposed upon them?

This is a warning cry to all those who call themselves people of religion and scholars. The reform or corruption of society depends upon those who are the representatives of that society, its religion and its law, namely the scholars and mashayikh. If they perform the duties of enjoining good and forbidding evil, there will be reform; and if they remain silent, there will be deterioration. As we have said earlier in Zilal al-Quran, this task requires a government that carries out enjoining good and forbidding evil, and this system is separate from preaching and propagation, because enjoining good and forbidding evil requires authority, an authority through which enjoining good and forbidding evil becomes a meaningful thing and not mere verbal lip-service.

Now an example is given of the intellectual crookedness and moral aberration of these people. The Qur'an gives a most abhorrent example of the crooked thinking and wrong conduct of these misguided and abject Jews.

"Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they have said. Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills." (5:64) "The Jews say, 'Allah's hand is chained.' Their hands have been chained, and they have been cursed for this nonsense they utter... Allah's hands are open; He spends as He pleases."

This was a very evil conception of Allah among the Jews. The Qur'an has recorded their many evil suspicions at various places. At one place they said, "Allah is poor and we are rich." They said this at the time when they were asked to contribute to Islamic causes. According to Arabic idiom, saying that Allah's hand is chained means that Allah is miserly. In their view, Allah gives people very little provision, and therefore they too are given little, so how should they spend? Their consciousness had become so corrupted and their hearts so hardened that they did not even use the word "miserly" for Allah, but used a worse word which is more insulting: that Allah's hands are chained.

Allah answers them in their own words. They are cursed, and they are declared outcast from His presence. "Their hands were chained, and they were cursed for what they said." (5:64) Their hands were tied because they uttered this nonsense, and they were cursed. And so it happened: in history there is no people more miserly and more devoted to wealth than the Children of Israel.

After this, Allah corrects their base thinking and clarifies concerning His own exalted Being that He is most generous. His hands are open, and He bestows the overflowing grace of His mercy upon His servants without measure.

"Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills." (5:64) Allah's gifts are continuous, and rain of them is falling upon all creation, clearly visible to those who see. Look, Allah's hands are open, His bounty and generosity are full, His gifts are great, and they speak for themselves. Yes, the Jews do not see them, because they are busy day and night in accumulating wealth, drowned day and night in disbelief and disobedience, and their attitude towards the Being of Allah is insulting day and night.

Allah shows the Prophet ﷺ a picture of their future: what their end is going to be. And this end is coming upon them because these people burned and seethed at the descent of the message of prophethood upon Muhammad ﷺ, especially because through this message an old and new charge was lodged against them.

"That which has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief." (5:64) "The truth is that the word revealed to you from your Lord has only increased most of them in their defiance and falsehood."

Because of this malice and envy, why was prophethood given to the Messenger ﷺ, and further because this prophethood recorded all their filth without omission or reduction, these people will proceed further on the path of rebellion, denial and disbelief. Because they refused to believe, they will keep advancing on the path of disbelief, the opposite of faith. Due to considering themselves great and increasing in disbelief, and due to their natural rebelliousness and transgression, these people will advance further on this path, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will become for them a cause of day-and-night torment and distress.

Another characteristic of theirs regarding the future is mentioned: these people will also be enemies of one another. Severe hostility will exist between them. Whenever they prepare some great conspiracy against Islam, kindle the fire of war, or devise some military scheme against the Islamic movement, Allah will defeat it and save the community of believers.

"And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Whenever they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it." (5:64) "We have placed among them enmity and hatred till the Day of Resurrection; every time they kindle the fire of war, Allah extinguishes it." Until today the Jewish sects are enemies of one another. Although in today's age it appears outwardly that world Jewry has united, and it kindles the flames of war in Muslim countries everywhere and is successful. It is the Islamic regiment through whose hands their humiliation is written. Since at present a regiment of people firm in faith, who rely on Allah's promises and who become the instrument and means of the hand of power, through which Allah does what He wills, is absent...

That is why whatever arrows of mischief and conspiracy they have in their quiver, they shoot against the Islamic ranks, and whatever grip they have in their hands, they use against those Islamic units which are becoming the vanguard of the movement for the revival of knowledge. These Jews are searching throughout the world and through their agents are crushing the heads of these Islamic regiments everywhere. They are committing most savage crimes and most detestable acts against the Islamic leadership. They pay no heed to any pact of alliance, any covenant, or any national or international charter against this Islamic regiment. But Allah has kept His affairs in His own hand; His promise is true that the party of Allah will surely prevail.

(Verse 65–66)

These two verses set out a great principle of the Islamic worldview. For this reason, they express a fundamental truth of human life. Here this principle needs proper explanation, and in the modern age the need for such explanation has become far greater than before. Human reason, human standards and human circumstances keep changing, and they go through ups and downs. Because of the agitation and intellectual confusion of the modern age, a person can even lose the right path in understanding this great truth.

Here Allah invites the People of the Book to believe, and says that if they believe, Allah will forgive all their faults and admit them into the Garden of Bliss; and this is the reward of the Hereafter. But if, in their worldly life, they had established the system of Allah that existed among them in the Torah and the Gospel, and the teachings that Allah had revealed to them, in which they later made alterations, then even if they had done so, at the very least this worldly life would have passed well for them. Their affairs would have prospered, their lawful provision would have increased, provision would have descended on them from the sky, and the earth beneath them would have yielded its gold; their produce would have been abundant, it would have been distributed well among them, and all their worldly affairs and problems would have been resolved. But alas, they neither believe, nor adopt the way of God-fearing conduct, nor do they implement the Islamic system of life... Yes, among them there have been a few people in their history who walked upon the straight path and did not wrong their own souls, but most of them were men of evil deeds (Qur'an 5:66: "وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون"). Thus these two verses make it quite clear that the establishment of the Islamic system of life, and acting upon Islam in this worldly life, is not merely a guarantee that it will provide the means of good in the life of the Hereafter for those who do so, although the great and lasting purpose of establishing the Islamic system is the attainment of salvation in the Hereafter. That too is an extremely important and lasting purpose, but the establishment of the religion is also the solution to the problems of this world, and those who establish the religion will also have a good worldly life. The resources of this world will be abundant, and their distribution will be very well managed. A system of mutual support will be established within society, and society will become self-sufficient in worldly terms. Allah depicts the economic prosperity found within an Islamic society in this way, and this portrayal expresses abundance and overflowing bounty: ("لاكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم" — Qur'an 5:66), "they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet." Here an indication is given that, according to the Islamic outlook, it is not the case that there is one separate path such that, the moment a person deviates from it, one should understand that his world and his Hereafter have been ruined. This single path is the path of faith, God-fearing conduct and the establishment of the religion, and the path of living under the religious system.

This system is not merely a name for creed, merely for theory, and merely for inner consciousness. Certainly these elements are also within it, but in reality it is, together with inner consciousness, also a practical system for human life, whose establishment is obligatory and whose transformation of life in accordance with it is obligatory. And alongside the establishment of the religion, there is also need for taqwa (God-consciousness). Taqwa is the standard through which life in this world can be set right. Through it the system of worldly life can be made right, and abundance of provision can be achieved. Through it the produce of the land can increase, and it can be well distributed, so that all people eat and drink, and under this system provision rains down on them from the sky and the earth yields its bounty.

In the religious system of life, renunciation of the world is not a requirement for religiosity, and nor is worldly humiliation and disgrace necessary for attaining the bliss of the Hereafter. Passing through this world is the only way to the Hereafter. These are the matters that have today clouded the thinking of the people of the world, and because of these ideas the practical lives of people are also affected.

In people's thinking, the paths of this world and the Hereafter are separate, and because of this a great difference arises in their conduct as well. Thus, in the thinking of an ordinary person, there is no form of combining this world and the Hereafter. Likewise, in the thinking of the world spread across this globe, there is no form in which the path of this world and the path of the Hereafter become one. The thinking of these people is that they will either take up this world, in which case they must abandon the Hereafter, or they will take the path of the Hereafter, and for that they must abandon this world. There is no conception in which this world and the Hereafter are gathered into one system, because in that age the real circumstances of people and their ways compelled a person to think in this manner.

It is a fact that misguided jahiliyyah (ignorance), godless jahiliyyah, and the jahiliyyah ignorant of the Islamic system have made the paths of this world and the Hereafter distant and separate. It keeps widening the distance between these two paths and wishes to uproot religion from its very root. This jahiliyyah has made it necessary that, in order to become prominent in society and to obtain the worldly interests, it is essential to forget the path of the Hereafter altogether, to sacrifice these religious guidances, and even to abandon moral values, and to leave aside lofty ideals and pure conduct; and these are precisely the matters on which our religion lays stress. Thus those who seek the Hereafter have made it binding upon themselves to withdraw from the struggle of this life, because the ways of this life are impure, and those who become prominent in society and earn profits through these means are involved in wrong practices. All the means of trade are impure and cannot be purified, nor can they be made to conform to religion and morality. These means cannot be made to conform to the will of Allah at all, therefore if one wishes to attain perfection in religion, one must sever ties with the world.

This modern jahiliyyah regards the present state of affairs as final and says that there is no way out of this evil situation. Union between this world and the Hereafter is impossible, nor is it possible to join these two paths, whereas it is by no means so. This is not an irreconcilable situation. The contradiction between this world and the Hereafter, and this separation between the paths of this world and the Hereafter that jahiliyyah has created, is not a final and decisive reality, nor is this situation unchangeable and incapable of reform. Rather, the present situation is extremely unnatural, and its change is necessary. It is a temporary thing, and the present circumstances are conditions imposed upon humanity.

The true reality is that in which the path of this world and the Hereafter is one. The path of the Hereafter's good should be the same path in which the good of this world lies, and in which the productive activity of this world, progress and growth, abundance of production, agriculture and the development of the land themselves become the path that proves to be the cause and means of the reward of the Hereafter. Just as these works are good works for this world, so too faithfulness, God-fearing conduct and righteous deeds should be a cause of the construction and development of this world. Just as these matters are a cause of Allah's pleasure and bring reward in the Hereafter, so too these matters should be a cause of our worldly progress.

This is in accordance with human nature and temperament, and is indeed the authentic and straight path. Humanity's being guided onto this natural and authentic path is possible only in the case that human life conforms to the system that is pleasing to Allah, because it is this system that turns all deeds into worship, and it is precisely this system that makes man's act of khilafah fil-ardh (vicegerency on earth) into worship. What is khilafah fil-ardh? It consists of labour and production, of the greatest possible progress and growth. The just distribution of the provision that reaches man from the heavens through the means of the earth is part of khilafah. Consider what Allah says in this verse...

According to the Islamic worldview, man on this earth is the vicegerent of Allah. This vicegerency has been granted to him by Allah's permission, and it is a conditional vicegerency: that the act of vicegerency conform to the Islamic method, and that the system of vicegerency run in accordance with the system of the Shariah. Man should obey Allah and seek the reward of the Hereafter. For this reason, any action of man by which some produce is obtained in the world, or any action by which raw materials are put to use and made beneficial for people, whether it is within the earth or beyond the universe, all these works fall under this theory of khilafah fil-ardh and are counted as worship. The result of the act of this khilafah is that if man proceeds correctly upon it, he will receive provision from within the earth as well as from the heavens, and blessings and outpourings of bounty will descend upon him. This matter can be well understood from the manner of expression of the Holy Qur'an.

According to the Islamic worldview, the one who does not till the bosom of the earth, does not bring forth springs and rivers from it, and does not put to use the other natural resources of this universe, is a disobedient sinner who neglects the duty of khilafah fil-ardh for which Allah has appointed him vicegerent. Allah said to the angels: "Indeni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifah" — "Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a vicegerent."

And elsewhere: "Wa sakhkhara lakum ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ardi jami'an minh" — "And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him." If a person does not carry out works of progress, he is in effect keeping suspended the provision that Allah has created for him, and when he has put his own world into loss, together with that the loss of the Hereafter has also occurred.

According to this view, the Islamic method of life creates a beautiful harmony and combination between worldly action and the success of the Hereafter. Therefore Islam does not advise man to renounce the world in order to attain the Hereafter, nor does it advise him to renounce the Hereafter so that his world may become better. This is because, according to the Islamic worldview, there is no contradiction between this world and the Hereafter; they are neither opposed nor alternatives to each other.

All the people of this world, according to the Islamic worldview, are placed by Allah in the station of khilafah fil-ardh. The people of all nations and communities are khulafa' of Allah. The human species is a vicegerent, but is the responsibility of a single individual human being in worldly matters any different? No, he too is a vicegerent; what is the obligation of the human collective according to the Islamic worldview is an obligation upon a single human being too. There can be no difference, contradiction or conflict between the duties of the individual and of society. Therefore Islam makes it obligatory upon every individual to devote his entire physical and intellectual strength to the development of the natural resources of the heavens and the earth for provision, but this work, production and abundance of output should be for Allah's sake; in this work he should commit no injustice, betray no one, not steal, not embezzle, not eat what is unlawful, and not usurp the right of his brother. He should distribute the resources that have gathered in his hands, even though these resources are in his individual ownership and he has the full right to keep them. Society has the right to take from his resources and his produce only that which Allah has prescribed. The Islamic system regards the work of one who performs it within these limits and bounds as an act of worship. Its benefit accrues to him in this world as well as in the Hereafter. Then, this Islamic system of life establishes a particular connection between the individual and his Lord through the acts of worship that Islam has prescribed for relation with Allah, so that this person's connection with his Lord remains established. For example, through the obligation of prayer five times a day this connection is renewed again and again. In the blessed month of Ramadan, once a year, through fasting, he is strengthened from strength to greater strength. Then, by performing Hajj at least once in a lifetime this connection becomes ever more firmly established, and through paying zakat once a year, the one who engages in the productive activity mentioned above strengthens this connection.

From this it becomes clear what value Islamic worship holds in the Islamic system. It is, as it were, a renewal of covenant with Allah. The responsibilities of this system of life include those responsibilities which it has to discharge in matters of productive activity on this earth, the just distribution of wealth, and the settlement of disputes when differences arise among people. Through these acts of worship, a fresh consciousness is renewed within him that Allah is his helper in this matter. In all the duties that are imposed upon him for the establishment and management of the collective system of Islam, Allah is his helper. Whatever obstacles are created on this path by his own desires, his carnal impulses, people's malice and enmity, people's deviation, and immorality and wickedness, Allah will assist him against them.

These Islamic acts of worship and the activities of this world, such as productive work, distribution of wealth, the work of the administration and judiciary, and all the affairs of undertaking and defending the establishment of Allah's system and the founding of an Islamic state, are not separate things from one another. Faith, God-fearing conduct and taqwa are a part of this Islamic system, just as other aspects of life are parts of it. Thus this is that worldview according to which faith and taqwa become a cause of abundance of provision and plenty of production in this world, and which these two verses explicitly state.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 65–66 (part 2 of 3):

The Islamic conception of life, and the Islamic system of living derived from it, does not give precedence to the life of the Hereafter over this worldly life, nor does it give precedence to this worldly life over the Hereafter. According to the Islamic conception, the world and the Hereafter are two stages of the human journey, and they are two stopping points on one and the same road. Both are attained through one path and one struggle. However, this compound of the world and the Hereafter can be prepared only in accordance with the method of the Islamic system of life. This goal can be achieved only by following the Islamic system, and that only on condition that a purely Islamic system is enforced in the world. No other system should be introduced into it, nor should there be anything within it that is not of the Islamic system. Nor should the personal inclinations of any individual be included in it.

The Islamic system, and the Islamic conception of life upon it, does not interpret faith, piety and righteousness in such a way that they become opposed to, or a substitute for, worldly activities, production, growth, and the beautification and embellishment of life. Nor does it provide the concept that it would indicate the path to the Hereafter and the attainment of Paradise, but leave people free to improve their worldly condition and to make the world a paradise, so that they may create for themselves whatever path they wish. That concept belongs to those who have studied Islam only superficially in this modern age. As for the Islamic conception of life, all activities, all productive works, the methods of growth, and every kind of beautification and embellishment of this life are demands of Islam, and they are duties arising from the concept of vicegerency on earth (khilafat fi'l-ard), a vicegerency which is the right of all human beings. Faith, worship, reform and piety are the links, the regulations, the motives and the incentives through which the Islamic system is actually established in people's lives. These two things together make a human being worthy and deserving of the earthly paradise and the heavenly paradise. This is the right path, and according to it there is no duality or contradiction between religion (al-din) and practical, material life. This is in contrast to the situation that the material jahiliyyahs spread across the whole globe have created, in which a distinction has been made between religion and materialism. This gives rise to confusion in people's minds, namely that renunciation of the world is necessary for the attainment of the Hereafter, and that according to no concept and no practical system can the world and the Hereafter be combined, nor can they come together.

This abhorrent distinction that has been maintained between the paths of this world and the Hereafter, the line that has been drawn between worldly deeds and otherworldly deeds, the enormous gulf that has been created between spiritual progress and material progress, and the gulf created between success in worldly life and salvation in the Hereafter, and again the gulf created between success in worldly life and salvation in the Hereafter: this abhorrent separation has not been imposed upon man by the divine decree (taqdir ilahi), nor has any such division been made by the divine commands regarding qada' and qadar. It is rather a most abhorrent burden that humanity has imposed upon itself, and it has imposed it because it has exiled the Islamic system of life from its own life and has fabricated for itself systems of life of its own, which are contrary and opposed to Islamic life.

This is the burden which has broken the nerves of man, and his worldly life has also become bitter. The Hereafter ruin that will befall man as a result of it will be even harsher and far more bitter. Yet these people continue, without interruption, to fulfil this duty which they have imposed upon themselves.

As a result, their life has become extremely bitter. They are immersed in bewilderment, constriction of heart and intellectual anxiety. Why is this so? Because they wish to believe in God, yet they also live in a society and in international conditions whose ways, whose ideas and conceptions, whose entire business, whose entire means of livelihood, and in which all the paths to success, are opposed to the path of God. In it there is a contradiction between religious concepts, religious beliefs and prevailing morality; its conduct, its laws and regulations, and its values and priorities are all, without exception, against religion and conscience.

At present the whole of humanity is suffering from this misfortune, whether it follows materialist and atheistic creeds, or lives under some materialist ideology whose adherents, although they profess a religion, keep religion far away from the sphere of practical life. These doctrines think, or the enemies of humanity propagate the idea, that "religion" is for God and this life is for people, and that religion consists of belief, morality, consciousness and worship, while the general system of people's lives, their law, their conduct and their productive pursuits, all lie outside the domain of religion.

At present the whole world is paying this heavy price as a compulsory tax. Misfortune, extreme anguish, bewilderment, anxiety and the spiritual void in life are a tax which man has imposed upon himself. He has to pay this tax because this world does not accept the Islamic system of life, in which there is no distinction between this world and the Hereafter, but rather both the world and the Hereafter are included among the constituent elements of that system. In that system there is no difference between the comfort and ease obtained in this world and the comfort obtained in the Hereafter; rather, there is complete harmony between them.

Here an important question arises: some peoples who are deprived even of faith, in whom there is no fear of God, and who do not accept the Islamic methodology of life, nevertheless have a great abundance of worldly production, worldly comforts, and the necessities of life. Certainly, in some periods of world history there have been temporary intervals of this kind, but these episodes have not been lasting. Therefore we cannot regard the life found within those intervals as a second sunnah of God. Very soon the bad consequences of this separation of religion and worldly life have appeared among such nations and societies, and in today's age the following bad signs are appearing within irreligious societies:

(1) In these societies the distribution of wealth has lost its balance: some people have become very rich and some very poor. Immense difficulties and rancour have arisen within these societies, and then, because of secret agencies and class conflict, fears of coming upheavals hang over them, and the lives of all people are afflicted with bitterness.

(2) Among some nations a suffocating atmosphere of oppression and pressure has been established. These nations wished to distribute wealth forcibly among people in an unnatural manner. As a result of this unnatural distribution of wealth, severe destruction, terror and bloodshed became the habit of societies. Through this forced distribution of wealth, extreme violence became prevalent in these societies. This coercive system brought upon humanity such a calamity that the peace of all people was ruined, and people longed for a single night of rest and tranquillity.

(3) Within these societies psychological and moral diseases have been born, and because of this, sooner or later these materialist societies will have to suffer disintegration and collapse, for every activity, material progress and the system of distribution of wealth also require moral restraints. That is why we see that in materially developed countries people trample on the law, and at present the legal systems of all these countries have no moral support from the common people.

(4) In those systems where religion and worldly life have been separated, people become afflicted with nervous disorders. Today nervous diseases are most widespread within the most highly developed countries of the world, and their godless material progress has badly affected their mental powers and their endurance. As a consequence, the productive process and production itself are being affected in those countries; economic progress itself and material facilities are declining, and these are great results which have begun to appear quite clearly.

(5) Besides this, that great catastrophe by which all humanity trembles, which hangs over our heads at every moment and by which the world is agitated, is the danger of a destructive, utterly devastating war. This danger affects the nerves of every human being, whether they know it or not, and because of it many kinds of diseases are also arising. Diseases such as heart attacks, cerebral ailments and suicidal tendencies are as widespread in Western society as they are not in other countries of the world.

(6) All these signs are clearly appearing within all the developed countries, and among the peoples who are advancing very swiftly towards ruin and disintegration as a result of this, the most prominent is France, which is declining in every respect. The ruin of France is a lesson for others, and the sole cause of that ruin is that people have expelled the divine system of God from the field of worldly progress. The paths of this world and the Hereafter have been separated. Religion has been removed from human life. People have begun to take their system of life for the Hereafter from God, and their system of life for this world they take from people, and there has come about complete duality between the Islamic system and people.

Before concluding this commentary on the great principle that the Qur'an has laid down, I consider it appropriate to say that the Islamic system, which has created the beautiful blend of faith, piety and the real life of man, and which has linked morality with continuous action and with the doctrine of vicegerency on earth, is precisely that balance which God Most High has made obligatory for the People of the Book and for all human societies living in the world. If they create within themselves this beautiful blend, they will obtain abundant provision. The sky will pour down its treasures upon them and the earth will yield up its treasures. In the event of this blend, even if there are any moral shortcomings on their part in this world, they will still enter Paradise in the Hereafter; and in this world they will be granted an earthly paradise, in which there will be abundant necessities, peace and security, and tranquillity of heart, and in the Hereafter they will receive Paradise, in which there will be everlasting bliss and the pleasure of God.

Yet, despite all these realities, and while emphasising them, we must not forget that the central pillar and the first principle of the Islamic system is faith, piety, and the establishment of the Islamic order itself. When the Islamic system is established, factors such as activity, production, progress and change come into being of their own accord. Let it be remembered that when a connection with God Most High is formed, a person's taste in all matters of life changes. All values are raised. The measures of life are set right. This is the fundamental principle of the Islamic conception of life and the Islamic system of life. All other things come into being after this principle, or rather this principle of principles; all branches sprout from it and return to this principle, and all matters of this world and the Hereafter are settled in the most balanced and harmonious manner.

Now, let this be fixed firmly in your mind: what benefit does God derive from faith, piety, worship, connection with God, reaching God, and the establishment of the Shari'ah in life? All these matters are for the good of man alone. They are only for setting human life right. God is the self-sufficient King. The Islamic system of life has made all affairs dependent upon faith in God and piety. If there is no faith, then action is void. All activities that are not based on this principle are null and void, mere wind and dust, forgotten and to be forgotten, and destined to dissolve into the air. Why? Does God gain any benefit from them? If all people were to believe, does God receive anything? Does God derive any benefit from the piety of people and from the position of the Islamic system of life? The real point is that God knew, in His knowledge, that people could not be reformed except through these things, and that their success is not possible apart from them.

Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) narrates from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a Hadith Qudsi, that Allah said:

"O My servants! I have forbidden injustice for Myself, and I have made it forbidden among you as well. So do not wrong one another. O My servants! All of you are astray except those whom I guide, so seek guidance from Me, and I shall guide you. O My servants! All of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so seek food from Me, and I shall feed you. O My servants! All of you are naked except those whom I clothe, so seek clothing from Me, and I shall clothe you. O My servants! You commit sins by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me, and I shall forgive you. O My servants! You have no power to harm Me so as to harm Me, and you have no power to benefit Me so as to benefit Me. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were all to become as righteous as the most God-fearing one among you, that would add nothing to My dominion. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were all to become as wicked as the most wicked one among you, that would diminish nothing from My dominion. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were all to stand in one plain and ask of Me, and I granted each one his request, that would diminish from My treasures no more than a needle diminishes when dipped into the sea. O My servants! Your deeds are what I count for you, and then I recompense you for them. Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame none but himself." (Narrated by Muslim)

This is the foundation upon which we should understand faith (iman), God-consciousness (taqwa), worship ('ibadah), and the establishment of the Islamic system of life and the implementation of the Shari'ah (nizam-i-Islami). All these things are for us, for human beings, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The need for all these matters arises because they are necessary for the reform and well-being of humanity, both in this world and in the Hereafter.

I believe there is no need to clarify that this condition, which has been imposed upon the People of the Book, is not specific to them. The condition mentioned for the People of the Book, that their well-being depends upon faith, God-consciousness, and the establishment of the Islamic system in the Books revealed to them, namely the establishment of the system of the Torah and the Gospel and the guidance given through their prophets, was imposed on them for the period before the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). This same condition now applies to us as well, to whom the Qur'an has been revealed. This condition automatically falls upon those who say, "We are Muslims." These Muslims explicitly believe in the Qur'an that has been revealed to them and also believe in the books revealed before them. It is necessary for them to act upon the commands revealed to them and also upon those revealed in the earlier shari'ahs, and the Islamic system has not abrogated them. They are Muslims, Islam is their religion, and with Allah, no religion other than Islam is accepted at all. Nor does He now accept any other religion from anyone apart from this religion.

Therefore, the conclusion is that the condition for the well-being of this world and the Hereafter that was prescribed for the People of the Book applies to us all the more. The covenant that was made with them is also a covenant with us. And these people are more deserving that they accept the choice of Allah which He chose for them. Let them benefit from the condition of Allah, through which their sins were forgiven, they entered Paradise in the Hereafter, and upon them rain of sustenance fell from the sky and the earth brought forth gold for them.

The Muslims are even more deserving, in comparison with the People of the Book, that they fulfil the condition of Allah and benefit from it, because they are now afflicted in the Islamic world with hunger, poverty, fear, sickness and destitution, and this is the condition of the entire Islamic world. Or, in the land that was once the Islamic world, the condition of Allah stands, and the method of acting upon it is known, if they would understand or try to understand. But alas, they do not understand.

Lesson No. 51 at a Glance:

This lesson also takes up the conditions of the People of the Book, both the Jews and the Christians. It expresses their doctrinal deviation and mentions their historical misdeeds. The Jews in particular are discussed in detail. The limits of their relationship with the Messenger of Allah are defined, and their relationship with the Muslims is settled. Then, in connection with them, the duties of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of the Muslims are determined. In this context, the great doctrinal matters that form the foundation of the Islamic conception of life are also settled. Moreover, the operating principles and boundaries of the community of Muslims for its movement have been laid down. It is also explained how Muslims should conduct themselves toward these deviant aims and conceptions.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been commanded that he should convey to people whatever teaching comes to him. He should transmit the entire teachings to people in full, leaving nothing out, and no part should be abandoned or deferred under the influence of circumstances. If he did so, it would be understood that he had fallen short in discharging the duty of conveying the message.

And the command given to the Prophet (ﷺ) to convey without reduction or concealment includes, foremost, that it be declared plainly to the People of the Book that until they establish the Torah and the Gospel, they have no standing. After that, the guidance that has come from Allah must also be conveyed. This conveyance must be definite, open, explicit and unambiguous, with no vagueness of any kind. He should also declare that the Jews killed the prophets and committed unbelief by breaking the covenant that had been concluded with Allah. The Christians too distorted the doctrine of tawhid, regarded Jesus (peace be upon him) as God, and then adopted the doctrine of the Trinity. This too is tantamount to clear unbelief. He should also declare that Jesus (peace be upon him) had plainly told the Children of Israel that Paradise would be forbidden to them as a consequence of the belief in shirk, and that the Children of Israel were cursed and reviled through David (peace be upon him) and Jesus (peace be upon him), because they had become disobedient and without deeds.

The lesson concludes with the point that the People of the Book are supporting the people of polytheism against the Muslims. They do this wicked thing because they do not have a correct faith in the being of Allah. They certainly do not accept the Prophet (ﷺ). But if they do not believe in the last Prophet now, they will not be believers. After this summary commentary, study the details.

(Verse 65–66)

These two verses set out a great principle of the Islamic worldview. For this reason, they express a fundamental truth of human life. Here this principle needs proper explanation, and in the modern age the need for such explanation has become far greater than before. Human reason, human standards and human circumstances keep changing, and they go through ups and downs. Because of the agitation and intellectual confusion of the modern age, a person can even lose the right path in understanding this great truth.

Here Allah invites the People of the Book to believe, and says that if they believe, Allah will forgive all their faults and admit them into the Garden of Bliss; and this is the reward of the Hereafter. But if, in their worldly life, they had established the system of Allah that existed among them in the Torah and the Gospel, and the teachings that Allah had revealed to them, in which they later made alterations, then even if they had done so, at the very least this worldly life would have passed well for them. Their affairs would have prospered, their lawful provision would have increased, provision would have descended on them from the sky, and the earth beneath them would have yielded its gold; their produce would have been abundant, it would have been distributed well among them, and all their worldly affairs and problems would have been resolved. But alas, they neither believe, nor adopt the way of God-fearing conduct, nor do they implement the Islamic system of life... Yes, among them there have been a few people in their history who walked upon the straight path and did not wrong their own souls, but most of them were men of evil deeds (Qur'an 5:66: "وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون"). Thus these two verses make it quite clear that the establishment of the Islamic system of life, and acting upon Islam in this worldly life, is not merely a guarantee that it will provide the means of good in the life of the Hereafter for those who do so, although the great and lasting purpose of establishing the Islamic system is the attainment of salvation in the Hereafter. That too is an extremely important and lasting purpose, but the establishment of the religion is also the solution to the problems of this world, and those who establish the religion will also have a good worldly life. The resources of this world will be abundant, and their distribution will be very well managed. A system of mutual support will be established within society, and society will become self-sufficient in worldly terms. Allah depicts the economic prosperity found within an Islamic society in this way, and this portrayal expresses abundance and overflowing bounty: ("لاكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم" — Qur'an 5:66), "they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet." Here an indication is given that, according to the Islamic outlook, it is not the case that there is one separate path such that, the moment a person deviates from it, one should understand that his world and his Hereafter have been ruined. This single path is the path of faith, God-fearing conduct and the establishment of the religion, and the path of living under the religious system.

This system is not merely a name for creed, merely for theory, and merely for inner consciousness. Certainly these elements are also within it, but in reality it is, together with inner consciousness, also a practical system for human life, whose establishment is obligatory and whose transformation of life in accordance with it is obligatory. And alongside the establishment of the religion, there is also need for taqwa (God-consciousness). Taqwa is the standard through which life in this world can be set right. Through it the system of worldly life can be made right, and abundance of provision can be achieved. Through it the produce of the land can increase, and it can be well distributed, so that all people eat and drink, and under this system provision rains down on them from the sky and the earth yields its bounty.

In the religious system of life, renunciation of the world is not a requirement for religiosity, and nor is worldly humiliation and disgrace necessary for attaining the bliss of the Hereafter. Passing through this world is the only way to the Hereafter. These are the matters that have today clouded the thinking of the people of the world, and because of these ideas the practical lives of people are also affected.

In people's thinking, the paths of this world and the Hereafter are separate, and because of this a great difference arises in their conduct as well. Thus, in the thinking of an ordinary person, there is no form of combining this world and the Hereafter. Likewise, in the thinking of the world spread across this globe, there is no form in which the path of this world and the path of the Hereafter become one. The thinking of these people is that they will either take up this world, in which case they must abandon the Hereafter, or they will take the path of the Hereafter, and for that they must abandon this world. There is no conception in which this world and the Hereafter are gathered into one system, because in that age the real circumstances of people and their ways compelled a person to think in this manner.

It is a fact that misguided jahiliyyah (ignorance), godless jahiliyyah, and the jahiliyyah ignorant of the Islamic system have made the paths of this world and the Hereafter distant and separate. It keeps widening the distance between these two paths and wishes to uproot religion from its very root. This jahiliyyah has made it necessary that, in order to become prominent in society and to obtain the worldly interests, it is essential to forget the path of the Hereafter altogether, to sacrifice these religious guidances, and even to abandon moral values, and to leave aside lofty ideals and pure conduct; and these are precisely the matters on which our religion lays stress. Thus those who seek the Hereafter have made it binding upon themselves to withdraw from the struggle of this life, because the ways of this life are impure, and those who become prominent in society and earn profits through these means are involved in wrong practices. All the means of trade are impure and cannot be purified, nor can they be made to conform to religion and morality. These means cannot be made to conform to the will of Allah at all, therefore if one wishes to attain perfection in religion, one must sever ties with the world.

This modern jahiliyyah regards the present state of affairs as final and says that there is no way out of this evil situation. Union between this world and the Hereafter is impossible, nor is it possible to join these two paths, whereas it is by no means so. This is not an irreconcilable situation. The contradiction between this world and the Hereafter, and this separation between the paths of this world and the Hereafter that jahiliyyah has created, is not a final and decisive reality, nor is this situation unchangeable and incapable of reform. Rather, the present situation is extremely unnatural, and its change is necessary. It is a temporary thing, and the present circumstances are conditions imposed upon humanity.

The true reality is that in which the path of this world and the Hereafter is one. The path of the Hereafter's good should be the same path in which the good of this world lies, and in which the productive activity of this world, progress and growth, abundance of production, agriculture and the development of the land themselves become the path that proves to be the cause and means of the reward of the Hereafter. Just as these works are good works for this world, so too faithfulness, God-fearing conduct and righteous deeds should be a cause of the construction and development of this world. Just as these matters are a cause of Allah's pleasure and bring reward in the Hereafter, so too these matters should be a cause of our worldly progress.

This is in accordance with human nature and temperament, and is indeed the authentic and straight path. Humanity's being guided onto this natural and authentic path is possible only in the case that human life conforms to the system that is pleasing to Allah, because it is this system that turns all deeds into worship, and it is precisely this system that makes man's act of khilafah fil-ardh (vicegerency on earth) into worship. What is khilafah fil-ardh? It consists of labour and production, of the greatest possible progress and growth. The just distribution of the provision that reaches man from the heavens through the means of the earth is part of khilafah. Consider what Allah says in this verse...

According to the Islamic worldview, man on this earth is the vicegerent of Allah. This vicegerency has been granted to him by Allah's permission, and it is a conditional vicegerency: that the act of vicegerency conform to the Islamic method, and that the system of vicegerency run in accordance with the system of the Shariah. Man should obey Allah and seek the reward of the Hereafter. For this reason, any action of man by which some produce is obtained in the world, or any action by which raw materials are put to use and made beneficial for people, whether it is within the earth or beyond the universe, all these works fall under this theory of khilafah fil-ardh and are counted as worship. The result of the act of this khilafah is that if man proceeds correctly upon it, he will receive provision from within the earth as well as from the heavens, and blessings and outpourings of bounty will descend upon him. This matter can be well understood from the manner of expression of the Holy Qur'an.

According to the Islamic worldview, the one who does not till the bosom of the earth, does not bring forth springs and rivers from it, and does not put to use the other natural resources of this universe, is a disobedient sinner who neglects the duty of khilafah fil-ardh for which Allah has appointed him vicegerent. Allah said to the angels: "Indeni ja'ilun fil-ardi khalifah" — "Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a vicegerent."

And elsewhere: "Wa sakhkhara lakum ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ardi jami'an minh" — "And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him." If a person does not carry out works of progress, he is in effect keeping suspended the provision that Allah has created for him, and when he has put his own world into loss, together with that the loss of the Hereafter has also occurred.

According to this view, the Islamic method of life creates a beautiful harmony and combination between worldly action and the success of the Hereafter. Therefore Islam does not advise man to renounce the world in order to attain the Hereafter, nor does it advise him to renounce the Hereafter so that his world may become better. This is because, according to the Islamic worldview, there is no contradiction between this world and the Hereafter; they are neither opposed nor alternatives to each other.

All the people of this world, according to the Islamic worldview, are placed by Allah in the station of khilafah fil-ardh. The people of all nations and communities are khulafa' of Allah. The human species is a vicegerent, but is the responsibility of a single individual human being in worldly matters any different? No, he too is a vicegerent; what is the obligation of the human collective according to the Islamic worldview is an obligation upon a single human being too. There can be no difference, contradiction or conflict between the duties of the individual and of society. Therefore Islam makes it obligatory upon every individual to devote his entire physical and intellectual strength to the development of the natural resources of the heavens and the earth for provision, but this work, production and abundance of output should be for Allah's sake; in this work he should commit no injustice, betray no one, not steal, not embezzle, not eat what is unlawful, and not usurp the right of his brother. He should distribute the resources that have gathered in his hands, even though these resources are in his individual ownership and he has the full right to keep them. Society has the right to take from his resources and his produce only that which Allah has prescribed. The Islamic system regards the work of one who performs it within these limits and bounds as an act of worship. Its benefit accrues to him in this world as well as in the Hereafter. Then, this Islamic system of life establishes a particular connection between the individual and his Lord through the acts of worship that Islam has prescribed for relation with Allah, so that this person's connection with his Lord remains established. For example, through the obligation of prayer five times a day this connection is renewed again and again. In the blessed month of Ramadan, once a year, through fasting, he is strengthened from strength to greater strength. Then, by performing Hajj at least once in a lifetime this connection becomes ever more firmly established, and through paying zakat once a year, the one who engages in the productive activity mentioned above strengthens this connection.

From this it becomes clear what value Islamic worship holds in the Islamic system. It is, as it were, a renewal of covenant with Allah. The responsibilities of this system of life include those responsibilities which it has to discharge in matters of productive activity on this earth, the just distribution of wealth, and the settlement of disputes when differences arise among people. Through these acts of worship, a fresh consciousness is renewed within him that Allah is his helper in this matter. In all the duties that are imposed upon him for the establishment and management of the collective system of Islam, Allah is his helper. Whatever obstacles are created on this path by his own desires, his carnal impulses, people's malice and enmity, people's deviation, and immorality and wickedness, Allah will assist him against them.

These Islamic acts of worship and the activities of this world, such as productive work, distribution of wealth, the work of the administration and judiciary, and all the affairs of undertaking and defending the establishment of Allah's system and the founding of an Islamic state, are not separate things from one another. Faith, God-fearing conduct and taqwa are a part of this Islamic system, just as other aspects of life are parts of it. Thus this is that worldview according to which faith and taqwa become a cause of abundance of provision and plenty of production in this world, and which these two verses explicitly state.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 65–66 (part 2 of 3):

The Islamic conception of life, and the Islamic system of living derived from it, does not give precedence to the life of the Hereafter over this worldly life, nor does it give precedence to this worldly life over the Hereafter. According to the Islamic conception, the world and the Hereafter are two stages of the human journey, and they are two stopping points on one and the same road. Both are attained through one path and one struggle. However, this compound of the world and the Hereafter can be prepared only in accordance with the method of the Islamic system of life. This goal can be achieved only by following the Islamic system, and that only on condition that a purely Islamic system is enforced in the world. No other system should be introduced into it, nor should there be anything within it that is not of the Islamic system. Nor should the personal inclinations of any individual be included in it.

The Islamic system, and the Islamic conception of life upon it, does not interpret faith, piety and righteousness in such a way that they become opposed to, or a substitute for, worldly activities, production, growth, and the beautification and embellishment of life. Nor does it provide the concept that it would indicate the path to the Hereafter and the attainment of Paradise, but leave people free to improve their worldly condition and to make the world a paradise, so that they may create for themselves whatever path they wish. That concept belongs to those who have studied Islam only superficially in this modern age. As for the Islamic conception of life, all activities, all productive works, the methods of growth, and every kind of beautification and embellishment of this life are demands of Islam, and they are duties arising from the concept of vicegerency on earth (khilafat fi'l-ard), a vicegerency which is the right of all human beings. Faith, worship, reform and piety are the links, the regulations, the motives and the incentives through which the Islamic system is actually established in people's lives. These two things together make a human being worthy and deserving of the earthly paradise and the heavenly paradise. This is the right path, and according to it there is no duality or contradiction between religion (al-din) and practical, material life. This is in contrast to the situation that the material jahiliyyahs spread across the whole globe have created, in which a distinction has been made between religion and materialism. This gives rise to confusion in people's minds, namely that renunciation of the world is necessary for the attainment of the Hereafter, and that according to no concept and no practical system can the world and the Hereafter be combined, nor can they come together.

This abhorrent distinction that has been maintained between the paths of this world and the Hereafter, the line that has been drawn between worldly deeds and otherworldly deeds, the enormous gulf that has been created between spiritual progress and material progress, and the gulf created between success in worldly life and salvation in the Hereafter, and again the gulf created between success in worldly life and salvation in the Hereafter: this abhorrent separation has not been imposed upon man by the divine decree (taqdir ilahi), nor has any such division been made by the divine commands regarding qada' and qadar. It is rather a most abhorrent burden that humanity has imposed upon itself, and it has imposed it because it has exiled the Islamic system of life from its own life and has fabricated for itself systems of life of its own, which are contrary and opposed to Islamic life.

This is the burden which has broken the nerves of man, and his worldly life has also become bitter. The Hereafter ruin that will befall man as a result of it will be even harsher and far more bitter. Yet these people continue, without interruption, to fulfil this duty which they have imposed upon themselves.

As a result, their life has become extremely bitter. They are immersed in bewilderment, constriction of heart and intellectual anxiety. Why is this so? Because they wish to believe in God, yet they also live in a society and in international conditions whose ways, whose ideas and conceptions, whose entire business, whose entire means of livelihood, and in which all the paths to success, are opposed to the path of God. In it there is a contradiction between religious concepts, religious beliefs and prevailing morality; its conduct, its laws and regulations, and its values and priorities are all, without exception, against religion and conscience.

At present the whole of humanity is suffering from this misfortune, whether it follows materialist and atheistic creeds, or lives under some materialist ideology whose adherents, although they profess a religion, keep religion far away from the sphere of practical life. These doctrines think, or the enemies of humanity propagate the idea, that "religion" is for God and this life is for people, and that religion consists of belief, morality, consciousness and worship, while the general system of people's lives, their law, their conduct and their productive pursuits, all lie outside the domain of religion.

At present the whole world is paying this heavy price as a compulsory tax. Misfortune, extreme anguish, bewilderment, anxiety and the spiritual void in life are a tax which man has imposed upon himself. He has to pay this tax because this world does not accept the Islamic system of life, in which there is no distinction between this world and the Hereafter, but rather both the world and the Hereafter are included among the constituent elements of that system.
