In that system there is no difference between the comfort and ease obtained in this world and the comfort obtained in the Hereafter; rather, there is complete harmony between them.

Here an important question arises: some peoples who are deprived even of faith, in whom there is no fear of God, and who do not accept the Islamic methodology of life, nevertheless have a great abundance of worldly production, worldly comforts, and the necessities of life. Certainly, in some periods of world history there have been temporary intervals of this kind, but these episodes have not been lasting. Therefore we cannot regard the life found within those intervals as a second sunnah of God. Very soon the bad consequences of this separation of religion and worldly life have appeared among such nations and societies, and in today's age the following bad signs are appearing within irreligious societies:

(1) In these societies the distribution of wealth has lost its balance: some people have become very rich and some very poor. Immense difficulties and rancour have arisen within these societies, and then, because of secret agencies and class conflict, fears of coming upheavals hang over them, and the lives of all people are afflicted with bitterness.

(2) Among some nations a suffocating atmosphere of oppression and pressure has been established. These nations wished to distribute wealth forcibly among people in an unnatural manner. As a result of this unnatural distribution of wealth, severe destruction, terror and bloodshed became the habit of societies. Through this forced distribution of wealth, extreme violence became prevalent in these societies. This coercive system brought upon humanity such a calamity that the peace of all people was ruined, and people longed for a single night of rest and tranquillity.

(3) Within these societies psychological and moral diseases have been born, and because of this, sooner or later these materialist societies will have to suffer disintegration and collapse, for every activity, material progress and the system of distribution of wealth also require moral restraints. That is why we see that in materially developed countries people trample on the law, and at present the legal systems of all these countries have no moral support from the common people.

(4) In those systems where religion and worldly life have been separated, people become afflicted with nervous disorders. Today nervous diseases are most widespread within the most highly developed countries of the world, and their godless material progress has badly affected their mental powers and their endurance. As a consequence, the productive process and production itself are being affected in those countries; economic progress itself and material facilities are declining, and these are great results which have begun to appear quite clearly.

(5) Besides this, that great catastrophe by which all humanity trembles, which hangs over our heads at every moment and by which the world is agitated, is the danger of a destructive, utterly devastating war. This danger affects the nerves of every human being, whether they know it or not, and because of it many kinds of diseases are also arising. Diseases such as heart attacks, cerebral ailments and suicidal tendencies are as widespread in Western society as they are not in other countries of the world.

(6) All these signs are clearly appearing within all the developed countries, and among the peoples who are advancing very swiftly towards ruin and disintegration as a result of this, the most prominent is France, which is declining in every respect. The ruin of France is a lesson for others, and the sole cause of that ruin is that people have expelled the divine system of God from the field of worldly progress. The paths of this world and the Hereafter have been separated. Religion has been removed from human life. People have begun to take their system of life for the Hereafter from God, and their system of life for this world they take from people, and there has come about complete duality between the Islamic system and people.

Before concluding this commentary on the great principle that the Qur'an has laid down, I consider it appropriate to say that the Islamic system, which has created the beautiful blend of faith, piety and the real life of man, and which has linked morality with continuous action and with the doctrine of vicegerency on earth, is precisely that balance which God Most High has made obligatory for the People of the Book and for all human societies living in the world. If they create within themselves this beautiful blend, they will obtain abundant provision. The sky will pour down its treasures upon them and the earth will yield up its treasures. In the event of this blend, even if there are any moral shortcomings on their part in this world, they will still enter Paradise in the Hereafter; and in this world they will be granted an earthly paradise, in which there will be abundant necessities, peace and security, and tranquillity of heart, and in the Hereafter they will receive Paradise, in which there will be everlasting bliss and the pleasure of God.

Yet, despite all these realities, and while emphasising them, we must not forget that the central pillar and the first principle of the Islamic system is faith, piety, and the establishment of the Islamic order itself. When the Islamic system is established, factors such as activity, production, progress and change come into being of their own accord. Let it be remembered that when a connection with God Most High is formed, a person's taste in all matters of life changes. All values are raised. The measures of life are set right. This is the fundamental principle of the Islamic conception of life and the Islamic system of life. All other things come into being after this principle, or rather this principle of principles; all branches sprout from it and return to this principle, and all matters of this world and the Hereafter are settled in the most balanced and harmonious manner.

Now, let this be fixed firmly in your mind: what benefit does God derive from faith, piety, worship, connection with God, reaching God, and the establishment of the Shari'ah in life? All these matters are for the good of man alone. They are only for setting human life right. God is the self-sufficient King. The Islamic system of life has made all affairs dependent upon faith in God and piety. If there is no faith, then action is void. All activities that are not based on this principle are null and void, mere wind and dust, forgotten and to be forgotten, and destined to dissolve into the air. Why? Does God gain any benefit from them? If all people were to believe, does God receive anything? Does God derive any benefit from the piety of people and from the position of the Islamic system of life? The real point is that God knew, in His knowledge, that people could not be reformed except through these things, and that their success is not possible apart from them.

Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) narrates from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a Hadith Qudsi, that Allah said:

"O My servants! I have forbidden injustice for Myself, and I have made it forbidden among you as well. So do not wrong one another. O My servants! All of you are astray except those whom I guide, so seek guidance from Me, and I shall guide you. O My servants! All of you are hungry except those whom I feed, so seek food from Me, and I shall feed you. O My servants! All of you are naked except those whom I clothe, so seek clothing from Me, and I shall clothe you. O My servants! You commit sins by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me, and I shall forgive you. O My servants! You have no power to harm Me so as to harm Me, and you have no power to benefit Me so as to benefit Me. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were all to become as righteous as the most God-fearing one among you, that would add nothing to My dominion. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were all to become as wicked as the most wicked one among you, that would diminish nothing from My dominion. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were all to stand in one plain and ask of Me, and I granted each one his request, that would diminish from My treasures no more than a needle diminishes when dipped into the sea. O My servants! Your deeds are what I count for you, and then I recompense you for them. Whoever finds good should praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise should blame none but himself." (Narrated by Muslim)

This is the foundation upon which we should understand faith (iman), God-consciousness (taqwa), worship ('ibadah), and the establishment of the Islamic system of life and the implementation of the Shari'ah (nizam-i-Islami). All these things are for us, for human beings, both in this world and in the Hereafter. The need for all these matters arises because they are necessary for the reform and well-being of humanity, both in this world and in the Hereafter.

I believe there is no need to clarify that this condition, which has been imposed upon the People of the Book, is not specific to them. The condition mentioned for the People of the Book, that their well-being depends upon faith, God-consciousness, and the establishment of the Islamic system in the Books revealed to them, namely the establishment of the system of the Torah and the Gospel and the guidance given through their prophets, was imposed on them for the period before the mission of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). This same condition now applies to us as well, to whom the Qur'an has been revealed. This condition automatically falls upon those who say, "We are Muslims." These Muslims explicitly believe in the Qur'an that has been revealed to them and also believe in the books revealed before them. It is necessary for them to act upon the commands revealed to them and also upon those revealed in the earlier shari'ahs, and the Islamic system has not abrogated them. They are Muslims, Islam is their religion, and with Allah, no religion other than Islam is accepted at all. Nor does He now accept any other religion from anyone apart from this religion.

Therefore, the conclusion is that the condition for the well-being of this world and the Hereafter that was prescribed for the People of the Book applies to us all the more. The covenant that was made with them is also a covenant with us. And these people are more deserving that they accept the choice of Allah which He chose for them. Let them benefit from the condition of Allah, through which their sins were forgiven, they entered Paradise in the Hereafter, and upon them rain of sustenance fell from the sky and the earth brought forth gold for them.

The Muslims are even more deserving, in comparison with the People of the Book, that they fulfil the condition of Allah and benefit from it, because they are now afflicted in the Islamic world with hunger, poverty, fear, sickness and destitution, and this is the condition of the entire Islamic world. Or, in the land that was once the Islamic world, the condition of Allah stands, and the method of acting upon it is known, if they would understand or try to understand. But alas, they do not understand.

Lesson No. 51 at a Glance:

This lesson also takes up the conditions of the People of the Book, both the Jews and the Christians. It expresses their doctrinal deviation and mentions their historical misdeeds. The Jews in particular are discussed in detail. The limits of their relationship with the Messenger of Allah are defined, and their relationship with the Muslims is settled. Then, in connection with them, the duties of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of the Muslims are determined. In this context, the great doctrinal matters that form the foundation of the Islamic conception of life are also settled. Moreover, the operating principles and boundaries of the community of Muslims for its movement have been laid down. It is also explained how Muslims should conduct themselves toward these deviant aims and conceptions.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been commanded that he should convey to people whatever teaching comes to him. He should transmit the entire teachings to people in full, leaving nothing out, and no part should be abandoned or deferred under the influence of circumstances. If he did so, it would be understood that he had fallen short in discharging the duty of conveying the message.

And the command given to the Prophet (ﷺ) to convey without reduction or concealment includes, foremost, that it be declared plainly to the People of the Book that until they establish the Torah and the Gospel, they have no standing. After that, the guidance that has come from Allah must also be conveyed. This conveyance must be definite, open, explicit and unambiguous, with no vagueness of any kind. He should also declare that the Jews killed the prophets and committed unbelief by breaking the covenant that had been concluded with Allah. The Christians too distorted the doctrine of tawhid, regarded Jesus (peace be upon him) as God, and then adopted the doctrine of the Trinity. This too is tantamount to clear unbelief. He should also declare that Jesus (peace be upon him) had plainly told the Children of Israel that Paradise would be forbidden to them as a consequence of the belief in shirk, and that the Children of Israel were cursed and reviled through David (peace be upon him) and Jesus (peace be upon him), because they had become disobedient and without deeds.

The lesson concludes with the point that the People of the Book are supporting the people of polytheism against the Muslims. They do this wicked thing because they do not have a correct faith in the being of Allah. They certainly do not accept the Prophet (ﷺ). But if they do not believe in the last Prophet now, they will not be believers. After this summary commentary, study the details.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 67-68:

(Verse) "Number 67 to 68.

The command from Allah to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is definitive: he should convey fully the entire message that Allah has sent down, should give no importance to any of the circumstances existing in the world, and should state his call completely openly and clearly. This is the duty of his prophethood, and if he did not do so, it would be as though he had not fulfilled the right of his prophetic mission and had not carried out his duties fully. As for the concern that the enemies may harm you, be assured that Allah will protect you from people, and when Allah takes on the responsibility of protecting someone, what standing do people have before Allah that they could cause him any harm?

It is not appropriate for the bearers of truth to tiptoe around or to hedge. They should speak plainly and without ambiguity. As for the people of falsehood and the opponents of truth, they may say whatever they wish and do whatever they wish. This is because those who speak the truth should not speak softly out of regard for people's desires, nor should they take into account the desires of people in this matter. The true word should be spoken with the utmost strength and force, so that it penetrates directly into the hearts of people. When the bearers of truth speak their word with strong and forceful expression, whoever has even a slight capacity to receive it, that word reaches them. And if the truth is presented in clear, unambiguous words, the hearts that do not have the capacity to accept the truth do not soften for it. These are the kind of people who wish that the caller would be gentle with them and would withdraw some of his demands, and only then would they accept the call. They set conditions of their own.

(Verse) "Indeed Allah does not guide the disbelieving people" (5:67). "Allah does not guide the disbelieving people." Therefore, you should state the truth in clear and unambiguous words, in comprehensive and decisive words. As for who believes and who does not, this depends upon whether the listener has the capacity to accept the truth or not, or whether his heart is open to that truth or not. Guidance does not depend upon compromise, consideration, or refraining from speaking the whole truth, nor does it benefit from these.

The purpose of making a decisive statement on the ideological level is also not that the speaker should speak in a very dry and harsh tone. Allah has also commanded the Prophet ﷺ to call people with wisdom and good admonition. Therefore, there is no contradiction in the Qur'anic guidance; that is, there is no conflict between the word of wisdom, the good exhortation, and the clear and decisive statement. One is the substance of the matter itself, which constitutes the components of a statement, and the other is the manner in which it is desired that this matter be conveyed to people. As far as the substance of the matter and the message of truth is concerned, it must be conveyed without any reduction or alteration, the whole matter must be conveyed, and no policy of give-and-take should be adopted in it. This is because belief and ideology are a reality whose components cannot be divided. Yes, there can be gentleness in the manner of conveying the matter. From the beginning of his mission, the Messenger ﷺ used to admonish with great wisdom and spoke in a very good manner, but the matter was always stated plainly. He would speak in this way by the command of Allah: "O people who have disbelieved, I do not worship what you worship." He would plainly say that you are disbelievers, and he would state the matter clearly that I do not worship your deities. He neither accepted those reconciliatory efforts whose aim was that there be give-and-take, nor did he ever compromise, even though they wished that he would do so. He never told the disbelievers that "I will make only minor changes in the system you follow." Rather, he would say that you people are entirely upon falsehood, and that he had come with complete truth. He would speak the truth with great force and in full, but in a manner that had no harshness and no severity of temperament. His speech was gentle. Here in this Surah, this command is given to you.

(Verse) "O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people" (5:67).

From the verses before and after this verse, it becomes clear that the purpose here is to tell the People of the Book in clear and unambiguous terms what the reality of the position they are holding is. And it should be made known that their position has no connection even remotely with reality. Neither their religion is a religion, nor their belief a correct belief, nor their faith acceptable. This is because these things of theirs do not conform to the Torah and the Gospel themselves, nor to divine guidance. Therefore, their claims that they are People of the Book, or that they hold any doctrine, or that they are religious and followers of a heavenly religion, are utterly false.

(Verse) "Say: O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord" (5:68).

"Say plainly: O People of the Book, you are not upon any foundation until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and those other books which have been sent down to you from your Lord."

When Allah commanded the Messenger ﷺ to state before the People of the Book, in explicit words, this reality regarding their religion, their belief, and their faith, that they have no reality and are not based on any solid truth, at that time they were reading their scriptures regularly. They called themselves Jews and Christians. They claimed that they were people of faith. But the decisive judgment that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to pronounce on their position contained the declaration that all their claims about themselves were false, because "religion" is not merely a name for words that someone utters with the tongue. Nor is religion the name of books which are recited with proper cadence and beautiful voice. Nor is religion a quality that is obtained by inheritance. Rather, religion is a system of life, and the components of religion include the belief and ideology that exist in the hearts, and the worship performed in the form of acts of servitude. It also includes the system of servitude upon which a complete system of life is built. As long as they do not establish this entire system of the Torah, they would be in the position of not being upon religion at all, neither among the People of the Book nor among the people of religion and belief. And this is the declaration that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to make, telling them that they should not claim for themselves any of these things.

The first requirement of establishing the Torah is that the People of the Book act upon the religion brought by Muhammad ﷺ, because Allah took from them a covenant that they would believe in all the messengers, and that whichever messenger came, they would support him and help him. In their Torah and Gospel, the attributes of Muhammad ﷺ are clearly present, as Allah Himself mentioned in the Noble Qur'an. Furthermore, they were also commanded to believe in the Torah, the Gospel, and the scripture that Allah has sent down (whether the phrase "what Allah has sent down" means the Qur'an or other books, such as the Psalms of David, etc.). We say that these people do not establish the Torah and the Gospel. Now they should enter this new religion, because this religion confirms the Torah and the Gospel, and the original teachings of the Torah and the Gospel have been preserved within it. If they do not enter Islam, they will have no religious standing, because Allah commanded the Messenger ﷺ to make this declaration; otherwise it would be considered that you have not fulfilled the right of conveying the message. And this is a severe warning that was given to the Messenger ﷺ.

Allah knew that when the religious standing of the People of the Book was challenged with these decisive and unambiguous words, they would advance further in disbelief and rebellion. They would be afflicted with more hostility and would engage in contentious argument. Yet despite these dangers, the Messenger ﷺ was commanded simply to make this declaration, and not to care about the disbelief, rebellion, misguidance, and insurrection that would result from this declaration, and not to despair. This is because the wisdom of Allah requires that the truth be proclaimed loudly and openly, and that the consequences that follow from it come to pass. Whoever adopts the path of guidance will openly be on the path of guidance, and whoever chooses the path of misguidance will openly adopt the path of misguidance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 68:

(Verse) "Wa la-yazidanna kathiran minhum ma unzila ilayka min rabbika tughyanan wa kufran, fala ta'sa 'ala al-qawm al-kafirin" (68)

It is certain that what has been revealed to you from your Lord will increase the rebellion and disbelief of many of them. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.

Through these instructions, Allah has laid down the outlines of the method of da'wah (the call to faith) for the caller and has also explained its wisdom. As for those who do not accept guidance and advance further in disbelief and rebellion, He has comforted you concerning them: they have come to deserve this outcome, because their hearts cannot bear the truth. The very substance of truthfulness has been extinguished in the depths of their hearts. Therefore, the word of truth was openly proclaimed before them, so that the filth of their hearts would become evident, they would advance further in disbelief and rebellion, and they would reach the end appointed for rebels and disbelievers.

Allah says that the People of the Book have no religious standing if they do not establish the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed from Allah, and consequently enter the new religion, as commanded in this verse and in many other verses. And if they do not do so, then they will be neither believers, nor upon any heavenly religion, nor people of a religion that Allah would accept. This also shows that because of the Prophet's (ﷺ) manner of preaching, these people were being afflicted with further rebellion and disbelief; yet despite this, the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to declare openly, to make no concession in this matter, and not to be daunted by the consequences.

Since this is a decisive matter, and it has been stated in decisive words, that (Lastum 'ala shay'), (5:68), there is no longer any room to call the People of the Book "people of religion" at all, nor any room for Muslims to establish ties of friendship and alliance with the People of the Book, much less to form a front with them against atheists and atheism, as some of our deluded and deceptive "cultural" figures do today. The People of the Book have neither established the Torah, nor established the Gospel, nor established the other teachings that were revealed from Allah; therefore no Muslim can acknowledge any religious standing for them. Nor can any Muslim grant them a status that Allah has not granted them. "And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair" (Qur'an 33:36). This is Allah's decision, and no "circumstances or conditions" can change it.

When we establish that the word of Allah is decisive, as in truth it is, we should not take into account how much agitation our proclamation of the truth creates among the People of the Book, or how fiercely they begin war against us. Nor should we strive to win their friendship, or acknowledge their religious standing, or, by pleasing them, conclude a pact of mutual support and alliance, so that the two communities would then join together to confront disbelief and atheism, when their religion is in fact nothing at all. Allah gives us no such guidance, and Allah does not accept that we should acknowledge the religious standing of the People of the Book. Allah will not forgive even this act of alliance and mutual support, nor is the thinking that gives rise to such alliance excusable, for in that case we would be making a decision that Allah has not made and choosing for ourselves what Allah has not chosen. Thus we would be affirming that the distorted and corrupted beliefs of the People of the Book are also religion, and that these two divine religions have come together to confront disbelief, whereas Allah's position is that they have no standing unless they establish the Torah, the Gospel, and all the guidance revealed from Allah; and it is evident that they are not doing so in practice.

Now consider those who say, "We are Muslims," yet do not establish what has been revealed from their Lord. They too will always be just like the People of the Book; they too have no religious standing. A scripture was revealed to the People of the Book, and they did not implement it in their lives, nor did they enforce it upon their own selves. Therefore, whoever wishes to become a Muslim should first establish Islam and the Book of Allah within his own self, then over his whole life, and then openly proclaim the truth before all people, that those who do not establish the Qur'an have no religious standing unless they implement the Qur'an in their lives. If they claim religion otherwise, their claim is refuted by the Lord of this religion. Therefore, in this matter every Muslim is obliged to speak decisively. It is obligatory upon every Muslim to call such people afresh to Islam, provided he has himself established what has been revealed from Allah in his own self and his own life. Merely claiming Islam verbally, or merely claiming it by inheritance, is of no benefit; neither does Islam come into existence through it, nor is the reality of faith produced within the self, nor will such a person be characterized by the religion of Allah. In every time and place, this is the principle and the decision.

If the People of the Book establish the Torah, the Gospel and what has been revealed from Allah in this sense, and Muslims establish the noble Qur'an in this sense, then they will be religious, and the People of the Book too will be religious according to their own understanding. In such circumstances they may conclude an agreement against some atheism; otherwise it would be deception, self-deceit, and would amount to melting down and squandering their own religious standing.

The religion of Allah is neither a flag, nor a uniform, nor an inheritance. Islam settles in the heart and manifests in life. It consists of certain beliefs that fill the heart, certain acts of worship that are performed, and a system that governs the whole of life. Islam is truly established when all these parts operate together and flow through human lives. Any other form would aim at melting down and squandering the solid shape of Islam; it would be a deception of conscience, and no sincere Muslim can be deceived by it.

A Muslim should proclaim the above-mentioned truth aloud and let whatever consequences follow come. Allah is the Protector. Allah never guides the disbelievers to the right path.

A caller cannot fulfil the right of da'wah, nor establish the proof of Allah upon people, until he makes the full reality of the call clearly known to them, and makes clear to them the position in which they currently stand, and says this without compromise and without equivocation. If the caller does not tell people plainly where they stand, that they are wrong, that they hold a false position, that the position to which he invites them is entirely different from their present stance, and that he calls for a complete transformation, he calls them to a long journey and long struggle; he wants a complete change, and this change extends to their ideas, their customs, their system of life and their moral order. Thus he afflicts them, and therefore people expect a caller to state clearly that their present position is wrong, so that whoever rejects may reject clearly and whoever accepts may accept clearly; let whoever dies die and whoever lives live.

When a caller hesitates and speaks in a muddled way, and does not tell people plainly what falsehood is in their lives, what the truth is to which he calls, and where the dividing line lies between the call to truth and their false position, and does this merely because of difficult circumstances, then he is in effect afflicting the people and deceiving them, because he is not saying clearly what he wants. His second offence is that he is not acting upon the command Allah gave him to state the matter plainly.

In da'wah, gentleness may be shown only in manner: one should adopt a gentle style, complete the message, but with great grace and in a gentle way, complete yet with wisdom and tact, as guided in "wisdom and good admonition."

Today some of our friends observe that the People of the Book live in large numbers in the world and possess great material power. They see that countless idolaters exist in the world and that their words are heard in the nations of the world; and when they see that the states holding material ideologies possess great power, and that these people have destructive weapons, and when these friends see that those who claim to be Muslims have nothing and do not implement the Book of Allah that they possess, such people find it very burdensome. They think: what is the point of telling such a vast number of people that they are all astray, and how can such a vast population be made to understand the true religion?

The truth is that this is not the method. Even if ignorance spreads across the whole universe, it remains ignorance. Whatever the practical circumstances of this world may be, they have no standing unless they are founded upon truth. If a large population stands before a caller in error, his duties are not diminished, nor can the bulk and abundance of falsehood affect the call, just as the call began and addressed all of humanity, declaring that they have no standing. So today too we must begin the work in the same way. After the turning of the ages, the matter has returned to exactly where it was in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ). He (ﷺ) was sent, and Allah addressed him:

(Verse) "Yā ayyuha al-rasul balligh ma unzila ilayka min rabbika" (5:67): "O Messenger, deliver what has been revealed to you from your Lord. If you do not do so, you have not fulfilled his mission; Allah will protect you from the people. Be assured that He will not guide the disbelieving people to the path." Say plainly: "O People of the Book, you are not upon any foundation unless you establish the Torah, the Gospel, and the other scriptures that have been revealed to you from your Lord."

The conclusion of this group of verses is that Allah states which religion is acceptable. As for the identity of people before the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ), whatever it was, and whatever religion they followed or whatever community they adhered to, the command now is this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 5, verse 69:

By "those who believe" (allatheena amanu) is meant the people of faith, the Muslims. By "those who are Jews" (allatheena hadu) is meant the Jews. By "the Sabians" (al-Sabi'un) is meant a group who did not worship idols. These people existed before the advent (ba'th) of the Prophet ﷺ, and they worshipped only One God, but their sect was not a defined or established sect. People of this kind were few and scattered in Arabia. By "the Nasara" is meant the Christians, who claim to follow Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him).

In this verse a decision is given: whatever creed and religion a person was upon earlier, now, if he believes in Allah, believes in the Hereafter and does righteous deeds, and this also implicitly includes that he believes in the Shariah revealed to the final Prophet ﷺ, as has been expressly stated in other places, then such a person will attain salvation, and there shall be no fear or grief for him. It does not matter that previously they were not on the right path. Their former religion and title will not be asked about. What matters is the final outcome.

The reason we say that this point is implicitly understood is that it is part of the necessary and self-evident (bidihiyat) elements of Islamic belief that Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets, and that he has been sent to all of mankind, and that all people, whatever their community, religion, beliefs, race or homeland, are being invited to believe in Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ and to shape their thoughts and their lives according to the guidance of the Noble Messenger ﷺ. Whoever does not accept you as the Messenger ﷺ, and whoever does not believe in you ﷺ, either in summary or in detail, is astray, and his religion and path will not be accepted; he will not deserve this proclamation: "So there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve" (5:69), meaning there shall be no place of fear for them nor of sorrow. This is the fundamental truth that emerges as a necessary consequence of this religion, so a true Muslim has no need to hesitate or waver about it. Especially, a Muslim should not, under the influence of the great jahiliyyah that is spread before him, be heedless while forming relations with the jahiliyyah, which is divided into various communities and sects. It is not appropriate for a Muslim, compelled and influenced, to regard the followers of any of these misguided communities as "people of religion," or to think that their religion is accepted in the sight of Allah and that a relationship of walayah (allegiance) can be established with it.

The walayah and the helper of the believers is Allah alone, and whoever takes as a friend Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and those who have believed, should be certain that the Party of Allah will remain victorious, however unfavourable the apparent circumstances may seem. And whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, and does righteous deeds, and does so in accordance with the principles of this final religion, there shall be no occasion for grief or fear for him: neither in this world shall there be fear for him, nor in the Hereafter shall there be any fear for him. He shall have no fear of the layered and massive powers of jahiliyyah, and they shall have no fear of faith.

Now another chapter of the history of the Children of Israel opens, and in this chapter it is shown why and how these Jews are without substance, and why it is necessary that they be made acquainted with the Islamic call and be invited to this new religion, so that they may enter the refuge of this religion. This chapter is opened so that it becomes known that there has been no change in their reality; they are still what they were. The purpose is that in the eyes of the people of Islam they should no longer have any standing, and that Muslims should not even consider that a relationship of walayah with them can be established, or that they can give any support, as long as they remain in that state and have not changed their attitude towards the truth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 70–71:

(Verse) "Number 70 to 71."

This is their ancient history. The stance they adopted toward the Messenger ﷺ was neither their first nor their last. These people are habitual rebels and turners away, hardened sinners. They are long-practiced violators of their promises. They have always taken their own desires as their deity and their ruler. At no time have they bowed their heads before the religion of Allah or before the Messenger ﷺ. These people have always been haughty and oppressive toward those who call to the truth.

﴿Indeed, We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group of them they denied, and a group of them they killed.﴾ (5:70)

"We took a firm covenant from the Children of Israel and sent many messengers to them. But whenever a messenger came to them with something their desires did not favour, some of them they denied, and some of them they killed."

The ancient history of the Children of Israel is filled with such events: they denied their messengers and turned away from their teachings. They laid hands on several of them and killed several. They always followed their own desires... This is why Allah related the lengthy accounts of the Children of Israel to the Muslim ummah, so that it too might not walk on the path of the Children of Israel. So that the Muslim ummah would know what the difficulties of this path are, and so that those who possess understanding and whose connection with Allah is established might fully grasp these points of slippage, and when they face the same circumstances that the prophets of the Children of Israel faced, they would draw strength from them. And so that the coming generations of the people of Islam, who were also destined to walk this path, and who after the passage of time were destined to display the same hardheartedness that the Children of Israel displayed, would also abandon the path of guidance and take their own desires as their deity, deny the coming callers to truth, and kill some of them, in exactly the same way as the rebels and disobedient ones of the Children of Israel did.

When these rebels of the Children of Israel were committing their acts of rebellion, they were certain that no punishment of Allah would come upon them and that they would not be held accountable. This belief became firm in them because they had forgotten the Sunnah of Allah, and they were caught in the delusion that they were the beloved people of Allah.

﴿And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf.﴾ (5:71)

"And they thought there would be no affliction, so they became blind and deaf."

The sight of their eyes departed, so whatever they looked at, they did not understand; and veils fell over their ears, so whatever they heard, they did not benefit from.

﴿Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness.﴾ (5:71) "Then Allah forgave them again." This was a special mercy of Allah, but they did not value it at all.

﴿Then they became blind and deaf again, many of them.﴾ (5:71) "Then they became blind and deaf again, many of them."

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ (5:71) "Allah observes all their actions." Therefore He will recompense them for all their deeds, and they will not escape.

It is sufficient for the believers here to know about the Children of Israel and to compare it with their own present stance, so that the believers become firm on this matter and cease even to think about alliance (muwalat) with them. Just as Hadrat 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him) declared, out of aversion, the termination of the bond of alliance, while hypocrites such as 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul maintained that bond.

These were the conditions of the Jews. As for the Christians, their daily life and night were also of the same kind. The Qur'an gives a decisive and plain verdict about them as well, and this verdict is entirely appropriate to the theme and purpose of this surah, for the stance the Qur'an intends to give to the people of faith here is best matched by it.

Earlier in this surah, mention was made of those whose belief was that Hadrat 'Isa (peace be upon him) is Allah, and that they are disbelievers. Now this is repeated: those who believe that only 'Isa is God, or who believe that Hadrat 'Isa (peace be upon him) is one of three, are both disbelievers. Their disbelief is supported here by the statement of Hadrat Masih (peace be upon him), who himself taught them: beware, do not take anyone as a deity besides Allah. He taught them that Allah is my Lord and your Lord, and in this matter I and you are equal. At the end, people are warned to abandon these false beliefs about Hadrat Masih (peace be upon him) and to adopt the beliefs that are held by the people of faith.
