(Verses 72–76)

Earlier we have already explained when and through which councils these polytheistic beliefs entered the monotheistic creed taught by Jesus (peace be upon him). Yet Jesus (peace be upon him) held the same belief as the other messengers, who were all callers to pure monotheism, with not the slightest trace of polytheism in it. For after Noah (peace be upon him), the purpose of the sending of all messengers was nothing but the proclamation of Tawhid (the oneness of God) and the refutation of shirk (associating partners with God).

Here we record briefly the creed on which these councils reached unanimous agreement, and the details of the differences that later arose over it have already passed.

In the book "Susanna Sulayman" by Nawfal ibn Ni'matullah ibn Jirjis the Christian, it is stated that the Christian creed on which no church disagrees, and which the Council of Nicaea adopted as the fundamental creed, is this: God is one; the Father is God, who controls all things; the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Creator of whatever is seen or unseen. Then one must believe in one Lord, Jesus, who is the only begotten Son, born of one Father, who was begotten before all ages from light. He too is God, God from God, begotten, begotten and uncreated, of one essence with the Father, through whom all creatures came into being, and because of whom we humans were created; and this Father descended from heaven because of our shortcomings. The Holy Spirit was given his rank. In the time of Pilate he was born of the virgin Mary, came in human form, was crucified in the time of Pilate, suffered, was buried in a grave, and rose from the dead on the third day, as is written in the books. He ascended to heaven and sat at the right hand of the Lord, and soon his coming will be glorious, and he will bring all the living into the religion; his kingdom will have no end. One must also believe in the Holy Spirit and in God who proceeds from the Father, who is present with God, and to whom both prostration is made, and who speaks with the prophets.

Dr. Post, in his book "History of the Church," says that the Divine Being consists of three hypostases, which are equal: God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit. Through the Son, people are related to the Father in that they are created; the Son sacrificed himself, and the Holy Spirit is holy.

Now consider how difficult it is to conceive that three are also one, and how hard it is to conceive of Tawhid and Trinity together. The theological writers among the Christians have proposed that reflection on the rational aspect of this belief be postponed, since reason rejects it the moment it is heard. One of their priests, Butros, writes in his treatise "Principles and Branches": "We have understood it in this way according to the strength of our reason, and in the future we will be able to understand it clearly when God lifts the veil from the secrets of the heavens and the earth. For now, this is sufficient."

God says that all these rational constructions are unbelief, because in all of them Jesus (peace be upon him) has been regarded as God, and to say that he is one of three is also unbelief. Therefore, after God's word there is no other word, and God's command is clear:

"Certainly they have disbelieved who said, 'Indeed, God is the Messiah, son of Mary.' But the Messiah said, 'O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates others with God – God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.'" (5:72)

Jesus (peace be upon him) had likewise warned them plainly, but they did not desist. After the death of the Prophet (ﷺ), they fell into the same error from which he had warned them. Yet the Prophet (ﷺ) had stated clearly that if they abandoned the creed of Tawhid and adopted shirk, they would be deprived of Paradise and would deserve the Fire of Hell. They forgot the saying of Jesus (peace be upon him): "O Children of Israel, worship God alone, who is my Lord and your Lord." In accordance with this saying, he had told them that before God he and they were equal servants, and that God, the Lord of all, has no partner. Here the Qur'an mentions all their unbelieving rational constructions.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 5, verse 73:

﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three," while there is no god except one God.﴾ (5:73)

And by refuting these false beliefs, it makes clear that the creed which all the Messengers brought is this: there is no god except Allah. And if the Christians do not desist from these their rationalisations, and continue to say such blasphemous things about the Divine Being and the Being of the Messiah, then it is not far-fetched that a painful punishment will befall them, and the Day of Resurrection is not far off.

﴿And if they do not desist from what they say, there will surely touch those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment.﴾ (5:73)

"If these people do not desist from these statements, then those among them who have disbelieved will be given a painful punishment." And despite this warning from Allah, the disbelievers did not repent of these rationalisations, although Allah had declared in a decisive manner that they had become disbelievers. Alongside this warning (tarhib), Allah also gives them encouragement (targhib) that Allah is Forgiving, if even now they turn back.

Then will they not turn in repentance to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. (5:74)

And this was said so that the door of repentance would not be closed, and everyone would have the opportunity to return before the time runs out.

Now the question arises: what is the true station of Hazrat Masih (Jesus)? It is explained in a firm, logical manner: who the Masih is, in the hope that his natural disposition (fitrat-e-saleemah) will help them grasp the station of the Masih. And after explaining the reality of the Masih, Allah, in an astonishing manner, says that despite this, these people turn away.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 75:

(Verse) "The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; messengers had passed away before him. His mother was a woman of truth, and they both used to eat food. Look how We make the signs clear to them, then look how they are turned away."

Hazrat Masih (peace be upon him) and his mother, the truthful woman (Siddiqah), eating food was a real matter. Eating is one of the important characteristics of living beings, and this is the greatest proof of the humanity of Hazrat Masih and his mother Siddiqah (may Allah be pleased with her). And according to their metaphysical interpretations, it is a strong proof against their being divine (nasut, the human nature). Eating is certainly a sign of human bodily need and bodily dependence. And how can a being that depends on food to remain alive become a god? Allah is living by Himself, subsisting by Himself, remaining by Himself; He does not need food, and things of the nature of food neither enter into the Being of Allah nor leave it.

Seeing this plain and simple reality, and seeing this clear matter, since no reasonable person can dispute it, their position is therefore regarded with great astonishment: that these people still turn away from this sound logic. "Look how We make the signs clear to them, and then look how they are turned away."

The truth is that for those who wished to clothe Hazrat Masih (peace be upon him) with divinity, the human life of Hazrat Masih (peace be upon him) remained an ever-troubling reality. This matter was also contrary to his teachings, so these people remained always engaged in debate, argument and wrangling. And among the Christians' doctrine of divinity, the divine nature (lahut) and the human nature (nasut) of Hazrat Masih (peace be upon him) remained an unresolved issue.

Now the sound logic of the Qur'an is presented to be considered from another angle, with wonder and disapproval.

(Verse 76) "Say: Do you worship besides Allah that which has no power to harm or benefit you? And Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

Say to them: do you worship, instead of Allah, that which holds no power to harm you or benefit you? Yet it is Allah who is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Here the Qur'an has used the word "ma" (what), whereas for Jesus the word "man" (who) should have been used, so that it would include all the creatures that have been worshipped, among them those possessed of reason. The word "ma" also points to the essential nature of this general category: the essential nature of these objects of worship is creation. Therefore, Jesus (peace be upon him), the Holy Spirit, and Maryam the Truthful (peace be upon her) are all included, because in their essential nature they are all creatures. Thus there is a particular indication in this manner of expression as well. The outcome will be that none of Allah's creatures remains deserving of worship, and no creature is the master of benefit or harm.

"...the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." That is, this is the reason He is able to bring benefit and harm. He hears the calls of His servants; He sees the worship of His servants; He knows the secrets of their hearts. He also knows the impulse behind their calling and worship, and whatever other creation exists apart from Allah neither hears, nor knows, nor has the power to respond.

Now this discussion is concluded with this comprehensive invitation. Allah the Exalted commands the Messenger ﷺ to put this proposal before the People of the Book.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 5, verse 77:

(Verse) "Number 77."

Because of the excess (ghuluw) in the teaching of Hadrat Isa (Alayhis salam), superstitions entered the beliefs of the Nasara (Christians). Afterwards, when the rulers of the Roman Empire entered Christianity, they introduced their idol-worship into Christianity. The delegates of the conferences held to resolve its issues also added these false notions into the religion of Allah, although the religion with which Allah sent Hadrat Masih, and which he (ﷺ) propagated, was completely clear. In the Holy Qur'an it is said: "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, who is my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his abode is Hell, and the wrongdoers will have no helpers."

This call is the final effort to save the Children of Israel, so that they may emerge from the bottomless sea of disputes, deviations and the desires of the self, into which those who passed before them fell, went astray themselves, and led others away from the path of truth.

Let us once again reflect on the part of the above verses that ends here. Three realities come before us from it, and it is necessary to mention them here briefly.

(1) Here the reality is how great a struggle has been undertaken in the Islamic system of life to correct the doctrinal concepts, and all beliefs have been established on the foundation of the pure doctrine of Tawhid. It has been purified of all the admixtures of idol-worship. It did not let even the breath of shirk touch it, as shirk had entered the beliefs of the People of the Book. Islam explained to people the reality of the Divine Being well. Allah was declared unique in His Being and His Attributes, and it was strongly denied that anyone could be a partner of Allah in His Being or His Attributes. From this magnificent arrangement for correcting doctrinal concepts, and from the decisive statement and clarification of the doctrine of Tawhid, it becomes known how great is the importance of correct beliefs in Islam, and how deep an effect correct beliefs have in reforming human life. Furthermore, it also becomes known that Islam has made all deeds dependent upon correct beliefs, and has linked all human relations to beliefs.

(2) The second reality before us is that the Qur'an has explicitly declared the disbelief of those whose belief is that Masih ibn Maryam is Allah, or whose belief is that Masih ibn Maryam is one of three gods. After this explicit declaration, no Muslim has any justification left for considering the People of the Book to be upon the religion, because these people have, by means of these beliefs, themselves become deniers of their own religion.

If Islam does not compel people to abandon the religion they are upon, Islam also does not allow someone who has already left the religion to be told, merely to please him, that he is upon the religion and that his religion is acceptable to Allah. Rather, Islam applies the label of disbelief to the religion of such people, and disbelief can never be the religion of Allah.

(3) The third reality, which follows as a necessary result of the first two, is that no relationship of alliance (muwalat) can be established between the holders of these beliefs, the People of the Book, and the Muslims who accept the doctrine of Tawhid stated by Islam. This is because a Muslim believes that the only religion now is that which was taught by Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ). For this reason, the idea that the followers of all religions should unite to confront disbelief and atheism would be a futile notion. From an Islamic standpoint, this idea would carry no weight. When there is such a decisive separation and distance in beliefs, it is not possible for the two parties to unite on any matter, because in the world everything stands on ideas, and Islam is their advocate. The essential thing is the idea and the belief itself.

At the end, it is explained what the stance of the prophets was regarding the disbelieving Children of Israel: another chapter of their history. It is shown what Hadrat Dawud (Alayhis salam) and Hadrat Isa (Alayhis salam) said about the Children of Israel. And Allah accepted their stance because of the rebellion and disobedience of the Children of Israel. Moreover, because of their collective corruption, and because they maintained complete silence regarding this collective corruption and this call, and then because these people were in friendship and alliance with the disbelievers, Allah cursed them and decreed that they would abide in Hell.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 78–81:

It is seen that the history of the Children of Israel is filled with disbelief, disobedience and accursed deeds. The prophets who were sent to guide them and to save them eventually cursed them, and drove them away from the path of Allah's guidance. Allah also accepted their supplication and their cry, and wrote a curse upon them, and they became accursed until the Day of Resurrection.

Those among the Children of Israel who adopted disbelief are the very people who distorted their Books. These are the same people who did not judge according to the Shari'ah of Allah, as the Qur'an has made clear in this Surah and in other places. These are the same people who broke the covenant that Allah had taken from them: that they would believe in every Messenger, would support him, and would help him.

﴿That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.﴾ (78)

The whole history of the Children of Israel is filled with rebellion and transgression. In their beliefs, their concepts and their conduct, glimpses of rebellion and transgression are visible everywhere, and the Holy Qur'an has given its full details.

Rebellion and transgression were not an individual act among the Children of Israel; rather, the collective traditions of their society were themselves coloured with rebellion and transgression. This became the very nature of the whole society, and the whole society would witness the commission of these evils and remain silent, and would not raise any voice against them.

"They did not forbid one another from the wrongs they committed. Evil indeed was what they used to do." (5:79)

Rebellion and oppression occur in every society, because every society contains mischievous, corrupt and deviant people. The earth can never be free of evil and corruption. Within society there are people whose conduct is unusual, but the collective temperament of society does not tolerate evil and wrongdoing, and does not permit rebellion and oppression to become accepted norms of society. Therefore, it is very difficult for rebellion and oppression to be committed within an awakened society. Likewise, in living societies it is difficult for wrongdoing to be committed, and society collectively reacts against evil; the collective bonds of society are strong, and wrongdoing remains confined to a few individuals. Society pursues them and does not let them settle. In such conditions obscenity and evil do not spread; they shrink, and this happens because of the collective conscience and temperament of society.

By presenting this collective scene of the Children of Israel in this repugnant form and criticising it, the Qur'an advises the Islamic system of community that it should have a strong collective existence, and that within this existence there should be such a capacity for defence that it does not tolerate rebellion and oppression at all, let alone let them become a common practice of society. The Islamic society is advised that it should be firmly established upon truth and be highly sensitive towards falsehood. The custodians of religion should protect the trust of which they are the guardians and trustees, and they should block the path of evil, corruption, rebellion and oppression, and in this matter not fear the blame of any blamer. Whether this evil comes from rulers who hold dominion over the government, or from capitalists who have gained influence by accumulating wealth, or from troublemakers who possess the power to harm others in society, or from the masses who have gone astray, the Islamic system is in any case a divine system, and those who rise against it, whether influential or uninfluential, will all be considered rebels.

Islam lays great emphasis on the performance of this duty. If the collective existence of society does not raise its voice against some evil, Islam holds the entire society guilty. Just as each individual is responsible, likewise the responsibility of rising against evil falls upon the entire society.

Imam Ahmad (rahimahullah) has related this narration from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (radiyallahu anhu): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Children of Israel began to commit sins, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist. Then those scholars also began to sit with these sinful people, eat and drink with them. So Allah united them all together, and cursed them through the tongues of Dawud (alayhis salam) and Isa (alayhis salam), because they rebelled and oppressed." When the Prophet (ﷺ) said this, he had been reclining on a pillow, but he sat up and said: "No, by Allah in whose hand is my soul, you must compel them firmly to the truth."

Abu Dawud has related the narration of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (radiyallahu anhu). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first flaw that entered the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another and say: 'O so-and-so, fear Allah and leave off what you are doing, for it is not permissible.' Then the next day he would meet him, and his wrongdoing would not prevent him from becoming his companion at table, his drinking companion, and his close associate. When they did this, Allah united them all together." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah cursed those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel through the tongue of Dawud and Isa ibn Maryam." (From "cursed" up to "transgressors.")

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By no means! You must enjoin good and forbid evil, you must hold the wrongdoer's hand, and you must make him stand upon the truth, or you must compel him to truth."

Merely enjoining and forbidding does not end the matter; one must insist that the oppressors desist. One must boycott them, and eliminate evil by force. The path of sin, corruption and transgression must be blocked.

Imam Muslim, with his chain of narration, has related the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (radiyallahu anhu). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is not able, then with his tongue; and if he is not able, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith."

Imam Ahmad, with his chain, has related from Adi ibn Umayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah does not punish the common people for the specific sins of the few. But when they see evil among them and are able to protest against it but do not, then Allah punishes both the common people and the specific criminals."

Imam Tirmidhi has related from Abu Sa'id: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best jihad is a word of truth before an oppressive ruler."

Texts of the Qur'an and Sunnah abound in this meaning. An Islamic society should be such that the situation is not one where a person sees evil and says, "What is it to me?" Rather, within an Islamic society there should arise a rising up against evil; he should rise up in support of the limits of the Shari'ah. This very spirit is what the foundation of an Islamic community rests upon, and without it the very concept of a Muslim society would not exist.

This zeal and passion can arise in the heart only when a person develops firm certainty in Allah and becomes conscious of what the demands of that faith are. Then he should gain correct understanding of the Islamic way of life, feel that the Islamic way of life is a complete system, take this ideal seriously, and begin striving for its establishment. An Islamic society is precisely one in which the source of law is the Divine Shari'ah, its upbringing is upon the Islamic methodology, and which gives a Muslim the opportunity to enjoin good and forbid evil. It should not be that his individual effort alone raises waves of reform that vanish into the ocean. Conditions should not be such that a Muslim cannot reform at all, as in today's situation in most lands of the Muslim world, where even individually no one can perform the duty of enjoining good, because the collective system of the Muslim world is founded on the principle that no one may interfere in the affairs of another, and in Muslim societies regards immorality and disobedience to Allah as private matters of individuals. No one can interfere in another's affairs; rather, in Muslim societies oppression, violence, rebellion and transgression are so powerful that people's mouths are completely shut from fear, tongues are locked, and whoever raises his voice against evil is subjected to persecution. Genuine struggle and heavy sacrifices must be offered so that a welfare-oriented and good-loving society is established, and a society founded on welfare and goodness can be established only under the shade of the Islamic system. This righteous society should be established by enjoining good and forbidding evil, before and prior even to other partial reforms and matters of personal goodness.

If the entire society is corrupt, no individual can be called clean, while the rebellion of jahiliyyah prevails and the collective structure of society is founded upon jahiliyyah, in which the Shari'ah law is not enforced. In such conditions, initial work must begin and goodness must be uprooted from its roots, and this is possible in the following way: an Islamic state should be established in some region, and once this authority is established, then the work of enjoining good and forbidding evil will begin from the foundation.

All these matters require firm faith and need the beginning of work with resolve and certainty in changing the system of life. When faith is complete, trust in Allah will be complete, and when trust in Allah is complete, the path, however long, will not be daunting, and a person will hope for his reward from Allah. Then this believer does not wait for a person who wants something in this world as well. Nor does the believer give any regard to a misguided society, and he does not seek help from the people of jahiliyyah.

All the Qur'anic texts and prophetic hadiths that relate to enjoining good and forbidding evil define the duties of a Muslim within an Islamic society. That is the society which has accepted the principle of Allah's supreme sovereignty, in which the Shari'ah of Allah has already been implemented, even if its government is oppressive, and sometimes sins spread. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most excellent jihad is a word of truth before an oppressive ruler." A just imam is still an imam, but as long as this oppressive ruler does not acknowledge Allah's sovereignty, he cannot become an imam at all. As long as he does not establish the Shari'ah, he is not an imam; he is something else, because Allah says: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers" (5:44).

The great evil within jahili societies, from which all other evils arise, is precisely this evil, by which Allah's right of sovereignty is rejected and Allah's Shari'ah law is not enforced. Now, if we are faced with such a society, the believers must first of all eradicate this great evil, because it is a fundamental evil. We should protest against it and not waste time on other partial evils that come into existence because of this great evil. Those are its branches, and their very existence is indebted to this great evil.

There will be no benefit in our expending our strength in struggle against these partial evils. Many righteous and pious people are engaged in struggle against these partial evils, although these evils are the offspring of that greater evil. That evil is that people, by encroaching upon Allah's rights, deprive Him of His right of sovereignty and deny His Shari'ah. Therefore we should not waste our energies in removing these partial evils, which arise as a result of that primary evil, namely the tyrannical supreme authority. There is no doubt or argument that these are its consequences.

Secondly, when in a tyrannical society we enjoin people against evil and say, "This is a bad deed, do not do it," what standard and criterion will we have before us? For instance, a Muslim person says, "This is evil," and ten people from here and there will rise up and say, "Certainly not, this is not a bad deed. Yes, speaking of old times, this was once so, but now the world has changed, society has progressed, and values have changed."

Therefore it is necessary that there be one standard, and that all people judge good and evil according to it. Now, from where shall we derive this standard and these values? Where shall we obtain this balance and criterion? Shall people's estimations, people's customs, and their desires become the standard of good and bad? These things keep changing. In this way we would enter a desert with no guide, and enter a sea without shore.

Therefore, the establishment of a balance of justice is necessary first. This standard and balance must be constant, not changing according to people's desires. And this is the balance of Allah, constant and everlasting.

Now, if a society does not accept Allah's balance at all... when people do not make their decisions according to the Shari'ah... rather, the situation is that the one who calls to the Islamic system is oppressed, is being avenged against, is being mocked and ridiculed... then, in such circumstances, will the struggle for partial reform not be wasted, becoming merely a joke? What benefit is there in your rising in such a society and enjoining good and forbidding evil, and launching struggle by forming associations for the reform of certain details, about whose weighing people's standards and balances differ, who hold differing opinions, where each person is free to live according to his desires?

Therefore it is necessary that, in principle, there be agreement on one judge, agreement on one standard, agreement on one supreme authority and ruler, agreement on the forum which will decide, and that in case of difference of opinion, its decision be accepted and implemented.

It is necessary that first of all the great ma'ruf be established, and the great ma'ruf is that Allah's right of sovereignty be acknowledged and the struggle for the implementation of the Islamic way of life be undertaken. First of all the great nahy 'an al-munkar must be carried out, and the great munkar is that the supreme sovereignty of Allah is being denied, and Allah's Shari'ah is abandoned. Only by establishing this foundation is the building of a righteous society possible. After this, efforts for reform of society can be started from every side. But at this time the need is to gather all efforts, direct them toward one direction, and establish this foundation, that is, an Islamic system of government.

Sometimes a person sees that very good people are engaged in a most great struggle, and they enjoin good and forbid evil, but in secondary evils, while that foundation upon which the Islamic society is built, and upon which enjoining good and forbidding evil stands, remains hidden from their sight.

What is the benefit of preventing people from committing adultery in a society that does not regard adultery as a crime at all? It considers only forcible sexual assault to be a crime, and even for that it does not impose punishment according to the Shariah, because it does not acknowledge the sovereignty of God, nor does it accept the Shariah as a system of life.

What is the benefit of preventing people from reviling Islam in a society where the sovereignty of God is not acknowledged, where the worship of God does not prevail, but rather human beings have been made lords? Where people in parliament enact laws for mankind, establish systems of life and ways of living for them, and set the standards of values and of good and evil for them, and both the one who reviles and the one who is reviled are outside the religion of God.

What would be the benefit of enjoining good and forbidding evil in such circumstances? I say, what is the benefit of restraining even minor sins, let alone these major sins, when no one restrains anyone from the greatest of the major sins, when disbelief is widespread and the Shariah of God and His system of life have been abandoned?

This matter is far worse and far more important than that. The effort and struggle of these righteous people is far greater than that. This is not a stage at which we should expend our strength on secondary matters and partial reforms. I say that even if there were no partial matters and only major matters, and even if they were the limits (hudud) of God, the hudud of God would be established only when we acknowledge the sovereignty and supreme authority of God, and this question is settled that supreme authority belongs to God. No one other than God has the right to sovereignty. Until this acknowledgment becomes a factual reality, until the Shariah is declared the source of law, until the lordship of God and the sovereignty of God become the sources of government and power, all efforts at secondary matters and all individual endeavours will be wasted and will continue to be wasted. It is appropriate that we first begin the struggle against the greatest evil and take the other evils afterwards.

The Messenger of God ﷺ said: whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he has not the strength, then with his tongue; and if he has not the strength, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.

There comes a time for the people of religion when they cannot change an evil with their hand. They cannot even act against an evil with their tongue and pen. After this, only the lowest level of faith remains: disapproving of it in the heart. Nothing can interfere in the world of the heart, so those who live in the world of the heart have always been at the level of the weakest faith, that is, regarding evil as evil in the heart. If they are sincere Muslims, they regard evil as evil in their hearts.

This is not a negative stance that someone adopts against evil, as it may apparently seem. The manner of expression the Messenger ﷺ adopted is a positive manner. For example, the heart's disapproval of evil is itself a positive act on the part of the heart. The heart considers it evil, hates it, and does not lay down its arms before the evil. The mind and heart do not regard such a situation as a lawful or legitimate state of affairs. And when the heart and mind do not accept a situation, this is in reality a positive step towards ending that situation. There is resolve in the heart that whenever an opportunity comes, the evil situation will be replaced by a righteous situation, and such a person sits in waiting for the time when he may attack the evil. All these acts are active and positive acts, although this is a weak level. For a Muslim in a bad time, it is no small thing that he remains at this level. At least he does not lay down his arms before evil, as if evil were a fact that must simply be accepted. And sometimes, when the sense of loss disappears, a person falls even from the station of the weakest faith... And then what happens? The whole society becomes deserving of the curse, like the Children of Israel, and this saying of God applies to them:

"Those among the Children of Israel who adopted disbelief were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus son of Mary, because they had rebelled and had begun to transgress. They had stopped forbidding one another from the evil deeds they committed."

Now, from here onward the discussion continues about the Children of Israel alone, and with this our portion of the Qur'an concludes. Their conduct during the time of the Messenger ﷺ is described. Their way of life has, roughly speaking, been similar in almost every age. These people have always colluded with the disbelievers and idolaters against the People of Islam and the community of Muslims, and the cause of this, despite their being People of the Book, is that they did not believe in God and in the Prophet ﷺ. Since they did not enter this final religion, they are not believers. Had they been believers, they would not have established relations of loyalty (muwalat) with the disbelievers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 80:

(Verse) "You see many of them turning in friendship to those who disbelieve. Evil indeed is what their souls have put forward for them, that Allah has become angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide forever. And if they had believed in Allah, and the Prophet, and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. But many of them are defiantly disobedient." (5:80-81)

"You will find the most intense of the people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, 'We are Christians.' That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant."

This matter applied to the Jews in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the same way that it applies to the Jews of today, and it will apply tomorrow as well. In every age, the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, and those spread across the corners of the earth, will remain as they are. From this we receive the lesson that we should reflect upon the secrets and mysteries of the Holy Quran. The Holy Quran contains wondrous guidance for the Muslim community, and the Islamic movement should at all times derive guidance and policies from the Quran.

The Jews, in that period, maintained a relationship of alliance with the polytheists. They were gathering them against the Muslims, and they used to say that the disbelievers and polytheists were on a more upright path than these Muslims, as the Holy Quran has explicitly stated; and this manifested itself clearly in the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwa al-Ahzab). Before and after that battle, they remained on the same policy, and to this day they remain upon the same stance. The establishment of Israel in Palestine itself came about through the efforts of these modern atheists and disbelievers.

As for the Christians, their condition is that whenever a matter involving the Muslims arises, the Christians stand with the polytheists. They become supporters and helpers of the idol-worshippers. Whenever a battle occurred between the Muslims and the polytheists, the inner hatred of these people against Islam came fully into the open, and it continues to persist to this day, even if the matter concerns those who are called nominal Muslims. How truly Allah the Exalted has spoken: "You see many of them turning in friendship to those who disbelieve" (5:80). "You see many of them turning in friendship to those who disbelieve."

(Verse) "Evil indeed is what their souls have put forward for them, that Allah has become angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide forever" (5:80).

This is the earnings that they have made, and it is the wrath of Allah that is being gathered for them, and the result will be that they will remain in Hell forever, and how wretched is this end. How wretched is the savings that they are accumulating. How bitter is the fruit. This fruit is for the relationship of alliance with the disbelievers!

Are we Muslims not listening to the word of Allah? Should we not refrain from those actions which we are continually performing, and which Allah has not permitted? Yet we Muslims still think about alliance with the People of the Book enemies, or we form a united front. What is the reason for this? The reason is simply that there is no faith in Allah and His Messenger.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 81:

(Verse) "Had they truly believed in Allah, in the Prophet, and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken the disbelievers as allies. But many of them are defiantly disobedient."

Verse 81 of Surah al-Ma'idah: "If they truly believed in Allah and the Prophet and in what was revealed to him, they would never have taken them as allies, but many of them are transgressors."

This is the real reason: they did not believe in Allah and in the final Prophet. Most of them are immersed in wickedness and sin. In their awareness and in their orientation, they are of the same kind as the disbelievers. Therefore they have become friends of the disbelievers and do not make friends with the believers.

Three clear truths emerge from this Qur'anic observation.

The first truth is that all the People of the Book, except those who believed in Muhammad (ﷺ), are not believers, because they did not believe in the final Messenger. The Qur'an did not say that they did not believe in the Prophet, but rather it also [says that they did not] make friendship and affection with [the disbelievers]. This is Allah's decision, and there is no room for interpretation in it, however much the People of the Book may verbally claim faith. And if we reflect on their deviant and corrupt beliefs about God, whose explanation we have just given in this same lesson, then they do not have faith in Allah either.

The second truth is that Islam invites all the People of the Book to enter Islam, and this invitation has been conveyed to them through the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ). If they accept this invitation, they are believers; otherwise they are not.

The third truth that emerges is that a relationship of loyalty (muwalat) and friendship cannot be established between the People of Islam and the People of the Book, and this relationship cannot exist in any matter, because the entire circumstances of life of a Muslim are subject to the religion, and these people are enemies of the religion of Islam.

As for the fact that Islam instructs good social conduct and proper behaviour towards the People of the Book, commands the protection of their lives, property, honour and dignity so long as they are in the Abode of Islam, permits them to remain upon the beliefs they hold, and that they be invited to Islam with wisdom and goodly exhortation, and that debate with them be conducted well, so long as they remain loyal to the Islamic state, and that they must not be commanded under any circumstances to abandon their beliefs, this is the policy Islam has established for all minorities residing in the Abode of Islam. This is Islam: its message is clear and plain. Islam desires goodness, promotes tolerance, and speaks plainly, because this is the word of Allah, and Allah is the guide to the right path.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 5, verse 82 (part 1 of 2):

An Overview of the Last Part of Surah al-Ma'idah:

This section contains the remaining portion of Surah al-Ma'idah. Details about its earlier portions have already been given in Part Six. This Part also contains the portion of Surah al-An'am from its beginning up to the verse (Ayah) "Wa law annana nazzalna ilayhimu al-malaikah" (﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels﴾). A detailed discussion of that portion will come at the beginning of Surah al-An'am. Here, only the portion of Surah al-Ma'idah that was left over is being commented upon.

In Part Six, in the introduction to this Surah, we had said:

"Allah Ta'ala revealed this Qur'an upon the blessed heart of Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) so that through it he would establish a nation (ummah). That nation would lay the foundation of a state, organize a society, and this state would refine the consciences and morals of people and train their intellects. Through this Qur'an, the limits and bounds of the collective relations of that society would be set, the relations of people within that state would be regulated, and then the relations of that state with other countries would also be established. The relations of this ummah with other nations and religious communities would be formed. The Qur'an would bind this entire ummah into a strong rope, gather its scattered parts, unite its sects, and firmly establish it upon a strong axis, bringing it under the sovereignty of Allah and directing it toward one direction. This is the religion of Islam, as it truly is in the sight of Allah, and as the Muslims understood it when they were true Muslims."

As we saw in the previous three long Surahs, this Surah also takes up various subjects. What is the common thread among all these subjects? It is that very purpose for which the message of Islam was felt necessary in this world: namely, the formation of an ummah, the establishment of a state, and the establishment of an ideal Islamic society. The establishment of this society was also intended according to a specific ideology, in the light of a specific outlook on life, and in a completely new manner. The spirit of this society was the belief in Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). Tawhid was affirmed as its first principle, and the essential elements of the belief in Tawhid are that the only Ilah (God) and Hakim (Sovereign) is Allah; He alone sustains this universe; His command prevails; the ways of living can be derived only from Him; He is the Lawgiver; He alone has the right to determine the supreme values of life, and only He can determine the criteria of good and evil.

"This Surah clarifies doctrinal ideas and purifies them from idolatrous superstitions and deviations. It also removes the distortions that the People of the Book made, and presents to the community of believers its own introduction: what its reality is, what its method of working should be, and how to avoid the thorns and snares along its path. It shows where the enemies of this religion lie in ambush and where the slippery places are. Along with this, this Surah also describes the acts of worship and the symbols of Islam through which the soul of a Muslim is purified and his connection with his Lord is established. Besides beliefs and worship, it also sets out the principles of collective relations, legislation for the state, and then the principles of the relations of the Islamic state with other governments. It also mentions the lawful and unlawful within the Islamic society: which foods are forbidden for Muslims, which drinks are forbidden to drink, and which women are forbidden in marriage. It describes which deeds are evil and which modes of conduct are non-Islamic. In short, this Surah is a complete bundle in which all these matters have come together in one place, and this bundle is the totality of the religion. From this viewpoint, Allah wishes to make Muslims understand that religion comprises all these matters."

In light of the nature of this Surah and this general description of its contents and themes, we also study its remaining portion with great care. Accordingly, in this portion too, there are the same discussions and subjects, or discussions similar to them, whose details have already passed in Part Six.

The elements opposing the Muslim ummah: in these discussions, some other camps are introduced, about which hints had remained there. It is most surprising that these are the very camps that always rise up against the Islamic movement or the movements for the revival of Islam. Although the enemies of this movement have different colours, the real malice is one, and it is lodged in their hearts. Among them, however, there is also a very small number of people seeking guidance; for example, some Christian groups who are accepting guidance, and when they heard the heart-stirring call from the Prophet (ﷺ) at that time, their hearts melted, and they responded, thereby making themselves deserving of the reward of the Hereafter and Paradise.

Another of the remaining discussions is this: the right of legislation on the subject of lawful and unlawful belongs exclusively to Allah, and it is strictly forbidden for the people of faith to trespass upon Allah's right of sovereignty and legislation in this matter. The believers should fear Allah, because this matter is one of faith and disbelief, and they have already declared their faith.

Besides this, rules and juristic injunctions concerning oaths, gambling, wine, dice, idols, and hunting during the state of ihram; matters concerning the Ka'bah, the sacred months, the hady (offering), and animals with garlands placed on their necks as a sign of sacrifice; the Shari'ah rulings revealed by Allah and the emphasis on following the instructions given by the Prophet (ﷺ); and the themes of warning against opposing Allah and His Messenger are also presented. It is also admonished that they should fear the punishment and retribution of Allah, and keep constantly in view that Divine Being to whom they must return.

After this, some aspects of the training of the Muslim community are also taken up, the values according to which it must deal with the whole world. For example, it should not be affected by the abundance of corrupt things; it should see that pure and wholesome things are always few. Also, among these values and etiquettes, an important etiquette is described: one should not ask Allah and His Messenger about every matter, and if Allah has left something unspecified, the believers should refrain from asking about it.

In this portion it is also declared that the customs and traditions of ignorance are nullified. Idolatry is prohibited, and the shirk and idolatry that remain in connection with certain kinds of animals and slaughtered beasts must be eliminated. For example: Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, and Ham, etc. And that the authority to determine what is lawful and unlawful belongs to Allah alone. The authority of legislation for the whole of life belongs to Allah, and no legislation can be according to the customs of people or the reforms they propose. This task belongs to Allah alone.

Along with this, the ummah is warned to recognise itself: its individuals should have complete mutual solidarity (takaful), and it should be completely distinct from other people and not be cut off from them. It should discharge its own specific responsibilities and keep itself completely free of responsibility for the responsibilities of other falsehood-followers. And it should entrust its own end and the end of other people completely to Allah, whose judgment will be given before Him on the Day of Resurrection.

In the course of Islamic legislation, the subject concludes with the point that if someone is on a journey and far from his family, and wishes to make a bequest, he should appoint witnesses for it. In this way it appears that this legislation was necessary because Muslims would go out for jihad fi sabilillah and for seeking provision and the bounty of Allah. But even in this legislation, all matters have been linked with the fear of the Hereafter.

The rest of the Surah takes up some other aspects of the beliefs of the Christians among the People of the Book, and for this purpose brings some details of the story of Hazrat Maryam (peace be upon her) and Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him). It also mentions the miracles that appeared through Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him): the food that the disciples (Hawariyyun) asked for, the issues of the divinity of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) and his mother, and that Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) never made such claims. It also gives a glimpse of one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, in which the matter of the people of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) is presented before all humankind, and they are brought before Allah, Lord of the worlds, and in that awesome scene all the nations of the Messengers are present.

The Surah concludes on the position that the true owner of the heavens and the earth is Allah, and that Allah's power is not bound by any restriction.

﴿Wa lillahi mulku as-samawati wal-ardi wa ma fihinna wallahu 'ala kulli shay'in qadir﴾
"To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent."

From this brief survey of the remaining portion of the Surah, it is known that its discussions are progressing according to the same method and the same mode of argument to which we pointed in the quotations cited above. Now we shall discuss the remaining lessons in detail.

Lesson No. 52 — An Overview:

This lesson is part of the lengthy discussion about the Jews, Christians, and polytheists that was going on in Part Six, and whose purpose was to show what the position of these people is regarding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslim ummah. This discussion occupies more than half of this Surah. In this discussion, generally the ideological corruption of both Jews and Christians has been unveiled, and specifically the evil intentions and evil conduct of the Jews have been examined. This conduct of theirs was towards their own earlier prophets, and it continued with the Prophet (ﷺ) as well; during this whole period they remained helpers and supporters of the polytheists rather than of the Muslims. It was also explained there that the beliefs to which the Jews and Christians have arrived are clearly disbelieving beliefs, because they have abandoned the beliefs contained in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. Unless they establish the Torah, the Gospel, and the Word of Allah now revealed, they will have no religious standing. Now the direction of the discourse turns toward the Prophet (ﷺ): whatever is revealed to him he should convey to the Jews, Christians, and polytheists alike, because all of them have abandoned the religion of Allah, and now their duty is to enter Islam, while the duty of the Muslim ummah is to take only Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as friends and allies, and not to establish relations of friendship (muwalat) with the Jews, Christians, and polytheists, because these people are friends of one another. The Jews even maintain friendship with the disbelievers and polytheists, although they have been cursed through Hazrat Dawud (peace be upon him) and Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him). This was the earlier subject; now, with reference to the Prophet (ﷺ), the position adopted by all these groups is described, and the attitude they have adopted towards the Muslim ummah and the end awaiting them in the Hereafter is described.

At the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, the Muslim ummah took the Qur'an in such a way that it kept shaping all its plans, all its activities, and all its positions and attitudes toward people according to it, and the condition was that the Qur'an was its guide, its motivator, its mentor, and its leader. For this reason, it remained victorious in every battle, and its opponents remained defeated, because in every battle it fought directly under the Divine command, since the Prophet (ﷺ) led the ummah according to the Divine instructions from the higher realm.

Are those Divine statements not before us? Does that noble Book in which those instructions are written not exist? It exists. And those who are conducting the call to Islam today, or who will do so tomorrow, should take these instructions and decisions as if they were being revealed right now, and determine their position in the light of these instructions in the face of all people. Their position is being determined in their light against all religions, sects, opinions, ideologies, all ways of life, values, and standards, and this work should be done in the same manner today as well as tomorrow.

﴿Latajidanna ashadda an-nasi 'adawatan lilladhina amanu al-Yahuda wal-ladhina ashrakû﴾
"You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity towards those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with Allah."

From the standpoint of Arabic grammar, the addressee of this verse may be the Prophet (ﷺ) or the believers in general, because this is a reality and meaning that is seen with the eyes by all, and this style of speech has parallels in Arabic usage. Whether the address is to the Prophet or to an ordinary Muslim, the apparent meaning of the verse is quite clear.

However, the point worth considering is that in this statement Allah has mentioned the Jews before the polytheists. This shows that the hostility of the Jews to Islam is greater than that of the polytheists, and historically and factually this is also quite clear, if one reflects.

It is true that, according to the rules of grammar, the conjunction with "wa" does not imply sequence or order, and the conjunct and the conjunct-of-reference are equal in ruling. But the Jews have been mentioned before the polytheists because they were originally People of the Book, and someone might assume that they would perhaps be less hostile to Muslims than the polytheists. Therefore, by this priority, departing from the rules of grammar, the intention is to convey the impression that these people are not less in hostility to Muslims. Although in the rules of grammar this priority does not convey this impression, there is certainly the possibility that the allusion intended is that these people are even more intensely hostile to Islam than the polytheists.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 82 (part 2 of 2):

From the beginning of Islam until today, when we study the history of Islam and reflect on the conduct of the Jews towards Islam, it becomes clear that compared with the polytheists of the world, the Jews have been far ahead in enmity towards Islam.

As soon as the Islamic state was established in Madinah, the Jews stood up against it, and when the Muslim community became one community, they began to plot against it. The Qur'an gave very clear decisions and indications about their plots and treacheries, which are clear proof of the struggle that the Jews waged against Islam, the Messenger of Islam and the Muslim community throughout its long history. The flames of that struggle have not died down at any time in the last fourteen hundred years, and its heat is felt everywhere in the world today.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, he first of all made a treaty of peace with the Jews and a treaty of peaceful co-existence (co-existence). He invited them to Islam, which confirmed the Torah that was in their possession, but the Jews did not keep that covenant. They adopted the same attitude that they had previously adopted towards their Allah's prophets, and because of which Allah, the Exalted, made this comment about them in the Holy Qur'an:

(Verse) "And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient. Is it not that every time they make a covenant, a party of them throws it aside? Rather, most of them do not believe. And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw away the Book of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know." (2:99-101)

"We have sent down to you clear verses that manifest the truth, and none reject them except the defiantly disobedient. Has it not been the case that whenever they made a covenant, a party of them cast it aside? Rather, most of them do not believe sincerely. And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah confirming and supporting the Book that was already with them, a group of the People of the Book cast the Book of Allah behind their backs as if they knew nothing."

On the day when, by the grace and kindness of Allah, the Aws and the Khazraj gathered upon Islam, the Jews became the sincere enemies of the Muslims, because through Islam the influence of the Jews among those tribes was completely eliminated. Because of this difficult and great unity, the leadership of the Muslim community came into being, and its reins of authority were taken in hand by Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ), and the opportunities for Jewish rule were ended throughout the whole region.

The Jews used every means and weapon that their deceitful mentality had at its disposal, and they used all of them against the Muslims. The cunning and guile that they had learned during the Babylonian captivity, the Egyptian slavery and the servile life of the Roman ascendancy, they used all of it against Islam. Although all nations and religions had treated them with narrow-mindedness, Islam, in contrast, showed them the greatest generosity. But they repaid Islam's good treatment with that deceit and trickery which has continued since the dawn of Islam until today, and which is a sign of an extremely base mentality.

They gathered all the forces of the Arabian Peninsula against Islam and the Muslims, and day and night they kept gathering the scattered tribes of Arabia for this campaign.

(Verse) "And they say to those who disbelieved, 'These are better guided on the way than those who believed.'" (4:51)

"They say to those who adopted the path of disbelief that these people are on a better path of guidance than those who believed."

And when Islam prevailed despite the plots of the Jews, they changed the colour of their plots. They adopted the policy of inserting fabricated statements of their own into Islamic literature. Only the Book of Allah remained beyond their reach, because Allah Himself had guaranteed its protection. They placed their agents within the ranks of the Muslims. Among those who had newly entered Islam and whose minds had not yet matured, they began to spread mischief. They continued this work in various regions, and to this day they gather people against the Muslims in every corner of the world. Thus, at this time, the Jews have spread their nets in every nook and corner of the world against Islam and the Muslims. In this war they are using both Christians and idolaters. It is these very people who introduce non-Islamic practices among Muslims and bring to the stage in Muslim countries such leaderships whose names alone are Muslim, and through them they are engaged in uprooting the religion of Islam from its very foundations.

Let us once again reflect on this word of Allah: "You will find the most hostile of people to the believers to be the Jews and the polytheists."

- Who gathered all the tribes against the young Islamic state of Madinah in the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), and gathered the Banu Qurayzah and other Jews, and gathered the Quraysh of Makkah and other tribes? Who was it? The Jews.
- The person who incited the masses, gathered the mischief-makers in Madinah, and spread a vile propaganda, as a result of which Hadrat Uthman was martyred and after which extremely destructive events occurred: who was he? The Jews.
- Those who kept inserting fabrications into the traditions of the Messenger: who were they? The Jews.
- In the era of the last Islamic caliphate, the Ottoman Caliphate, who raised the slogans of nationalism, who brought about revolutions throughout the Muslim world and abolished Islamic law and Islamic constitutions, and who, after abolishing the Ottoman Caliphate following Sultan Abdul Hamid, introduced a secular system? That person was Ataturk, a Jew.
- All the measures that are taken against Islamic movements throughout the Muslim world and the whole world: who stands behind them? The Jews.
- Who is the originator of materialism and atheistic ideologies on this earth? Who stands behind the movements for spreading animal instincts and sexual licentiousness? Who propagates all those ideologies which are against all religious sanctities and symbols? Only and exclusively the Jews.

In short, the account of the struggle that the Jews have waged against Islam throughout Islamic history is very long. Compared with it, what the polytheists and idolaters have done against Islam is very little, both in ancient times and in modern times. Do you not see that the Islamic struggle with the polytheists of Arabia lasted, in total, only twenty years? Likewise there was a short period of war with the Persians. In the modern era, although the polytheists of India appear to be fighting against Islam, their enmity and war are not even a fraction compared with that of the Jews. Global Zionism (let it be remembered that socialism and communism are regarded as branches of global Zionism) has always been at the forefront of enmity towards Islam, and the hostility that the Jews waged against Islam before this, how long and vast it was, compared with it, even the Crusades alone are of such little significance, about which we will speak further on.

If we reflect again and again on these words of Allah, "You will find the most hostile of people to the believers to be 'the Jews and those who associate partners with Allah,'" the truth of the matter becomes clear. In this verse the Jews are given first place over the polytheists, and when we also keep in view the historical role that the Jews played against Islam, some of whose events we have pointed out above, we will know why Allah has placed the Jews first in this phrase.

Truly, the Jews are people of extremely evil nature; there is wickedness in their temperament, and enmity against Islam and the Prophet of Islam is filled in their hearts. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, here warns the Muslims and the Prophet (ﷺ). And if anyone in the world has been able to gain control over this evil and wicked nature of theirs, it was Islam and the Muslims, but only at the time when the Muslims were truly Muslims. It was Islam alone that delivered people from this evil-natured creature, but only at the time when the people of Islam fully discharged the rights of Islam.

(Verse) "You will certainly find the most intense of the people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associated others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, 'We are Christians.' That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflow with tears from what they recognize of the truth. They say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses. And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth, while we aspire that our Lord will admit us [to Paradise] with the righteous people?' So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally, and that is the reward of the doers of good. But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire." (5:82-86)

"Reflect upon these verses. They point to a specific situation, and the judgment in them is also within a specific situation. This is a comment about a group among the followers of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) who said that they were 'Nasara' (Christians), and the comment is in these words, that in affection towards the Muslims these people are nearer. But it should be kept in mind here that this is a comment on a determined situation, so it applies only to that particular situation. Most people have not understood this comment well. Some people are using this comment for the purpose that the people of Islam should soften their stance towards certain opposing camps, although softening one's stance is extremely harmful for the people of Islam. It may also lead to error in understanding the enemy's policy and stance. Therefore we consider it appropriate here to clarify, in Zilal al-Quran, the situation that is depicted in these verses."

The people described in these verses are those who said that they were "Nasara", and who are nearer in friendship to the Muslims, and these people are scholars and ascetic-type poor people, and they are also neither proud nor arrogant.

(Verse) "That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant." (5:82)

"That is because among them are scholars and ascetic poor people, and they do not show arrogance." But the Holy Qur'an does not end the matter here. Nor is the matter left vague, nor is it left general for everyone who says "I am a Christian." Some more colour is added to the picture of this group, and the stance of this group is clarified thus.

This is a living scene, and in it the complete picture of that group is visible. This is the group that, among all others, stands closest in friendship to the believers. It is a group that, when the latest portion of the Quran is revealed, has its emotions stirred. Their hearts soften and they are so affected that their eyes fill with tears. This shows that they take a very deep impression from this Quran. They express this impression only in the language of tears, and this kind of expression is made when a person cannot express his impressions in words. Therefore the impression is expressed through tears, and in this way pressure and suffocation are relieved, because the pressure of emotions is extremely severe and deep.

These people do not stop merely at shedding tears. Having been affected by the truth they have heard in the Quran, they do not take a negative attitude toward it. They do not remain silent in the face of the true consciousness the Quran carries and the intense feeling it produces. They do not merely hear, become affected, and stop after shedding tears; rather they go further, adopt a positive attitude, and accept this truth, this consciousness and this feeling. They believe, they are convinced, and not only this, they also declare their faith and conviction, and they make this declaration with great fervour.

﴿They say: "Our Lord, we believe, so write us down among the witnesses." (83) And why should we not believe in Allah and in the truth that has come to us, when we long that our Lord would admit us among the righteous people?﴾ (84)

They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so record our names among the witnesses." And they say, "Why should we not believe in Allah and accept the truth that has come to us, when we desire that our Lord admit us among the righteous people?"

See, these people declare the truth that reached them, and they recognised it. After this they pray, "O Allah, include us in the list of witnesses, include us in that thread, and include us in that thread which is striving on this earth to establish this truth. Admit us into that community upon which this Quran bears witness that it is the true community, and which, through its tongue, its deeds and its struggle, is discharging the duty of bearing witness to the truth, and wishes to see this truth flowing and pervading the lives of people." Thus these people themselves become included among those who discharge the duty of bearing witness to the truth. They call Allah to witness that they have entered this community, and then they also request that their names be registered.

After doing all this, they themselves put forward, in the form of a rhetorical question of denial, what obstacle could now stand in the way of their acceptance: that they should hear, be convinced, and yet not believe, so that their Lord would accept their prayer, raise them in rank, and record them among the righteous. Why, and why would they not do so? There is no justification for it.

﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and in the truth that has come to us, when we long that our Lord would admit us among the righteous people?﴾ (84)

This is a clear, straightforward and decisive stance, in which they openly accept the truth revealed in the Quran. In short, these people hear, understand, are deeply affected, and declare their faith. They accept Islam, become part of the Muslim community, and yet still pray that He grant them the ability to discharge the duty of bearing witness to the truth, so that they become among those who, through their deeds and through jihad in the way of Allah, strive for the establishment of religion and endeavour to establish it in people's lives. In their view the path becomes so clear that they are convinced this is the way, and that it is not permissible for them to follow any other path. This is the path of faith in Allah and of the truth that Allah has now sent down; the path of hope that Allah will include them among the righteous.

The Quran does not stop even here. These are the people who say that they are Christians and are closest in friendship to the Muslims. Their conduct and manner is that they turn towards the truth stated in the Quran, adopt a most positive attitude, declare their faith, enter the ranks of Islam, discharge the duty of bearing witness to the truth through struggle with their lives and wealth, supplicate before Allah that He record their names in the list of witnesses to the truth, and hope that Allah will include them among the righteous. The Quran does not conclude its description of them merely with these qualities, but further colours are added to complete their picture, and it is also made known what the end of these people will be on the Day of Resurrection.
