This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 105:

Number: 105.

This is a complete separation between the believers and the opposing camp, and among themselves there is mutual guarantee and surety, complete sympathy with one another, and that they are one ummah (nation) and one community.

﴿O you who believe, take care of yourselves; the one who has gone astray cannot harm you when you are guided﴾ (5:105).

"O you who believe, take care of yourselves; the straying of another does not harm you." You are a single unit, distinct and set apart from others. You are mutually bound and mutually responsible, so remain gathered around your center. Keep yourselves pure, purify yourselves, and look after your community and your collective body. If you remain on the path of guidance, the straying of others cannot cause you any loss, because you are a separate collective and distinct from others. You are friends, sympathizers and mutual guarantors of one another. Your bond with other nations is neither friendship nor inner connection.

This single verse makes clear what the principles of connection between this ummah and other nations will be, and what the nature of relations with other peoples will be.

The Muslim ummah is the party of Allah, and all nations other than the ummah are parties of Satan. For this reason, friendship and mutual solidarity cannot be established between the Muslim ummah and other nations, so there is no ideological common ground between the Muslim ummah and other nations. There is no commonality of aims, and in means and ends there is no unity between them. There is no unity in responsibilities or in their rewards.

It is the duty of the Muslim ummah to be mutually supportive and to act as guarantors for one another, and its members should be sympathetic and sincere toward one another. They should keep following the guidance of Allah, because it is Allah who has made them a distinct ummah. If they do so, no power in the world will be able to harm them, even if all the people around them adopt misguidance. But this principle will continue to operate only as long as the ummah remains upon guidance and steadfast.

However, this does not mean that the Muslim ummah should withdraw from the duty of calling to the religion. Its duty is to invite people to the religion and to guidance, because calling people to the path of guidance is indeed our religion. This is our system. When the ummah establishes its system somewhere on this earth, then its duty is to invite all human beings to this religion, and then to strive to guide them. This duty remains upon it in any case: that it guide them onto the path of justice, watch over justice, and protect human beings from proceeding further on the road of misguidance. It should not permit them to enter that jahiliyyah (age of ignorance) from which Allah has delivered them.

The point that the ummah is responsible only for its own self, and that if it is on guidance it will suffer no harm from the straying of others, does not mean that if it neglects enjoining good and forbidding evil, it will face no accountability. It has the duty first to discharge enjoining good and forbidding evil within the ranks of the ummah, and after that to discharge it across the whole earth. The first and most important ma'ruf (good) here is that one submits before Allah and accepts the Shariah of Allah as law. The greatest munkar (evil) is jahiliyyah and encroachment upon Allah's right of sovereignty. The command of jahiliyyah is also the command of taghut (tyrannical powers), and the rule of taghut is precisely that in which the rule of anyone other than Allah prevails, whereas the Muslim ummah is first a guardian over itself and then a guardian over all humanity.

The meaning and purpose of this verse is not what some earlier exegetes understood, nor what some modern people understand, namely that an individual is not obligated to enjoin good and forbid evil provided he himself adopts correct conduct. Nor does its meaning imply that the Muslim ummah is also not obligated to establish the Shariah of Allah on this earth, provided it is itself upon the right path, even though the people around it are astray.

This verse does not declare either an individual believer or the entire ummah exempt from confronting the evil found in the world. Confronting misguidance and disobedience is obligatory, and it is also evident that the greatest misguidance is for someone to encroach upon Allah's right of sovereignty and usurp Allah's right of legislation. This is a munkar from which neither an individual nor the ummah benefits, and as long as this munkar persists, no ummah can attain success.

Abu Dawud and the compilers of the Sunan have narrated that Hazrat Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) once delivered a speech and said: "O people! You recite this verse:

﴿O you who believe, take care of yourselves; the one who has gone astray cannot harm you when you are guided. To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you about what you used to do﴾ (5:105).

You apply this verse to a situation which is not what it means. I have heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that when people see evil and do not try to prevent it, it is possible that Allah will afflict them all with punishment."

The first caliph, Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), removed this misunderstanding at the most opportune moment. This misunderstanding had arisen in the minds of some people in his time. Today we are greatly in need of this advice, because the duty of removing evil has become very difficult today, so weak people like us may very quickly incline toward this meaning of the verse. In this way they would be relieved of the hardship and difficulties of jihad and would not have to bear the difficulties of jihad fi sabilillah.

This meaning can by no means be intended, because this duty can be established only through struggle and jihad. Therefore the religion needs people who call the masses to this religion, who rescue people from slavery to human beings and bring them into the slavery of Allah, and who establish the sovereignty of Allah in the world. They should take back the right of sovereignty of Allah from those who have seized it, establish the Shariah of Allah over people's lives, and mould them upon the Shariah. For this purpose, struggle is necessary, so that the effort to bring goodness and light to misguided individuals may be made. If some force is preventing people from coming onto the path of guidance, it should be confronted with force. The influence of that force which keeps Islam suspended and stands as an obstacle in the way of the establishment of the Islamic system and Islamic Shariah should be eliminated.

After removing this obstacle standing in the way of Islam, the responsibility of the believers ends, and only then will the misguided bear their own punishment when they are presented before Allah: ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you about what you used to do﴾ (5:105). If you yourselves are upon the right path, your return is to Allah, all of you, and then He will tell you what you were doing.

Now the last of the legal rulings mentioned in this surah is stated, and this ruling relates to some collective matters of Islamic society. This ruling concerns the case where someone is making a bequest while on a journey, so that two just and trustworthy witnesses are appointed over him, in circumstances where he is far from his society and family. This testimony is established so that the right may reach the one entitled to it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 106–108:

The rule laid down in these three verses is this: whoever feels that death is near and wishes to write a will for his family must call two just witnesses from among the Muslims. If he is at home and gives them the will, they must hold it before his heirs. And if he is travelling and no Muslim witnesses are available, then it is permissible for him to appoint two non-Muslims as witnesses.

If the Muslims or the heirs of the deceased doubt the testimony of these two concerning the will, believing that what they have testified is not correct, and that they are not properly performing what they were charged with, then these witnesses shall be made to swear, after the prayer or after the worship according to their own religion, that they are not giving this testimony for any worldly gain of their own or of anyone else, even if it concerns a relative, and that they have not concealed any matter, and that if they do so they will surely be sinners. After such an oath, their testimony is considered established and binding.

Now, if after this oath it becomes clear that they committed a sin, gave false testimony, and betrayed the trust, then two persons from among the heirs shall swear that their testimony is truer than the testimony of the first two witnesses, and that in swearing this they are not transgressing. After this proof and oath, the testimony of the first two witnesses is considered null, and the testimony of these other witnesses is enforced.

After this, Allah says that through these arrangements a matter can be examined thoroughly, people will be able to give testimony, and people will also not have the fear that other testimony will be produced against their own.

(Verse) "Dhalika adna an ya'tu bil-shahadati 'ala wajhiha aw yakhafu an turadda aymanun ba'da aymanihim." (5:108)

"By this method there is greater expectation that people will give testimony correctly, or at least they will fear that after their oaths, other oaths may refute them."

At the end, all people are invited to adopt the attitude of God-fearing piety and to realise that Allah is watching. They should fear Him and obey His commands, for Allah does not guide to the right path those who are disobedient, nor does He lead them to goodness.

(Verse) "Wattaqullaha wasma'u; wallahu la yahdi al-qawma al-fasiqin." (5:108)

"Fear Allah and listen. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people."

Regarding the occasion of revelation of these three verses, Imam al-Qurtubi says: "To the extent of my knowledge there is no disagreement that these verses were revealed concerning Tamim al-Dari and Adi ibn Bada'." Bukhari and Daraqutni narrate from Hadrat Ibn Abbas (radiyallahu anhu) that Tamim al-Dari and Adi ibn Bada' used to travel to and from Makkah. A young man of the Banu Sahm tribe set out on a journey with them. He died in a land where there was no Muslim. He made a will to the two of them, and they delivered his estate to the young man's heirs. They kept back a silver cup decorated with gold. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made the two of them swear that they had neither concealed it nor had any knowledge of it. Afterwards this cup was found in Makkah, and those from whom it was found said, "We bought it from Tamim and Adi." Then the heirs of the deceased Sahmi came and swore that this very cup belonged to the Sahmi, and that our testimony is more worthy than their testimony, and that we are not transgressing. After this the cup was given to the Sahmis. These verses were revealed concerning this. (The words are those of Daraqutni.)

It is evident that the society for whose reform these verses were revealed leaves its mark upon these arrangements, and the nature of these measures may likewise reflect it. The particular manner of testimony and the particular method of proof were necessarily influenced by the social conditions of that time, especially the swearing of an oath after the prayer, because after prayer a person's religious consciousness and inner feeling are fresh. The person also fears that he is swearing before a general gathering, and if the matter turns out to be false he will face great disgrace. All these points show that the arrangements contain the reflection of the social conditions of the Arabs, and at that time such measures were needed.

In modern societies there exist modern means of proof and new forms of arrangements for evidence, such as written documents, registration, trusts, and lockers. The question arises: have these arrangements ceased to be workable in today's modern societies?

Sometimes we speak with a specific society in mind and decide that certain arrangements are no longer workable in this modern age, that they are no longer needed, and that they are remnants of societies whose era has passed, because the resources of the modern age have advanced greatly.

Most people fall into this delusion, and it happens because we forget that this religion has come for all of humanity. It has come for every age, and even in this modern age a large number and population of humanity remains in a very primitive and backward condition. They are sunk up to their ears in backwardness. For that large part of humanity there are also arrangements that can function within such backward societies. And as these societies progress, Islam fulfils their developed needs. Within Islamic Shariah there are rules for trust and proof, and Islamic Shariah then leads them further along the path of development. This is a miraculous perfection of the Islamic system of life and the Islamic Shariah, and it is a proof that this Shariah is from Allah, and that Allah, glorified is His majesty, has revealed it for humanity.

Moreover, we also err in understanding that the needs of every developing society are fulfilled within the Islamic system. The Islamic system of life makes arrangements for every society according to its circumstances, which contain both comprehensiveness and ease and facility for people. In this way this religion adopts resources and methods in keeping with the condition of every society, whether in backwardness or in developed circumstances, in the desert or in the forest, because this religion is the religion of all humans. It is the religion of every region and every age, and this too is one of the miracles of this religion.

Our greatest misunderstanding is that we humans think we understand the interests of people better even than the Lord of mankind, and when we face practical situations we feel deep shame. But it is not good for us to think this before we encounter events and occurrences. We should respect the Creator of humans and speak before the Divine court as a servant and a slave. Would that we took heed. Would that we acknowledged our shortcomings.

Lesson No. 54 at a glance:

Although this section is relatively long, its subject too is linked with the theme of doctrinal reform. The aim is to correct the deviations that had arisen in the beliefs of the Christians. These deviations were so far-reaching that because of them the Christians, in their fundamental beliefs, had departed from the principles of the heavenly religion, and had gone out of that doctrine of tawhid which Hadrat Isa (alayhi as-salam) and the messengers before him had taught. They had adopted forms of shirk that had no connection with the religion of Islam.

Accordingly, the purpose of this lesson too is to establish in people's religion the correct meaning of the divinity of Allah and the servanthood of the servants. This reform is carried out in such a way that in a great assembly, in which Hadrat Isa (alayhi as-salam), all the messengers and all humans are present, Hadrat Isa (alayhi as-salam) himself declares that he never taught that people should accept him and his mother and other people as deities, and that he taught none of the doctrines fabricated by the Christians.

The Qur'an vividly depicts this scene, which is one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection that the Qur'an presents in a living and luminous manner. It is a highly effective, moving scene that penetrates to the depths of hearts, whose effect is such that a person's very being trembles. Reflect carefully on the words of the Qur'an, and see how the human being is moved.

(Verse) "Yawma yajma'u Allahu al-Rusula fa-yaqulu madha ujibtum; qalu la 'ilma lana, innaka anta 'allamu al-ghuyub." (5:109)

Allah will gather all the messengers who were sent in different ages, who came one after another, or who were in one period but had separate spheres. Each was working in his own domain. Or each was sent to a particular people and was working among his own people. Their call was one, although their times, places and peoples were separate, until the Seal of the Prophets (ﷺ) came. He gave the complete and final call for all the worlds, which is for every place, every time, every nation and community, and for every race and lineage.

All these messengers, who were sent to various nations and communities and came in different eras, are now being gathered in one place by the One who sent them, and He is asking all of them one and the same question. These people are representatives of humanity in the world, and each was given the mission for one domain, for different periods and places. Now these representatives are all present before the Lord of humankind, and it is a magnificent scene of a great gathering, which appears to move everywhere along with life.

They called their peoples to the path of guidance. Some of them accepted the call, and some turned away. Although the messengers knew that the deniers had rejected them, they were not aware of the reality of those who believed, whether they had accepted it sincerely or not. They could pass judgement only on the outward matter. As for the hidden matter, they have no knowledge of it. Now they stand in the presence of the Divine Majesty, and He is more knowing than all who know, and they fear Allah as much as anyone can fear. Moreover, these messengers hold a very high station in the knowledge of the Creator, and they feel shame before the Creator to stand up and display their knowledge, for He is the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.

They express this lack of knowledge out of mere courtesy and modesty, and because they know that Allah knows everything.

This reform is carried out in such a way that in a great assembly, in which Hadrat Isa (alayhi as-salam), all the messengers and all humans are present, Hadrat Isa (alayhi as-salam) himself declares that he never taught that people should accept him and his mother and other people as deities, and that he taught none of the doctrines fabricated by the Christians.

The Qur'an vividly depicts this scene, which is one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection that the Qur'an presents in a living and luminous manner. It is a highly effective, moving scene that penetrates to the depths of hearts, whose effect is such that a person's very being trembles. Reflect carefully on the words of the Qur'an, and see how the human being is moved.

(Verse) "Yawma yajma'u Allahu al-Rusula fa-yaqulu madha ujibtum; qalu la 'ilma lana, innaka anta 'allamu al-ghuyub." (5:109)

"On the day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, 'What response were you given?' They will say, 'We have no knowledge; You are the Knower of the unseen.'"

Allah will gather all the messengers who were sent in different ages, who came one after another, or who were in one period but had separate spheres. Each was working in his own domain. Or each was sent to a particular people and was working among his own people. Their call was one, although their times, places and peoples were separate, until the Seal of the Prophets (ﷺ) came. He gave the complete and final call for all the worlds, which is for every place, every time, every nation and community, and for every race and lineage.

All these messengers, who were sent to various nations and communities and came in different eras, are now being gathered in one place by the One who sent them, and He is asking all of them one and the same question. These people are representatives of humanity in the world, and each was given the mission for one domain, for different periods and places. Now these representatives are all present before the Lord of humankind, and it is a magnificent scene of a great gathering, which appears to move everywhere along with life.

(Verse) "Yawma yajma'u Allahu al-Rusula fa-yaqulu madha ujibtum." (5:109) "On the day when Allah gathers the messengers and asks, 'What response were you given?'" The question was "madha ujibtum" (what response were you given). These messengers were human beings and mortals. Their knowledge was acquired knowledge, and they knew nothing of hidden things. They called their peoples to the path of guidance. Some of them accepted the call, and some turned away. Although the messengers knew that the deniers had rejected them, they were not aware of the reality of those who believed, whether they had accepted it sincerely or not. They could pass judgement only on the outward matter. As for the hidden matter, they have no knowledge of it. Now they stand in the presence of the Divine Majesty, and He is more knowing than all who know, and they fear Allah as much as anyone can fear. Moreover, these messengers hold a very high station in the knowledge of the Creator, and they feel shame before the Creator to stand up and display their knowledge, for He is the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.

It is a day of great responsibility in a great assembly. It is a summons before the court of the higher world, in the open court before all people, and it is an inquiry whose purpose is also that the questioning be done in public, and that this question and answer take place in the presence of those who in the world denied the messengers, so that it becomes openly clear that these messengers did not come of their own accord, but came from Allah bearing the religion of Allah. It was also intended to show that they had carried out this work responsibly, not merely as a matter of inclination. Now observe, they are answering according to their responsibility, giving an account of their duty, the mission of messengership, and concerning their people who denied them.

As for the messengers, they are declaring that true knowledge belongs to Allah alone. Therefore they do not wish to display the little information they possess before God, the Knower of the unseen. They express this lack of knowledge out of mere courtesy and modesty, and because they know that Allah knows everything.

(Verse) "Qalu la 'ilma lana, innaka anta 'allamu al-ghuyub." (5:109) "They will say, 'We have no knowledge; You are the Knower of the unseen.'"

As for the other messengers, some of whom were believed by some people and some of whom were denied by others, their principled answer to the question is accepted. They said that true knowledge is with Allah, the Knower of the unseen. They entrusted their own affair and that of their people to Allah. In this scene no further question is put to those messengers. The only additional question is put to Hadrat Isa (alayhi as-salam). This further question is asked because, after him, his people fell into severe trial concerning him, complexity arose in the atmosphere about him, and people became victims of illusions and superstitions regarding his person. His people fabricated strange and bizarre doctrines about his person, his attributes, his birth and his upbringing.

Now he is questioned before those who regarded him as a deity, who worshipped him, and who had built around his person and his mother false ideas. He is addressed, saying: see how much favour and honour I bestowed upon you and your mother; that I gave you many miracles so that people might believe in you. Some people denied him severely. Some people, seeing these signs and miracles, fell into severe trial and made him a deity. Yet these signs and miracles were given by Allah, and whatever occurred at his hands was by the support and help of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 109–111:

Verses 109 to 111.

This is a reminder of the favours bestowed upon Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) and his mother: that he was supported through the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus); that in the cradle he was given the ability to speak with people, and thus he declared his mother free of accusations. Because of the unprecedented manner of his birth, countless doubts had arisen in people's minds. Then, when he grew up, he also spoke with them and called them to Allah. In the call to Islam too, Hadrat Jibril continued to support him and to teach him the Book.

When he descended into this world, he had no knowledge, and Allah taught him writing and granted him wisdom in matters of judgement. Allah also gave him knowledge of the Torah, which was present among the Children of Israel, and the knowledge of the Injil which was revealed to him, and which too confirmed the Torah. After this, Allah gave him miracles that break the normal course of things, whose occurrence was impossible without the permission of Allah. Behold: he fashions a bird out of clay, and then, by the permission of Allah, you blow into its mouth and it comes alive. We do not know the reality of these miracles, because to this day we have not been able to learn what the reality of life is, or how this life spreads into living things. Now behold: a person born blind comes, and by the command of Allah he receives sight, whereas to this day physicians have not been able to discover how the congenitally blind person gained sight. But Allah, who created the very system of sight, is capable of granting sight anew to someone. He used to treat illness without any medicine. Medicine is a means, whose effect too occurs by the permission of Allah, but by the command of Allah the means can also be changed, and Allah can bring a reality into existence directly, without any means. By His command Allah can bring the dead back to life; He is the Giver of life. He can also raise them again.

Then Allah reminds Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) that he came to the Children of Israel with clear proofs, evidences and miracles, and yet they denied him, and they propagated that these miracles were manifest sorcery. For they could not deny the occurrence of these miracles, since thousands of people had witnessed them. These people, out of mere obstinacy and arrogance, were not prepared to accept these miracles. Then, when they wished to kill him, Allah saved him. Then Allah reminds that in such difficult circumstances the disciples (Hawariyyun) showed courage; they believed, bore witness, became true Muslims, and made Allah their witness that they are those who submit.

(Verse 111) "And when I inspired the disciples: 'Believe in Me and in My Messenger,' they said: 'We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims.'"

These are the favours that Allah bestowed upon Hadrat Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him), and these were proofs and clear evidences for him, but for the majority of his followers they became a cause of misguidance and error, and because of them they fabricated great falsehoods. And behold: Allah questions Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) about this in the scene of the higher realm, in which the prophets and messengers are present and people from all over the world are also present. All of Hadrat Isa's people are also present. These realities are presented before them so that his people too may hear, and their shame may become even more severe. They will be disgraced before all the worlds.

Now the discussion continues along the same line, with the favours bestowed upon Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) and his mother. Those favours which were bestowed upon his people are also enumerated: they too were shown miracles, they saw everything with their own eyes, and the disciples believed and bore witness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 112–115:

(Verse) "Verses 112 to 115."

From this discussion we learn what the disposition of the people of Jesus (peace be upon him) was, and what kind of disposition the sincere among them had, namely his disciples (al-hawariyyun). There was a very great difference between these disciples and the Companions (Sahabah) of our Messenger ﷺ, may Allah be pleased with them all. In the hearts of these disciples, Allah had cast faith by way of inspiration (ilham). They believed, and they made Jesus (peace be upon him) a witness to their faith. Alongside these facts, now observe that, having witnessed this inspiration and these miracles, they again demand a new miracle, so that their hearts may be at rest and they may know that Jesus (peace be upon him) is truthful, and that after Jesus they will spread this call.

The state of the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ is that after accepting Islam they do not ask him for even a single miracle. As soon as faith entered their hearts and they were at peace, they affirmed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and on that affirmation they made no demand for any proof or argument. They gave their testimony to the truth of the Messenger solely by reading the Qur'an.

This is a great difference between the disciples of Jesus (peace be upon him) and the disciples of Muhammad ﷺ. They stand on one level and these stand on another level. Yet these too are Muslims, and those too are Muslims. These too are chosen by Allah, and those too are chosen, but just as Allah willed, the difference in the level of the two is very great, a very great difference.

"The table of food is mentioned in the Qur'an, but there is no mention of it in the literature of the Christians. It is not mentioned in the Gospels that were written for Jesus (peace be upon him), although they were written much later. In such a long span of time, it cannot be said that events were reported accurately in them. Moreover, from the study of these Gospels it appears that some scholars narrated these traditions, and in them they related events of the life of Jesus (peace be upon him). Therefore these narrations do not contain the words that Allah revealed and named the Injil."

However, these Gospels narrate the story of this table in a different manner. At the end of chapter 15 of the Gospel of Matthew it comes: Jesus called his disciples and said, "I am concerned about all of them, because they have only three days with me, and they have no food. And I cannot send them away fasting, for they will become weary on the way." Their disciples said, "Our number is large, and from where can we get food?" Jesus said to them, "How many loaves do you have?" They said, "Seven loaves and a few small fish." He told everyone to sit down on the ground. He took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and broke them. They gave these loaves to the disciples, and they served everyone, and all were satisfied; and when they picked up the loaves, seven baskets were full, and those who ate were four thousand, not counting women and children. Similar narrations appear in the other Gospels as well.

Some of the Tabi'un hold the view that this table (ma'idah) was not sent down. Mujahid and Hasan adopted this view, because when the disciples heard, "I am going to send it down, but whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment such as I have not inflicted upon anyone in all the worlds," they became afraid and withdrew their demand.

Ibn Kathir says: Layth, through Ibn Sulaym, narrated from Mujahid that this was an example which Allah gave here, and that in fact no food was sent down. Ibn Jarir narrated, through al-Harith, Qasim, Hajjaj, and Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, that it was a table with food upon it. They withdrew this demand when they were told that a punishment would come upon them if they showed ingratitude after the food arrived. Through Abu al-Layth, Muhammad ibn Ja'far, Shu'bah, and Mansur ibn Zadhan, he narrated from Hasan that the table was not sent down. Through Bishr, Yazid, and Sa'id, Qatadah narrated that Hasan used to say that when they were told that if they showed ingratitude after it they would be given such a punishment as was not given to anyone among the worlds, they said out of fear that they had no need of such a table. Thereupon the table was not sent down.

However, the majority of the righteous predecessors hold that this food was indeed sent down, because Allah used the words (verse) "Inni munazziluha 'alaykum" (5:115), "I am sending it down upon you," which is a kind of promise from Allah. We consider that the words of the Qur'an itself support this view, and we believe this is correct. On a great assembly in the place of gathering, Allah reminds Jesus (peace be upon him) before his people, saying: I bestowed upon you these and these blessings.

(Verse) "Idh qala al-hawariyyuna ya 'Isa ibna Maryam hal yastati'u rabbuka an yunazzila 'alaynā ma'idatan mina al-sama'" (5:112). This event is also to be remembered: when the disciples said, "O Jesus son of Mary, can your Lord send down upon us a table of food from heaven?" The disciples were the students of Jesus (peace be upon him); they were poor people and knew most about him. They knew that he was a human being. They knew that he was the son of Mary, and they said only what they knew about him. They knew that Jesus was not a lord, but a servant nurtured by his Lord. That he was not the son of God, but the son of Mary and a servant of Allah. They knew that the Lord is the One who was bringing about these miracles through the hand of Jesus (peace be upon him). They could not themselves produce any of these miracles. They did not make the demand of Jesus (peace be upon him) by their own power, because they did not possess power in themselves; rather, they framed the demand in these words.

(Verse) "Ya 'Isa ibna Maryam hal yastati'u rabbuka an yunazzila 'alaynā ma'idatan mina al-sama'" (5:112). "O Jesus son of Mary, can your Lord send down upon us a table of food from heaven?" Now various interpretations come forward regarding the phrase "hal yastati'u" (can...?). The question was: after faith and the testimony of the creed, can they ask this, when they themselves made Jesus (peace be upon him) a witness to their Islam? The meaning of "yastati'u" has also been given as "hal yaqdiru" (is He able?). But the purpose is the result that may come from this power and capacity, namely a table from heaven. Some have also said that they were asking Jesus whether, if he asked, Allah would fulfil their request. According to one reading, "hal tastati'u rabbaka" means: do you have the authority to ask for the descent of the table? In any case, whatever the meaning, in reply Jesus (peace be upon him) warned them not to ask such questions and to fear God.

(Verse) "Qala ittaqu Allaha in kuntum mu'minin" (5:112). Jesus (peace be upon him) said: "Fear Allah, if you are believers." But the disciples repeated their demand, and they also explained the purpose and aim of their request:

(Verse) "Qalu nuridu an na'kula minha wa-tatma'innu qulubuna wa-na'lama an qad sadaqtana wa-nakuna 'alayha mina al-shahidin" (5:113). They said, "We only wish to eat from it, so that our hearts may be at rest, and we may know that you have spoken truly to us, and that we may be witnesses to it."

They wanted, in any case, to eat this table, on which there was no sign on earth, so that their hearts would be at rest, that they would see this miracle happen before their eyes, and be certain that Jesus (peace be upon him) had told them the truth. Then they themselves would become witnesses for their remaining people that this great miracle had occurred. All these matters establish that the position and standard of the disciples of Jesus (peace be upon him) was somewhat lower than that of the disciples of Muhammad ﷺ. If the two models are compared, the status of the Companions of Muhammad appears very distinguished.

Now Jesus (peace be upon him) turns in supplication before his Lord:

(Verse) "Qala 'Isa ibnu Maryama Allahumma Rabbana anzil 'alayna ma'idatan mina al-sama'i takunu lana 'idan li-awwalina wa-akhirina wa-ayatan minka, warzuqna wa-anta khayru al-raziqin" (5:114).

Upon this, Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him) prayed: "O Allah, our Lord, send down upon us a table from heaven, which shall be a day of festivity for us, for our first and our last, and a sign from You; and provide us with sustenance, and You are the best of providers."

As is repeatedly emphasised in the context, the supplication of Jesus (peace be upon him) is extremely respectful. It appears as though a devoted servant speaks in a most intimate manner with his Lord and his Master. Jesus (peace be upon him) begins his prayer with the words "O Allah" and "O our Lord." He submits: O Allah, I request that a table be sent down upon us from heaven, and that it be such that it becomes a cause of joy and delight for us, and a source of happiness for our first and last. Moreover, it should come from Your special provision, and You are the true Provider among those who give sustenance. Jesus (peace be upon him) knows that he is a servant and that Allah is the Lord of the worlds, and he makes this acknowledgement in an open assembly and court. This open court is on the Day of Resurrection and is before the people of his community.

Allah accepted the supplication of Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him). But He gave this acceptance a note of seriousness befitting the station of Jesus (peace be upon him). He asked for a miracle; Allah granted it, but imposed a condition: that if anyone showed ingratitude after this, he would face a severe punishment, of a kind for which there is no parallel, and such a punishment as had never come upon any people.

(Verse) "Qala Allahu inni munazziluha 'alaykum; faman yakfur ba'du minkum fa-inni u'adhdhibuhu 'adhaban la u'adhdhibuhu ahadan mina al-'alamin" (5:115).

"Allah replied: I am sending it down upon you. But whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment such as I have not given to anyone." This seriousness befits the majesty of Allah, so that the demand for miracles does not become a mockery, and so that those who are presented with clear and manifest proofs and still disbelieve should also have the fear of facing the punishment of Allah.

Before Jesus (peace be upon him), it has been the practice of Allah that when peoples asked for miracles and then did not accept the truth, Allah surely destroyed them. As for the verse under discussion, it may be that what is meant is the punishment of this world, and if it is not in this world, then it is the punishment of the Hereafter.

Now, after this warning and admonition, the context falls silent as to whether this table was actually sent down or not, and the discourse returns to its principal theme, namely the matter of divinity (uluhiyyah) and lordship (rububiyyah), since the main subject of this lesson is precisely that. This great court is still in session, and people are watching its spectacle. It is fitting that we return to it briefly and enjoy the direct question and answer. Now Allah asks, in this court, about the divinity of Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother Mary; and those followers of Jesus who regarded him and his mother as gods are also present, so that they may hear, and that he may, in their presence, declare his disavowal of their false beliefs. This response creates an extremely frightening atmosphere. Observe:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verses 112–115:

(Verse) "Verses 112 to 115."

When could a Messenger make such a claim, and that too one of the Messengers of firm resolve, a Messenger like Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him)? Allah had granted him miracles and high stations before his mission and after it, and had bestowed great favours and honours upon him. How could such Messengers make such a claim? A righteous Messenger walking on the straight path.

For this reason, his answer comes in utmost humility and submission, beginning with extreme praise: ﴿Glory be to You! It was not for me to say what I had no right to say.﴾ (5:116) Thus he quickly replies that he never said any such thing at all.

Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) calls Allah as witness to his innocence, and while displaying his own humility, he mentions the attributes of divinity that belong to Allah alone and the acts that befit a servant of Allah.

﴿If I had said it, You would surely have known it. You know what is in my self, though I do not know what is in Your Self. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ (5:116)

After glorifying Allah and declaring Him free of all imperfection, Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) now dares to make a positive statement: he clearly denies having said any such thing, and states what he did say, that he is a servant of Allah and that they too should worship Allah alone.

﴿I said to them nothing except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ (5:117)

He says that he was a watcher over them only for as long as he was among them; after his death he was not their watcher. The apparent verses of the Qur'an indicate that Allah caused Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) to die and then raised him to Himself, whereas some reports state that he is alive with Allah. In my view there is no contradiction between these two kinds of texts. It is equally possible that his connection with earthly life was severed and he was raised up, and that he was raised up while still alive, since martyrs too are alive with their Lord, even though their life in this world is cut off. We do not have detailed knowledge of the nature of the life of martyrs. The same is the case with Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him), who says that after my death I did not know what they had been doing.

﴿I was a witness over them as long as I was among them. But when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things.﴾ (5:117)

Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) entrusts their case to Allah: if You wish, punish them, and if You forgive them, You are indeed All-Mighty. In any case, they are Your servants, and You alone know whether their destiny is punishment or forgiveness.

﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are indeed the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.﴾ (5:118)

Consider how fearful these righteous and near servants of Allah are in the presence of Divinity, and observe the audacity of those people who fabricated this falsehood, from which Hazrat Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) clearly declares his innocence, and because of whose fabrication this servant speaks before Allah in such humble supplication.

Look at the position of those people, and look at that great court. In that court, because of their false position, they appear so degraded and contemptible that during the whole of that dialogue no word is addressed to them, and no regard is shown to them. Perhaps in that scene they were drenched in sweat from shame and remorse. Just as Allah has ignored them, so too we leave them in that state, and let us now look at the final scene of that court.

(Verse) "On this day the truthful shall benefit from their truthfulness." This is the word of Allah, and it is a decisive comment on the shame of the liars. They fabricated this falsehood, and they fabricated it against one of the honoured messengers, among the messengers of firm resolve (ulul-azm). And they fabricated it concerning the matter of divinity and worship, a matter upon which this entire universe is founded, upon which truth in the world is founded, and upon which all creation stands.

"On this day the truthful shall benefit from their truthfulness." At the close of this great scene and royal court of question and answer, this is the decision of the Lord of the worlds. In the presence of all the people of the worlds, these are the final words of this dialogue, and how decisive these words are. After this, a glimpse of the end of the truthful is again shown.

(Verse) "For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the great triumph." (119)

"For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. That is the great success."

After ranks, higher ranks; then eternal life in them; and then Allah's good pleasure. Indeed, this is the great success.

We have seen this scene, and the Qur'an has presented this scene in its own distinctive style and manner. We have also heard the final dialogue of this scene: it is as though we saw it with our own eyes and heard it with our own ears. According to the Qur'an's manner of depicting, speech is not conducted by saying "it will be so," but rather the scene is presented in actuality. A person does not have to wait for this promised scene. The Qur'an does not present mere dry text to be only read, but presents living, embodied, personal scenes in which people are seen moving and walking, and dialogues are seen taking place as on a screen.

According to our thinking and imagination, this will be a scene that will occur; however, according to Allah's knowledge, it has already occurred, because Allah's knowledge is free from the bounds and limits of time and place. The concept of time and place is for the limited knowledge of humans. Our knowledge is limited and transient.

At the end of this lesson, and at the conclusion of the statement of this great fabrication, the greatest fabrication that no follower of any messenger has ever attributed, and at the end of the statement of the great misunderstanding of the followers of Hazrat Masih, in which they disassociated themselves from this fabrication and entrusted the matter of those who fabricate to Allah, at the conclusion of this question and answer and this great court established for that question and answer, it is now declared that Allah, the Exalted, is free from such fabrications, and that sovereignty over the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone, and His sovereignty is without bounds and without limits.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 5, verse 120:

(Verse) "120.

This is a concluding remark, suited to bringing the discussion of this great matter to a close. It is also in harmony with the impression conveyed by this grand scene. Here, Allah is the one God, and He alone is the Absolute Power. Before Him all the Messengers bow in submission, and all the Messengers entrust their final judgment to Allah. Among them, Hazrat Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) also entrusts his judgment to Allah, the One in whose hand is the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth.

And this final remark points to the subject matter of the whole surah. The central theme of this surah is "al-Din" (the religion), and the manifestation of religion and religiosity lies in obedience to Allah's Shariah. It means taking laws and regulations only from Allah and making decisions only in accordance with them, because He is the King, and there is no king but Him. Whatever exists between the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, and this Owner and King issues this decree: (Verse) "Wa man lam yahkum bima anzal Allah fa-ulaika humul kafirun" ("And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then they are the disbelievers"). This is the one issue, and it is the issue of Allah's sovereignty (hakimiyyah). It is the issue of the belief in Tawhid. It is the issue of judging according to Allah's law, after which complete Tawhid comes into being and Allah alone is established as the Deity and the Sovereign."
